title: Chart Settings
summary: The general Chart Settings provides options to customize the appearance and presentation of a Line Analysis chart.
markdown:
## Chart Settings

***

###

### ![Line analysis settings chart](/img/help/lineanalysissettings-chart.png)

###

### Overview

The general Chart Settings provides options to customize the appearance and presentation of a Line Analysis chart. These settings allow you to control the title and background elements.

Any changes are applied directly to the Line Analysis as they are made.

#### Accessing the Line Analysis Settings

You can access the Line Analysis Settings through the chart interface:

1. Open the Line Analysis you wish to customize
2. Double left-click on the Chart
3. Select Chart Settings from the treeview in the Line Analysis Settings dialog

### Available Settings Categories

The general Chart Settings are organized into two main sections:

#### Title

Control how the chart title appears on your graph:

- Title: Add or modify the text of the main title of the Line Analysis

* Font: Customize font (size, style, colour) with the options available by clicking Select. A preview of the current font is shown with the "Preview" label.

#### Background

Configure the visual backdrop of your Line Analysis:

- Plot Background: Set the appearance of the Line Analysis area
  - Background colour
  - Border style and colour

* Graph Background: Control the background of the graph component
  - Background colour
  - Border style and colour

+ Page Background: Set the appearance of the plotting area
  - Background colour
  - Border style and colour

- Page Border Side Options: Enable/disable the individual sides of the page border

title: RFT Plots
summary: An RFT Plot displays Repeat Formation Test (RFT) data as a property-versus-depth chart for a single well, timestep and branch, shown alongside a data grid of the plotted values.
markdown:
## RFT Plots

***

### Overview

An RFT Plot displays Repeat Formation Test (RFT) data as a property-versus-depth chart for a single well, timestep and branch, shown alongside a data grid of the plotted values. RFT Plots are used to review measured reservoir pressure and saturation profiles against depth.

If a case has no RFT file of its own, an equivalent data set is derived automatically from the loaded Grid, Init and Solution data, so an RFT Plot can be created even when no dedicated RFT file has been loaded.

### Creating an RFT Plot

Unlike other chart types, RFT Plots are not created from a right-click menu. Instead they can be created by:

- Double left-clicking an RFT property in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view).
- Drag and dropping an RFT property from the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) onto the [Display Area](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/display-area).

Both actions open a new RFT Plot pane in the [Display Area](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/display-area), pre-selecting the case, timestep, well, branch and property that was double-clicked or dragged.

#### Selecting the Data

Each RFT Plot includes a Selection Panel to the left of the chart, offering:

- Case: Select from the loaded cases containing RFT data.
- Type: Select between RFT and PLT properties.
- Timestep: Select the timestep the measurement was recorded at.
- Well: Select the well the RFT data belongs to.
- Branch: Select the lateral or perforated interval of the well, for wells with multiple branches.
- Property: Select the property plotted against depth, e.g. PRESSURE, SOIL or SGAS.

Selecting new values from these lists updates the chart and data grid without needing to open a new pane.

#### Depth Lines

The Depth Lines checkbox toggles horizontal reference lines at each measured depth data point. Hovering over a Depth Line shows a tooltip with the depth and value at that point.

### Example

![RFT plot example](/img/help/rftplotexample.png)

This example shows an RFT Plot of PRESSURE against Depth for a well B1, with Depth Lines enabled. The corresponding Depth and Pressure values are listed in the data grid to the left of the chart.

### Modifying RFT Plots

The appearance of an RFT Plot can not be changed.

### Exporting RFT Plots

RFT Plots can be exported with the [Report](/docs/reference/exporting-reports) Feature.

### Scripts and RFT Plots

RFT Plots are supported by [Python Scripting](/docs/reference/python-scripting).

title: Resampling
summary: When Summary data is loaded it is presented with its own time vector.
markdown:
## Resampling

***

###

### Overview

When Summary data is loaded it is presented with its own time vector. This is based on the timesteps of the simulation.

Summary data in a Project can be resampled to match another set of timesteps. This can aid comparisons between two different cases. A case may either be resampled to a fixed time basis (e.g. every month, every 4 weeks, etc.) or to match another case, if two or more cases have been loaded.

Resampling is live, in that it will apply to all open views of the data. This means that charts and tables will update automatically when the resampling settings change.

#### Accessing Resampling

To access the Resampling Settings for a data set, click on the ![Create restart](/img/help/create-restart-16-n-p.png) button attached to the chosen Project folder in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view):

![Project view crop](/img/help/projectviewcrop.png)

This will show the Resample Settings dialog from which the resampling can be set for the Summary data in the chosen Project:

![Resample settings](/img/help/resamplesettings.png)

### Resampling a Data Set

From the settings a resample mode is chosen and any options set.

#### Available Modes

There are a number of available modes for setting the timesteps of the case. The available modes are:

- None: The data set will use the time intervals that it was loaded with.
- Case: Resample the data to align with a selected case (only available if 2 or more cases are loaded).
- Fixed: Resample to a fixed set of time intervals or timesteps.

A project can be switched between these modes at will.

#### Case Resampling

For Case mode any of the cases within the Project are available to use as a resampling target. Select a case from the Selected Case drop-down menu to set the time steps for the chosen Project.

![Resample settings case](/img/help/resamplesettingscase.png)

#### Fixed Resampling

In Fixed Resampling mode, you can select the resampling start date, the period and the period type. Available period types are:

- Day
- Week
- Month
- Quarter
- Year

The start and end date of the chosen data is listed for reference. The start date of the resampling can be selected from the Resample Start Date date picker. The period and interval between the chosen period can then be set.

The project will be resampled to have timesteps at every fixed interval from the chosen start date until the data end date.

![Resample settings fixed](/img/help/resamplesettingsfixed.png)

### Resampling Method

Different techniques are used to resample data depending on the data type:

##### Cumulative Data (Production Totals etc)

Linear interpolation is used.

##### Rate Data

Rates are accumulated into cumulative values, which are then interpolated.

##### Pressure Data

A weighted average is used. This will include all the original points within a resampled time range.

##### Anything Else

Linear interpolation is used.

title: Thresholds
summary: Thresholds let you filter and highlight cells in a Grid Display based on the value of a chosen property, showing only the cells that meet criteria you define.
markdown:
## Thresholds

***

### Overview

Thresholds let you filter and highlight cells in a Grid Display based on the value of a chosen property, showing only the cells that meet criteria you define.

An example of a Threshold based on a FIPNUM value of 1.

![Threshold example](/img/help/thresholdexample.png)

#### Accessing the Grid Thresholds

You can access the [Grid Threshold Settings](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-settings/threshold-settings) through the grid display interface:

1. Open the Grid you wish to customize
2. Double left-click on the Grid
3. The Grid Editors dialog will be displayed
4. Select Threshold Settings from the Treeview.

### What Grid Thresholds Do

A threshold is made up of one or more items, each assigned to a chosen property with a value range set on a slider. Any item can be inverted, so it keeps everything outside its range instead of within it, and multiple items are combined using AND, OR or XOR logic to build up more specific criteria. Cells that don't satisfy the combined condition are hidden from the grid, and the effect is applied instantly as you adjust the settings.

A threshold setup can be saved as a named [Region](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/regions) so it can be reapplied to other grids, or reused elsewhere in the application, without rebuilding it from scratch.

### Why Use Grid Thresholds

- Highlight or isolate cells that meet a specific criterion, such as saturation above a given value or pressure below an abandonment limit.
- Build up more specific criteria by combining several thresholds with AND, OR, or XOR, for example to spot cells with both high oil saturation and high permeability.
- Save a threshold setup as a named Region so it can be reused on other grids, or in tools such as Histograms and Grid Scatter Plots.
- See the effect of a threshold change on the grid instantly, which makes it easy to explore cut-off values interactively.

### How to Use Thresholds

Thresholds can be defined in a [Grid Display](/docs/reference/grid-displays) and then exported for reuse and filtering data in other [Charts](/docs/reference/chart-displays):

1. Open the [Threshold Settings](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-settings/threshold-settings) for the grid, as described above, and check On to enable the display of Thresholds.
2. Using the blank Threshold item already added to the list, choose the property it should be based on, e.g. FIPNUM, Pressure, or Saturation.
3. Set the value range for that item using the slider, or by typing values directly into the numeric fields. The [Grid Display](/docs/reference/grid-displays) updates instantly to show only the cells within the range.
4. If you want to keep everything outside the chosen range instead, select ![Invert colours](/img/help/invert-colours-16-n-p.png) Invert Item on that item.
5. Repeat to add further items for other properties or ranges. Use each item's Operator Selection to combine it with the previous item using AND, OR or XOR, building up a more specific combined condition.
6. Use ![Refresh reload](/img/help/refresh-reload-16-n-p.png) Reset or ![Red cross](/img/help/red-cross-16-n-p.png) Remove on an item, or ![Invert colours](/img/help/invert-colours-16-n-p.png) Invert All, ![Refresh reload](/img/help/refresh-reload-16-n-p.png) Reset All or ![Red cross](/img/help/red-cross-16-n-p.png) Remove All, to adjust or clear the Threshold as you refine it.
7. Once the Threshold gives the result you want enter a name in the Region box and click ![Save icon](/img/help/save-icon.png) Save. It will now be stored as a named [Region](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-features/regions) so it can be re-applied to other grids or used in tools such as [Histograms](/docs/reference/chart-displays/histograms) and [Grid Scatter Plots](/docs/reference/chart-displays/grid-scatter-plot). See [Threshold Regions](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-settings/threshold-regions) for details.

Saved Thresholds can be found under the [Regions node](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements#CalculatedData) of the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view).

For a worked example showing how selecting, inverting and combining items with AND, OR and XOR affects the grid, see the Threshold Region Example.

title: Multi-Plot
summary: A Multi-Plot chart allows users to combine multiple charts into a single, unified display.
markdown:
## Multi-Plots

***

### Overview

A Multi-Plot chart allows users to combine multiple charts into a single, unified display. This is particularly useful for comparing trends across different cases, wells, or properties in a compact and organized layout. Each pane within the Multi-Plot can host its own chart, and the layout can be customized to suit the user's analytical needs.

### Creating a Multi-Plot

Multi-Plot charts can be created from the Multi-Plot button on the [Home Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/home-tab).

Clicking on this button offers an initial arrangement of panes on the chart window from a drop down menu. The options are: 1x2, 2x1, 2x2, 2x4 or a 3x3 array of panes. This arrangement of panes can be modified from the [Multi-Plot Design Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs/multi-plot-tools/design-tab).

#### Setting Panes

Each pane can house one chart. To create a chart on a pane drag and drop a property from the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) to the chosen Multi-Plot pane.

Time-series data, such as Summary data, will create a [Line Plot](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots) chart.

Map data, such as Solution data, will offer a dialog prompt to select which type of chart to create. The options are:

- Cell Line Analysis: Creates a [Line Analysis](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-analysis) chart.
- Grid Display: Creates a [Grid Display](/docs/reference/grid-displays).
- Histogram: Creates a [Histogram](/docs/reference/chart-displays/histograms) chart.
- Scatter Plot: Creates a [Grid Scatter Plot](/docs/reference/chart-displays/grid-scatter-plot).

Each chart can then be customised, such as titles, axes and colours according to their type.

The pane are treated as separate charts and any data or settings changes are not shared. There is an exception when [Broadcasting](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/window-view/broadcasting) is applied to the Multi-Plot. In this case, all the charts within the Multi-Plot are affected by the updates from Broadcasting.

### Example

![Multi plot example](/img/help/multiplotexample.png)

This Multi-Plot chart shows a Line Plot of the Oil Production Rate for multiple wells in the top pane and Line Plots of the Field Oil Production Total and Water Cut in the bottom panes.

### Modifying Multi-Plots

Multi-Plots have a settings to define the arrangement of the panes in the [Multi-Plot Design Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs/multi-plot-tools/design-tab).

Chart within the Multi-Plot can be modified in the same way that individual chart are modified. This includes adding more data series to am existing chart and accessing the chart settings and [Contextual Ribbon Tabs](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs).

Each chart has access to the settings for the specific chart type. Double-clicking on a chart in a pane will present the settings dialog for that chart type.

### Exporting Multi-Plots

Multi-Plots can be exported using the [Report](/docs/reference/exporting-reports) Feature, just like other chart types. This allows users to include comparative visualizations in presentations or documentation.

### Scripts and Multi-Plots

Multi-Plots are supported by [Python Scripting](/docs/reference/python-scripting).

title: Mismatches Analysis
summary: Mismatch Analysis compares simulated results against the observed (historical) data loaded with a case, the classic history-matching check of how well a simulation reproduces measured field and wel...
markdown:
## Mismatch Analysis

***

###

### Overview

Mismatch Analysis compares simulated results against the observed (historical) data loaded with a case, the classic history-matching check of how well a simulation reproduces measured field and well performance. The analysis is presented as an interactive dashboard listing the cases ranked by their fit to the historical data and charts showing the comparison between simulated and observed properties.

For every historical vector in the data set (production/injection rates and cumulatives, pressures, etc.) S3analyse automatically identifies the matching simulated vector and calculates the error between them at every history-matched timestep.

The tool is most useful when working with an ensemble of cases (history-matching iterations or different realizations): it ranks every case by an overall Objective Function, lets you drill into which wells or measurements are driving a poor match, and overlays observed and simulated data on a chart so the shape of the mismatch, not just its magnitude, is visible.

#### Accessing Mismatch Analysis

Mismatch Analysis is accessed from the View Actions group of the [Home Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/home-tab). The analysis is only meaningful for data sets that include observed/historical vectors alongside the simulated results (for example, Eclipse RSM history vectors); if none are present there is nothing to compare.

### The Mismatch Analysis

The window is split into a control panel on the left and the mismatch charts on the right.

![Mismatch analysis example](/img/help/mismatchanalysisexample.png)

#### Objective Function

Objective Function ... opens a dialog listing the various Summary measurement types (e.g. FOPT, WGPR, WWCT) with an editable Weight (default of 1). Increasing a measurement's weight makes it count for more in each case's overall score. This is useful for prioritising a well-trusted pressure history over a noisy rate history, for example. Changes to the weights re-ranks the case list when clicking Apply. Any changes can be disregarded by clicking Cancel.

![Objective function window](/img/help/objectivefunctionwindow.png)

#### Case Ranking

The table at the top of the left panel lists every case in the project with its overall Objective Function value, sorted from best match (lowest value) to worst. Selecting one or more cases in this table determines which cases are plotted and included in the item table below. This is designed for ensemble models.

#### Comparison Scope

Two drop down menus control the scope of the comparison:

- Field/Well: Compare field-level totals or individual well performances.
- Cumulatives/Rates: Compare cumulative volumes or instantaneous rates.

Beneath these, a set of checkboxes lists the available vectors for the current scope combination (only properties that actually have observed data are shown) so the comparison can be narrowed to specific measurements.

Both of these settings control what charts are shown on the left-hand side. Both simulated and observed data has to be available to produce a plot.

#### Comparison Table

The lower table lists the field (or each well) with a column per selected property (where data is available) showing that vector's contribution to the Objective Function, plus a ∑|x| total Objective Function column. This makes it straightforward to spot which wells are contributing most to a poor history match. Selecting a row filters the charts to that well.

### Mismatch Charts

For each selected property, a chart plots the observed data as black points against time, with one coloured line per selected case showing the simulated result. A single shared legend lists Observed properties plus one entry per case, using a consistent colour for each case across every chart. The y-axis is scaled consistently across the observed and all simulated series so the mismatch is easy to read visually, not just from the objective function value.

### Typical Workflow

A typical workflow might be:

1. Load an ensemble of history-matching cases into a [Multi-Case Project](/docs/reference/loading-data/projects/multi-case-projects).
2. Open [Show Mismatches](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/home-tab) and review the case ranking to identify the best- and worst-matching realizations.
3. Adjust measurement weights in the Objective Function dialog if some historical data should carry more or less influence, and re-check the ranking.
4. Switch the Comparison Scope to Well and step through wells with a high ∑|x| contribution to see which wells and measurements are driving the mismatch.
5. Use the observed-vs-simulated charts to judge whether the discrepancy is a level offset, a trend/timing issue, or noise, informing what to adjust in the next history-matching iteration.

title: Welcome to S3analyse
summary: S3analyse is Sciencesoft’s next generation reservoir simulation post-processing software package.
markdown:
## Welcome

***

### Next generation reservoir simulation analysis

S3analyse is Sciencesoft’s next generation reservoir simulation post-processing software package. Built on our experience of developing and supporting S3GRAF over many years, S3analyse takes reservoir simulation plotting and analysis to the next level.

S3analyse supports the widest range of simulators in the market, including Eclipse, Intersect (corner point grids), Nexus, T-Nav, Meteor/UTCHEM and CMG. The power and ease-of-use of S3analyse will enable reservoir engineers to enhance their productivity and make key decisions fast.

S3analyse will load and plot data from ensembles with 100s of simulation runs in seconds. Multiple standard dashboards include single run and ensemble NPV, with the ability for the user to create their own dashboards.

S3analyse also contains our proprietary and innovative HPG (High Performance Grids) technology. HPG enables engineers to load and view large grids (tens of millions of cells) and associated data (potentially several Gbytes in size) in seconds, thus eliminating the data loading bottleneck.

[Getting help](/docs/reference/welcome-to-s3analyse/getting-help)

[System requirements](/docs/reference/welcome-to-s3analyse/system-requirements)

### Note

Parts of this help are still in development and further content will be added in future releases.

markdown:
## Radar Plot Settings

***

### Overview

The data and its point of interest that define the chart are available to set for each widget chart type. These settings shown when the mouse cursor is hovering over the Radar Plot. They allow the selection of a property or setting to update the chart.

For Radar Plots the appearance settings are available from the Radar Plot Settings dialog.

### Radar Plot Data Settings

The data that forms the Radar Plot can be set. The settings are available on the Radar Plot itself when the mouse cursor is hovering over the plot. The settings are:

#### Vector

This drop down list contains all the available properties to be plotted.

The list of Radar Plot properties lists the Init vectors; Absolute of Field Errors Summed; Summed Absolute Field Errors; and Summary Field vectors.

#### Point of Interest

The Point of Interest is the data point of the chosen property to plot on the Radar Plot. For cumulative vectors, the point of interest lies naturally with the last point. First value, averages, minimums and maximums are also available.

### Radar Plot Appearance Settings

The appearance settings are available from the Radar Plot Settings dialog. This includes:

- [Radar Settings](/docs/reference/dashboards/widgets/radar-plot/radar-plot-settings/radar-settings)
- [Axes](/docs/reference/dashboards/widgets/radar-plot/radar-plot-settings/axes)
- [θ-Axis](/docs/reference/dashboards/widgets/radar-plot/radar-plot-settings/axes/axis)
- [R-Axis Settings](/docs/reference/dashboards/widgets/radar-plot/radar-plot-settings/axes/r-axis-settings)

#### Accessing the Radar Plot Widget Settings

You can access the Radar Plot Settings through the widget interface:

1. Open the [Dashboard](/docs/reference/dashboards) you wish to customize
2. Double left-click on the Radar Plot widget within the Dashboard

title: Line Analysis
summary: Line Analysis charts are a method of viewing maps data of a single cell and how it changes when viewed from each of the cell's four dimensions; I, J, K and Time.
markdown:
## Line Analysis

***

### Overview

Line Analysis charts are a method of viewing maps data of a single cell and how it changes when viewed from each of the cell's four dimensions; I, J, K and Time.

The Line Analysis chart is composed of four unified plots. These are, for the given cell and time step:

- Plot the chosen vectors values for all cells in that I-row
- Plot the chosen vectors values for all cells in that J-row
- Plot the chosen vectors values for all cells in that K-layers
- Plot the chosen vectors values for all time steps

### Creating a Line Analysis Chart

Line Analysis charts are limited to map properties (Solution or Init data). They can be created by:

- Navigating to the appropriate map property in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view).
- Right-click the chosen property in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) and selecting Line Analysis for <property>.

The Line Analysis appearance can then be customised, such as titles, axes and colours.

### Example

![Line analysis example](/img/help/lineanalysisexample.png)

In this example the Line Analysis has been shown for Pressure for cell (10, 10, 5):

- The top-left plot has Pressure values for all cells in I-row (1, 10, 5) to (21, 10, 5)
- The top-right plot has Pressure values for all cells in J-row (10, 1, 5) to (10, 31, 5)
- The bottom-left plot has Pressure values for all cells in K-layers (10, 10, 1) to (10, 10, 14)
- The bottom-right plot has Pressure values for cell (10, 10, 5) for each time step date

### Modifying Line Analysis Plots

The appearance of a Line Analysis can be changed as desired and the data used in the chart can also be updated.

#### Modifying the Line Analysis Plots

Line Analysis Plots have an extensive list of settings to customise the appearance. These are outlined in [Line Analysis Settings](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-analysis/line-analysis-settings) and can be accessed by double left-clicking on the any part of the Line Analysis chart.

These are in complement to the [Line Analysis Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs/chart-tools/line-analysis-tab) that offers a selection of settings controlling the formulation and the data used in the chart.

#### Modifying the Data in the Line Analysis Plots

Changing the map property used to generate a chart is achieved with the Selected Property group in the [Line Analysis Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs/chart-tools/line-analysis-tab). This allows the selection of any appropriate data from the Project to update the chart.

The Line Analysis Ribbon Tab allows for the selection of which cell to base the analysis on. This is available in the Selected Cell group. The cell I, J and K can be set. The timestep is instead selected from the Selected Property group via the Timestep drop down list.

##### Interactivity

The Line Analysis chart is interactive and can be updated by clicking on marker points of any of the four plots. Left-clicking on a line point will update the cell index or time step value the analysis is based on and update the plots accordingly.

For example, clicking on the 3rd marker in the I-chart (for I = 3) will update the J and K analyses to the third row of cells so (3, J, 5) and (3, 10, K). Likewise the date chart will update with the values of the (3, 10, 5) cell.

### Exporting Line Analysis Plots

Line Analysis Plots can be exported with the [Report](/docs/reference/exporting-reports) Feature.

### Scripts and Line Analysis Plots

Line Analysis Plots are supported by [Python Scripting](/docs/reference/python-scripting).

## Widgets

***

### Overview

There are a range of widgets that can be added to the Dashboard.

#### Available Dashboard Widgets

Each widget represents a different type of chart or analysis:

- [Cross Plot](/docs/reference/dashboards/widgets/cross-plot)
  - Visualizes relationships between two variables.
  - Supports parameter-based axes (e.g., from [.](/docs/reference/loading-data/supported-data-types/input-parameter-files)[params](/docs/reference/loading-data/supported-data-types/input-parameter-files)[files](/docs/reference/loading-data/supported-data-types/input-parameter-files)).

* [Cumulative Distribution Plot](/docs/reference/dashboards/widgets/cumulative-distribution-plot)
  - Shows distribution of values across cases.
  - Includes overlays for P10, P50, and P90.

+ [Ensemble Summary Plot](/docs/reference/dashboards/widgets/ensemble-summary-plot)
  - Displays summary trends across all cases.
  - Supports overlays like min, max, average.

- [Grid Property Plot](/docs/reference/dashboards/widgets/grid-property-plot)
  - Visualizes spatial properties from grid data.

* [Pearson Coefficient Plot](/docs/reference/dashboards/widgets/pearson-coefficient-plot)
  - Shows correlation between input parameters and output metrics.

+ [Radar Plot](/docs/reference/dashboards/widgets/radar-plot)
  - Compares multiple metrics in a radial format.

- [Well Statistics Plot](/docs/reference/dashboards/widgets/well-statistics-plot)
  - Summarizes well-level performance metrics.

markdown:
## Y-Axis Settings

***

###

### ![Grid property settings y axis](/img/help/gridpropertysettings-yaxis.png)

###

### Overview

The Grid Property Y-Axis Settings provides options to customize the appearance and presentation of a Grid Property Dashboard widget. These settings allow you to control the Y-axis title, line, label and range elements.

Any changes are applied directly to the Grid Property widget as they are made.

#### Accessing the Grid Property Widget Settings

You can access the Grid Property Settings through the widget interface:

1. Open the Dashboard you wish to customize
2. Double left-click on the Grid Property widget within the Dashboard
3. Select Y-Axis from the parent Axes node of the treeview in the Dashboard Settings dialog

### Available Settings Categories

The Y-Axis Settings are organized into four main sections:

#### Axis Title

Control how the axis title appears on your graph:

- Title: Add or modify the text of the main title of your Axis

* Font: Customize font (size, style, colour) with the options available by clicking Select. A preview of the current font is shown with the "Preview" label.

#### Axis Line

Configure the appearance of the axis:

- Thickness: Set the thickness of the axes lines.

* Colour: Set the colour of the axes lines.

+ Location: Toggle the top/bottom or left/right location of the axis.

#### Axis Labels

Customize how value labels appear along the axis:

- Visible: Toggle the visibility of the axis labels.

* Angle: Set the angle of the axis labels either with the slider or by typing into or stepping through the text box.

+ Format: Set the format for the axis labels:
  - Normal: Decimal representation of the label values, e.g. 2,000 or 3,000,000
  - Abbreviate: Engineering notation representation of the label values, e.g. 2K or 3M
  - Scientific Notation: Scientific notation representation of the label values, e.g. 2x103 or 3x106
  - Date: Represent the axis values as dates (when applicable)

- Font: Customize font (size, style, colour) with the options available by clicking Select. A preview of the current font is shown with the "Preview" label.

* Location: Toggle between presenting the labels Inside or Outside of the Chart.

#### Range Values

This section provides options for the user to set the limits and the interval steps of the axis:

- Minimum: Sets the maximum value for the axis limit
- Maximum: Sets the minimum value for the axis limit
- Interval: Sets the major interval value between labels for the axis
- Minor Interval: Sets the minor interval value between labels for the axis
- Invert: Toggles the inversion of the axis limits
- Log: Toggles a log scale for the axis

Any changes to the Range Values can be reset by clicking ![Undo icon](/img/help/undo-icon.png)

title: Regions
summary: A Region is a saved, named subset of grid cells that can be applied to any grid, or used in other analysis tools such as Histograms and Grid Scatter Plots to view data for just that subset.
markdown:
## Regions

***

### Overview

A Region is a saved, named subset of grid cells that can be applied to any grid, or used in other analysis tools such as [Histograms](/docs/reference/chart-displays/histograms) and [Grid Scatter Plots](/docs/reference/chart-displays/grid-scatter-plot) to view data for just that subset. Two kinds of region are available: [Threshold Regions](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-features/thresholds), which you define yourself by saving a Grid [Threshold](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-settings/threshold-settings), and Numeric Regions, which are predefined by the loaded simulation dataset, for example PVT, Saturation or Fluid-in-Place regions.

#### Accessing Regions

You can access [Regions](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/regions) through the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) treeview. Open the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) and expand the [Regions](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements#CalculatedData) node under the [Calculated Data](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements#CalculatedData) node to show the Threshold Regions and Numeric Regions nodes

![Regions treeview element group](/img/help/regionstreeviewelementgroup.png)

### What Regions Do

#### Threshold Regions

A Threshold Region captures a [Threshold Settings](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-settings/threshold-settings) combination, the chosen properties, value ranges, inversions and AND/OR/XOR logic, under a saved name, so the same filter can be reapplied to any grid without having to recreate it.

#### Numeric Regions

A Numeric Region comes from the loaded [simulation dataset](/docs/reference/loading-data) itself. Each [Numeric Region node](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements#CalculatedData) lists the property it is based on and how many distinct regions are defined by the model, for example PVT (PVTNUM) or Saturation (SATNUM) regions.

### Why Use Regions

- Reuse a carefully-tuned [Threshold](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-features/thresholds) definition, such as high saturation and low pressure, across multiple grids without rebuilding it each time.
- Compare data for a specific subset of cells, such as a fault block, saturation region or PVT region, using [Histograms](/docs/reference/chart-displays/histograms) or [Grid Scatter Plots](/docs/reference/chart-displays/grid-scatter-plot) filtered to just that region.
- Work directly with the simulator's own defined regions to analyse reservoir behaviour by the model's native region breakdown, without manually re-deriving them from Thresholds.
- Keep a library of named Regions in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements#CalculatedData), so recurring analyses of a particular zone of interest are one drag-and-drop away instead of a manual Threshold setup each time.

### How to Use Regions

#### Threshold Regions

To create a new Threshold Region, set up the desired [Threshold](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-features/thresholds) with the [Threshold Settings](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-settings/threshold-settings) on a [Grid Display](/docs/reference/grid-displays), then [save](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-settings/threshold-regions) it with a name.

Drag a saved region from the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) onto a [Grid Display](/docs/reference/grid-displays) to apply it, or select it from the saved Region drop-down in [Threshold Settings](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-settings/threshold-settings)

#### Numeric Regions

Numeric Regions are not [Threshold](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-features/thresholds) definitions. Dragging and dropping them on the [Grid Display](/docs/reference/grid-displays) will shows the values for that property for all active cells.

These Numeric Regions are used for Region Filtering for [Histograms](/docs/reference/chart-displays/histograms) and [Grid Scatter Plots](/docs/reference/chart-displays/grid-scatter-plot).

title: Well Lists
summary: A Well List is a named, saved subset of the wells in a project.
markdown:
## Well Lists

***

###

### Overview

A Well List is a named, saved subset of the wells in a project. Well Lists let you build a filtered set of wells defined by name pattern, well type, or selected from a list, and save it for reuse. This can then be applied to filter which wells are used across the project (Well selection dialogs, [Charts](/docs/reference/chart-displays), and [Grids](/docs/reference/grid-displays)) without needing to re-select the same wells every time.

#### Accessing Well Lists

The Well List controls sit on the [Project Folder](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements#Project) node in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view). This consists of:

- ![Select well list control](/img/help/selectwelllistcontrol.png) Select Well List: Dropdown for quickly switching between saved Well Lists.
- ![Well list](/img/help/welllist-16-n-p.png) Show WellList Manager: Button that opens the Well List Manager Settings dialog to create or edit lists.
- ![Well list filter](/img/help/welllistfilter-16-n-p.png) Apply Well List: Toggle the filtering on or off. When on, only wells in the selected list are used; when off, all wells are available regardless of which list is selected.

### Active Well Lists

When a Well List is active (a list is selected and Apply Well List is toggled on), only the wells in that list are offered for new well selections across the project. Wells outside the list are not deleted or hidden from the underlying data – they are simply excluded from pickers, markers and searches until the Well List is turned off or a different list is selected.

#### Effect on Grid Displays

On a [Grid Display](/docs/reference/grid-displays), the active Well List restricts which wells are drawn as Well Markers (including their labels and perforations) on the grid map. Wells not in the active list are hidden, regardless of the Show Well setting in the [Ribbon](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs/grid-tools/grid-view-tab) or grid [Well Marker Settings](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-settings/well-markers).

All existing grids update their well markers when the Well List is applied, toggled off, or changed.

#### Effect on Charts

Using the Plot <property> for Well List: <welllist> [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) context menu option (see [Summary](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements#Summary)) creates a single Line Plot containing one line per well in the active Well List, for the chosen property.

If that chart is the active window when the Well List's membership subsequently changes (a different list is selected, the list is edited, or filtering is toggled), its lines are updated to match the new set of wells, there is no need to re-create the chart. Charts not created from a Well List, and lines already plotted for wells that have since dropped out of the active list, are left as they are; re-plotting is required to pick up the change.

#### Effect on Broadcasting and Indexing

When [Indexing](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots/indexing) by Member (i.e. by well) from the [Chart Data Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs/chart-tools/chart-data-tab), the list of wells offered to search or broadcast to is restricted to those in the active Well List. This applies to stepping to the next/previous well and to selecting target wells in the [Broadcast](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/window-view/broadcasting) picker, and therefore also to [Broadcast Groups](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/window-view/broadcasting): replacing the well on one chart in a Group will only offer wells from the active list to propagate to the rest of the Group. Indexing by Case or Property Name is not affected by an active Well List.

If none of a chart's own wells fall within the active Well List, the filter is bypassed for that chart and the full set of wells is offered instead, so the picker is never left empty.

### Well List Manager Settings

The Well List Manager Settings dialog is where lists are built and edited.

#### ![Well list manager dialog](/img/help/welllistmanagerdialog.png)

#### Well Lists

Previously created Well Lists can be chosen from the saved list by selecting the named from the Selected well list dropdown list. By default this is set to <All Wells> list, which always contains every well in the project. This selection will populate the rest of the dialog with its definition and its well selection.

#### Filter

A filter can be defined to quickly find a subset of well names, defining what wells appear in the list for selection:

- Name Filter: A text pattern to narrow the well list by name, including wildcards, can be set in this textbox.
- Well type filter: Restrict the list of wells to the Injector, Producer or Shut wells (wells are classified automatically from the simulation's grid or summary data).

The Filter lists the available wells matching filter. Each well can be included/excluded from the Well List be checking/unchecking the corresponding checkboxes. There are some controls that can help navigate the list:

- ![Check all](/img/help/check-all-16-n-p.png) Select All: Select all the listed wells (this does not apply to the hidden wells).
- ![Uncheck all](/img/help/uncheck-all-16-n-p.png) Deselect All: Deselect all the listed wells (this does not apply to the hidden wells).
- ![Invert colours](/img/help/invert-colours-16-n-p.png) Invert Selection: Toggle the selected and deselected wells.
- ![Sort](/img/help/sort-16-n-p.png) Sort: Sorts the listed wells alphanumerically.
- ![Show hide show](/img/help/showhide-show-16.png) Show/Hide: Show/hide the unselected wells.

#### Saving

Type a name into Well list name and click ![Save icon](/img/help/save-icon.png) Save to store the current checkbox selection as a new (or updated) named Well List.

#### Apply / Close

Apply applies the currently selected list's filtering across the project immediately. Close dismisses the dialog.

#### Manage Well Lists

Clicking Manage Well Lists opens the Well List Files dialog, which lists every saved Well List file. It allows one or more to be selected via their checkbox and deleted with the Delete button. If a list is currently in use it is highlighted in bold.

![Well list file manager dialog](/img/help/welllistfilemanagerdialog.png)

#### Storage of Well Lists

Well Lists are saved as individual XML files in a WellLists subfolder of the project's base folder. They and are automatically reloaded and re-validated against the project's current wells the next time the project is opened. A saved list that no longer matches the project's wells (e.g. after loading different data) is silently skipped rather than shown.

title: Filtering
summary: Dashboards offer the ability to filter the cases included in the display.
markdown:
## Filtering

***

### Overview

[Dashboards](/docs/reference/dashboards) offer the ability to filter the cases included in the display. Cases can be included/excluded explicitly or based on values of the Summary Field property values. Filtered cases are no longer included in the widget charts. This allows easy exclusion of outlier data sets or poorly performing simulation runs in a sensitivity runs.

Dashboards support advanced [Filtering](/docs/reference/dashboards/filtering). This is achieved with:

- [Project-Wide Filter](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/project-wide-filter): This allows case filtering for multi-case model from a global filter.
- [Summary Property Filter](/docs/reference/dashboards/filtering/dashboard-filter): This allows case filtering based on Summary properties for only this Dashboard.

Any changes to the list of valid cases will be reflected in the widget charts.

title: Grid View Tab
summary: The Grid View tab contains the common settings for the appearance of the active Grid.
markdown:
## Grid View Ribbon Context Tab

***

![Ribbon grid view context tab colours group](/img/help/ribbon-gridviewcontexttabcoloursgroup.png)![Ribbon grid view context tab cell display group](/img/help/ribbon-gridviewcontexttabcelldisplaygroup.png)![Ribbon grid view context tab display group](/img/help/ribbon-gridviewcontexttabdisplaygroup.png)![Ribbon grid view context tab views group](/img/help/ribbon-gridviewcontexttabviewsgroup.png)![Ribbon grid view context tab axis group](/img/help/ribbon-gridviewcontexttabaxisgroup.png)![Ribbon grid view context tab wells group](/img/help/ribbon-gridviewcontexttabwellsgroup.png)![Ribbon grid view context tab scaling group](/img/help/ribbon-gridviewcontexttabscalinggroup.png)

### Overview

The Grid View tab contains the common settings for the appearance of the active [Grid](/docs/reference/grid-displays).

### Access and Visibility

The Grid View tab appears in the ribbon when a [Grid display](/docs/reference/grid-displays) is active.

The tab updates its content based on what you select.

### Main Functional Groups

The Grid View ribbon tab is organized into several key groups:

#### Colours Group

##### Invert

This inverts the colours of the background and the axes and grid colouring.

##### Colours

Allows colour selection for various aspects of the grid which can be chosen.

This includes the Active Cells, Inactive Cells, Background, Grid Wireframe and Gird Wall.

#### Cell Display Group

##### LGR

Toggles the display of the Local Grid Refinements (LGRs), if they exist in the model.

##### Active Cells

Toggles the display of Active Cells.

##### Inactive Cells

Toggles the display of Inactive Cells.

##### Cell Information

Displays cell information as a tooltip. Control of what is included in the tooltip is available in the [Tooltip Settings](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-settings/tooltip-settings) for the Grid.

#### Display Group

##### Wireframe

Toggles the display of the grid cell outline.

##### Cell Faces

Toggles the display of the grid cell faces.

##### Lighting

This turns on the lighting facility, which gives a feeling of depth to the grid display.

##### Transparency

Set the transparency level of the grid.

Changing the transparency of the cells allows you to see inside the grid for details which would you would otherwise be unavailable to view. Valid figures lie between 0 (opaque) and 100 (totally transparent).

#### Views Group

The Layers settings allow easy switching between the grid display modes. These are:

| ![Alllayers3d](/img/help/alllayers3d-16-n-p.png) 3D All | View the full grid in 3D |
| --- | --- |
| ![Singlelayer3d](/img/help/singlelayer3d-16-n-p.png) Single Layer | View a single chosen layer/section in 3D |
| ![2dview](/img/help/2dview-16-n-p.png) 2D View | View a single chosen layer/section in 2D plan view |

When using Single Layer or 2D View the layer/section displayed can be selected from the dropdown menus. Which slice and what plane (XY, XZ or YZ) can be selected. For 2D View the top, middle or bottom cell faces can be shown.

#### Axis Group

The orientations of the X, Y and Z axis can be inverted or mirrored:

| ![Flipx 16x16](/img/help/flipx-16x16.png) Flip X | Toggle the direction of the X-axis |
| --- | --- |
| ![Flipy 16x16](/img/help/flipy-16x16.png) Flip Y | Toggle the direction of the Y-axis |
| ![Flipz 16x16](/img/help/flipz-16x16.png) Flip Z | Toggle the direction of the Z-axis |

#### Wells Group

![Wells](/img/help/wells-32-n-p.png) Show Wells

Toggle the display of the wells. This includes markers, labels and perforations.

##### Labels

Toggle the display of well labels.

##### Perforations

Toggle the display of well perforations.

##### Markers Above

This shows the well markers and labels above the grid bounding box.

#### Scaling Group

##### Mode

Predefined scaling modes can be applied to the grid. These are:

| Arbitrary | Scaling mode where the user [Scale Factors](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-settings/scale-factor) are applied to the grid |
| --- | --- |
| Fit Window | Scaling mode where the grid is adjusted to occupy the entire available display area |
| Square | Scaling that ensures that the grid maintains equal scaling across all axes, resulting in a uniform square grid |
| True Scale | Scaling mode where the grid maintains accurate, real-world proportions |

##### Z Scaling

Set the scaling of the Z-axis. This helps to see the grid in more detail if the grid layers are compressed.

title: CMG
summary: The CMG Settings provide options for loading CMG data sets.
markdown:
## CMG Settings

***

![Main settings CMG](/img/help/mainsettings-cmg.png)

### Overview

The CMG Settings provide options for loading CMG data sets.

#### Accessing the CMG Settings

The General Settings dialog can be accesses in two ways; either click the Settings cog ![Options icon](/img/help/options-icon.png) icon in the Quick Access Toolbar or selecting Settings in the File menu. From this select CMG in the treeview.

### CMG Settings

#### Use Load Dialog

Selecting Use Load Dialog will add a step to the load process for CMG data sets to allow the user to configure the load of each data set. The CMG [Load Dialog](/docs/reference/loading-data/supported-data-types/cmg/load-dialog) will be presented when selecting a CMG model for loading allowing the selection of data types to load. The load dialog will be initialised with the setting defined in CMG settings.

If unselected the load operation will use the settings as defined in CMG Settings.

#### Data Types to Load

Select the relevant checkboxes for each data type to be included when loading the model.

#### Summary Data

Select the relevant checkboxes for each Summary data class to be included when loading the model summary data.

### Dialog Controls

#### ![New item2](/img/help/newitem2.png) Reset Current to Default

Resets the current page of settings to the system default.

#### ![New item1](/img/help/newitem1.png) Reset All to Default

Resets all the settings to the system default.

#### OK

Applies any changes to the load selections without applying the settings as a new default.

#### Cancel

Exits the settings and cancel any changes.

#### ![New item](/img/help/newitem.png) Help

Open the Help at the relevant section.

title: Design Tab
summary: The Dashboard Design tab contains the settings for the layout of the active Dashboard and controls to add widget charts to the Dashboard.
markdown:
## Design Ribbon Context Tab

***

![Ribbon dashboard context tab tiles group](/img/help/ribbon-dashboardcontexttabtilesgroup.png)![Ribbon dashboard context tab panels group](/img/help/ribbon-dashboardcontexttabpanelsgroup.png)

### Overview

The Dashboard Design tab contains the settings for the layout of the active [Dashboard](/docs/reference/dashboards) and controls to add widget charts to the Dashboard.

### Access and Visibility

The Design tab appears in the ribbon when a [Dashboard](/docs/reference/dashboards) is active.

### Main Functional Groups

The Design ribbon tab is organized into several key groups:

#### Tiles Group

##### Max Columns

This sets the maximum number of columns of widget charts in the Dashboard. Rows will be added as necessary.

#### Panels Group

The type of plot to be created and added to the Dashboard is chosen here:

##### Cross Plot

This will add a [Cross Plot](/docs/reference/dashboards/widgets/cross-plot) to the Dashboard.

#####

##### Cumulative Distribution Plot

This will add a [Cumulative Distribution Plot](/docs/reference/dashboards/widgets/cumulative-distribution-plot) to the Dashboard.

#####

##### Ensemble Plot

This will add a [Ensemble Summary Plot](/docs/reference/dashboards/widgets/ensemble-summary-plot) to the Dashboard.

#####

##### Grid Property Plot

This will add a [Grid Property Plot](/docs/reference/dashboards/widgets/grid-property-plot) to the Dashboard.

## Grid Details

***

### Overview

The Grid Details window reports the size and geometry statistics of a loaded grid, such as the number of active and loaded cells, the number of visible faces and vertices, and an estimate of the graphics memory required to display it. This is particularly useful when working with large grids or grids containing Local Grid Refinements (LGRs), where it can be difficult to judge size and complexity from the display alone.

#### Accessing Grid Settings

Grid Details is opened from the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view):

1. Right-click on a Grid item in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements#Grid).
2. Select View Grid Details from the Grid Context Menu.

### Grids Details Window

The Grid Details window is split into a summary of the whole grid and a table breaking the statistics down by individual grid and LGR.

![Grid details window](/img/help/griddetailswindow.png)

#### Summary Totals

A table of totals combining every grid loaded for the case, including any Local Grid Refinements:

- Origin: Case name for the model.
- \# Grids: The total number of grids, i.e. the root grid plus any Local Grid Refinements.
- \# Loaded Cells: The total number of cells loaded into memory.
- \# Active Cells: The total number of active cells.
- \# Visible Faces: The total number of cell faces currently rendered.
- \# Vertices: The total number of vertices used to render the grid.
- Graphics: An estimate of the graphics memory required to display the grid, shown in the most appropriate unit (e.g. MB, GB).
- Vertices/Cell: The average number of vertices per loaded cell, an indicator of rendering complexity.

#### Individual Grid Table

Below the summary, a table lists each individual grid that makes up the case. This comprises the root grid and, if present, each Local Grid Refinement (LGR):

- Name: The name of the grid.
- Parent Grid, Start Cells, Stop Cells: These are only shown when the case contains Local Grid Refinements. These identify the parent grid an LGR was carved from and the I, J, K cell range it occupies within that parent.
- Dimensions: The grid’s Nx × Ny × Nz dimensions and total cell count.
- \# Loaded Cells, \# Active Cells, \# Visible Faces, \# Vertices, Vertices/Cell: The same statistics as the summary totals above, but for this grid only.
- Open: Click this icon to open this specific grid as a [Grid Display](/docs/reference/grid-displays).

markdown:
## Cut Plane Settings

***

![Grid settings cut planes](/img/help/gridsettings-cutplanes.png)

### Overview

The Cut Plane Settings provide options to create and adjust a plane, cut through the body of the grid, to observe the cell values within.

The [Cut Plane](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-features/cut-planes) can be arranged as a single plane sliced through the grid or as a series of planes in a regular pattern. These allow a method of viewing the data within the grid display while maintaining the three-dimensionality.

Any changes are applied directly to the Grid as they are made.

#### Accessing the Grid Settings

You can access the Cut Plane Settings through the grid interface:

1. Open the Grid you wish to customize
2. Double left-click on the Grid
3. Select Cut Planes from the treeview in the Grid Editors dialog

### Cut Plane Modes

The [Cut Plane](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-features/cut-planes) is defined by a Mode. There are two general types of Mode; a single or pair of planes that can be orientated in any direction or a stacked arrangement of regular planes aligned to a grid direction.

### Available Settings Categories

The Cut Plane Settings are organized into a number of sections dependant upon the Mode.

#### Show Cut Plane

Show Cut Plane toggles the Cut Plane on/off. If unchecked, planes will not appear in the grid.

#### Multi-Plane Mode

The Mode controls what type of Cut Plane display is being shown on the grid.

The available modes are:

- Free-Orientated Planes:
  - Single Plane: Show a single Cut Plane on the grid with settings to control its orientation.
  - Plane Pair: Show a pair of parallel Cut Planes on the grid, in the same orientation and separated by a distance from a common point.
- Axis-Orientated Planes:
  - Stacked X: Show a series of parallel Cut Planes orientated to the YZ-plane at various steps in X.
  - Stacked Y: Show a series of parallel Cut Planes orientated to the XZ-plane at various steps in Y.
  - Stacked Z: Show a series of parallel Cut Planes orientated to the XY-plane at various steps in Z.
  - Mesh in X and Y: Show two series of parallel Cut Planes orientated to the YZ-plane and to the XZ-plane at various steps in X and Y to form a waffle pattern.
  - Mesh in X, Y and Z: Show three series of parallel Cut Planes orientated to the YZ-plane, XZ-plane and XY-plane at various steps in each direction.

### Free-Orientated Plane Mode Settings

When using the Single Plane or Plane Pair Mode the Plane Orientation settings are made available.

#### Plane Orientation

The orientation and position of the plane can be controlled from these settings:

##### Orientation

The Orientation of the plane can be selected from this drop-down menu:

- XY: Create a Cut Plane on the XY-plane
- XZ: Create a Cut Plane on the XZ-plane
- YZ: Create a Cut Plane on the YZ-plane
- Arbitrary: Create an arbitrary plane

##### Use Centre of Rotation

Toggle the Cut Plane to be centred around the [Centre of Rotation](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-settings/centre-of-rotation) rather than the centre point of the grid.

##### Position

The position of the Cut Plane can be controlled from these settings. Only in Arbitrary orientation will the Rotation and Tilt be available. Only in Plain Pair Mode will the Spacing be visible and available.

- Rotation: Set the rotation angle around the centre-point of the plane (only available for Arbitrary orientation).
- Tilt: Set the tilt angle to the XY-plane (only available for Arbitrary orientation).
- Offset: Set the offset in the chosen dimension (X-value for YZ-plane, Y-value for XZ-plane, Z-value for XY-plane and grid centre-point for Arbitrary planes).
- Spacing: Set the spacing between the Plane Pair (only visible in Plane Pair mode).

#### Grid Cell Display Options

The Cut Plane can be arranged to only show cell data incident with the Cut Plane. Alternatively it can show all the cells on one side of the cut as well:

For Single Plane mode the cell display options are:

- Plane Only: Only show cell data that intersects the Cut Plane.
- Minus Side: Show cell data on the Cut Plane and all cells on the minus side (of the Offset) of the Cut Plane.
- Plus Side: Show cell data on the Cut Plane and all cells on the plus side (of the Offset) of the Cut Plane.

For Plane Pair mode the cell display options are:

- Planes Only: Only show cell data that intersects the Cut Planes.
- Between: Show cell data on the Cut Planes and all cells between the Cut Planes.
- Outside: Show cell data on the Cut Planes and all cells outside the space between the Cut Planes.

### Axis-Orientated Plane Mode Settings

When using the Stacked X, Stacked Y, Stacked Z, Mesh in X and Y or Mesh in X, Y and Z modes different the Plane Orientation settings are made available.

#### Plane Spacing

The spacing of the planes can be controlled from these settings:

##### Set Plane Spacing

This will set whether a set number of planes are added to the grid or planes are added with a set spacing between them.

![Cut plane spacing group box no planes](/img/help/cutplanespacinggroupboxnoplanes.png)

Spacing by number of planes:

- No. X Planes: Set the number of YZ Cut Planes to be fit in the X-dimension (only available for Stacked X and the Mesh modes).
- No. Y Planes: Set the number of XZ Cut Planes to be fit in the Y-dimension (only available for Stacked Y and the Mesh modes).
- No. Z Planes: Set the number of XY Cut Planes to be fit in the Z-dimension (only available for Stacked Z and the Mesh in X, Y and Z modes).

One plane is paced at each extremity of the chosen axis and one at the centre point. Planes are added in pairs so there is always a plane at these positions. For this reason the number of planes is always odd.

![Cut plane spacing group box spacing](/img/help/cutplanespacinggroupboxspacing.png)

Spacing by distance:

- X Spacing: Set the spacing between YZ Cut Planes in the X-dimension (only available for Stacked X and the Mesh modes).
- Y Spacing: Set the spacing between XZ Cut Planes in the Y-dimension (only available for Stacked Y and the Mesh modes).
- Z Spacing: Set the spacing between XY Cut Planes in the Z-dimension (only available for Stacked Z and the Mesh in X, Y and Z modes).

### Common Settings

#### Plane Appearance

The appearance of the Plane/Planes and their Normal are controlled from these settings:

- Show Plane: Toggle the plane on/off. Select the colour of the plane with the colour picker.
- Show Normal: Toggle the normal of the plane on/off. Select the colour of the normal with the colour picker.
- Transparency: Set the level of transparency of the plane from 0% (opaque) to 100% (complete transparency).

## Y-Axis Settings

***

###

### ![Cross plot settings y axis](/img/help/crossplotsettings-yaxis.png)

###

### Overview

The Cross Plot Y-Axis Settings provides options to customize the appearance and presentation of a Cross Plot Dashboard widget. These settings allow you to control the title and axes elements.

Any changes are applied directly to the Cross Plot widget as they are made.

#### Accessing the Cross Plot Widget Settings

You can access the Cross Plot Settings through the widget interface:

1. Open the Dashboard you wish to customize
2. Double left-click on the Cross Plot widget within the Dashboard
3. Expand the Axes treeview node from the Cross Plot node
4. Select Y-Axis from the parent Axes node of the treeview in the Dashboard Settings dialog

### Available Settings Categories

The Y-Axis Settings are organized into four main sections:

#### Axis Title

Control how the axis title appears on your graph:

- Title: Add or modify the text of the main title of your Axis

* Font: Customize font (size, style, colour) with the options available by clicking Select. A preview of the current font is shown with the "Preview" label.

#### Axis Line

Configure the appearance of the axis:

- Thickness: Set the thickness of the axes lines.

* Colour: Set the colour of the axes lines.

+ Location: Toggle the top/bottom or left/right location of the axis.

#### Axis Labels

Customize how value labels appear along the axis:

- Visible: Toggle the visibility of the axis labels.

* Angle: Set the angle of the axis labels either with the slider or by typing into or stepping through the text box.

+ Format: Set the format for the axis labels:
  - Normal: Decimal representation of the label values, e.g. 2,000 or 3,000,000
  - Abbreviate: Engineering notation representation of the label values, e.g. 2K or 3M
  - Scientific Notation: Scientific notation representation of the label values, e.g. 2x103 or 3x106
  - Date: Represent the axis values as dates (when applicable)

- Font: Customize font (size, style, colour) with the options available by clicking Select. A preview of the current font is shown with the "Preview" label.

* Location: Toggle between presenting the labels Inside or Outside of the Chart.

#### Range Values

This section provides options for the user to set the limits and the interval steps of the axis:

- Minimum: Sets the maximum value for the axis limit
- Maximum: Sets the minimum value for the axis limit
- Interval: Sets the major interval value between labels for the axis
- Minor Interval: Sets the minor interval value between labels for the axis
- Invert: Toggles the inversion of the axis limits
- Log: Toggles a log scale for the axis

Any changes to the Range Values can be reset by clicking ![Undo icon](/img/help/undo-icon.png)

markdown:
## Ternary Settings

***

![Grid settings ternary settings](/img/help/gridsettings-ternarysettings.png)

### Overview

The Ternary Settings allow you to display a combined Oil/Gas/Water saturation colour map on the grid, using the SOIL, SGAS and SWAT solution vectors for the currently loaded timestep. It will override the currently displayed property and show the saturations as a combined display.

Any changes are applied directly to the Grid as they are made.

#### Accessing the Grid Settings

You can access the Ternary Settings through the grid interface:

1. Open the Grid you wish to customize
2. Double left-click on the Grid
3. Select Ternary Settings from the treeview in the Grid Editors dialog

### Available Settings Categories

The Ternary Settings are organized into four sections:

#### Show Ternary

The ternary display on the grid can be switched on or off by toggling Show Ternary.

Show Ternary is only available when the SOIL, SGAS and SWAT solution vectors are all present and a timestep is loaded. If this is not the case, the control is disabled. Only when this is checked are the other controls enabled.

#### Limits Mode

Choose how the minimum and maximum saturation limits used to build the ternary colour map are determined:

- Default Limits: Use the full 0 to 1 range for each phase.
- Data Limits: Use the minimum saturation value actually present in the currently loaded timestep for each phase. These limits are recalculated whenever the timestep changes.
- User Defined Limits: Manually specify the minimum saturation value for each phase in the Limits section below.

#### Colour Scheme

Customise the colours used to render the ternary map:

- Colour Scheme: Choose one of the predefined corner colour schemes (Default, Scheme 2, Scheme 3, Scheme 4) used to colour the Oil, Gas and Water phases of the ternary diagram.
- Out of Bounds Colour: Set the colour used for cells whose combined saturation values fall outside all three phase ranges. This is intended for when cell values lie outwith user defined limits.

#### Limits

The Limits section displays the minimum and maximum saturation value used for the Oil, Gas and Water phases:

- Oil/Gas/Water Saturation Min/Max: These are read-only in Default Limits and Data Limits mode. In User Defined Limits mode, the minimum value for each phase can be edited directly, and the maximum for each phase updates automatically to 1 minus the minimum values of the other two phases:

![Grid settings ternary settings user limits](/img/help/gridsettings-ternarysettings-userlimits.png)

If the three minimum values sum to 1 or more, the limits are invalid: the Oil minimum value is kept, the Gas and Water minimum values are reset to 0, and a warning is displayed: "Limits sum is greater or equal to 1. Oil kept, Gas/Water reset to 0."

## Nexus Load Dialog

***

![Load dialog nexus default](/img/help/loaddialog-nexusdefault.png)

### Overview

By default when an Nexus file is loaded into S3analyse the data set is loaded and presented in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) with the default load options. These default options can be changed for the system in the [Nexus Load Settings](/docs/reference/general-settings/simulators/nexus).

Additionally, a load dialog can be shown to allow the user to tailor the load options for each Nexus data set. From this the user can select what data types and what summary classes to load and then click OK to complete the load.

#### Accessing the Nexus Load Dialog

The Nexus Load DIalog is presented when attempting to load an Nexus file and Use Load Dialog is checked in the [Nexus Load Settings](/docs/reference/general-settings/simulators/nexus).

### Available Settings Categories

The Nexus Load options are organized into three main sections:

#### Use Load Dialog

Selecting Use Load Dialog will cause this dialog to be presented during the load process for Nexus data sets to allow the user to configure the load of each data set.

Checking/checking this options will only affect future loads and only if Save Settings & Load is also clicked.

#### Data Types To Load

Select which types of simulation data to load:

- Grid: Loads structured grid data for the model.
- Init: Loads the initialised map data.
- Summary: Loads the summary data.
- Solution: Loads the dynamic map data.

Selecting Select All will check all the data types.

#### Summary Data

Use this section to specify which data classes from the summary/plot file should be loaded:

- AREA: Area data.
- CONN: Connection data.
- CONNLIST: Connection List data.
- FIELD: Field-wide data.
- FLOSTA: Flow Station data.
- GATHER: Gathering Centre data.
- NODE: Node data.
- PATBAL: Pattern Balance data.
- REGION: Region-wide data.
- SLAM: Slam data.
- SLPERF: SLPERF data.
- SURFACE: Surface Network pressure and rate data.
- TARGET: Target and Inject Balance data.
- WELLS: Well production/injection data.
- WLLYR: Well data by layer perforation.
- WELLBORE: Wellbore data.

Selecting Select All will check all the Summary data types.

#### Save Settings & Load

Saves current selection as a new default and starts data loading.

#### Load

Loads using current selections without applying the settings as a new default.

#### Cancel

Exits the dialog and cancel the load process.

markdown:
## Cumulative Distribution Plot Settings

***

### Overview

The data and its point of interest that define the chart are available to set for each widget chart type. These settings shown when the mouse cursor is hovering over the Cumulative Distribution Plot. They allow the selection of a property or setting to update the chart.

For Cumulative Distribution Plot the appearance settings are available from the Cumulative Distribution Plot Settings dialog.

### Cumulative Distribution Plot Data Settings

The data that forms the Cumulative Distribution Plot can be set. The settings are available on the Cumulative Distribution Plot itself when the mouse cursor is hovering over the plot. The settings are:

#### Vector

This drop down list contains all the available properties to be plotted.

The list of Cumulative Distribution Plot properties starts with each of the parameters in the [.params file](/docs/reference/loading-data/supported-data-types/input-parameter-files). Following this are Init vectors; Absolute of Field Errors Summed; Summed Absolute Field Errors; and Summary Field vectors.

#### Point of Interest

The Point of Interest is the data point of the chosen property to plot on the Cumulative Distribution Plot. For cumulative vectors, the point of interest lies naturally with the last point, and for rates and pressures, usually the averages or perhaps the minimum on pressures.

### Cumulative Distribution Plot Appearance Settings

The appearance settings are available from the Cumulative Distribution Plot Settings dialog. This includes:

- [Cumulative Distribution Settings](/docs/reference/dashboards/widgets/cumulative-distribution-plot/cumulative-distribution-plot-settings/cumulative-distribution-settings)
- [Axes Settings](/docs/reference/dashboards/widgets/cumulative-distribution-plot/cumulative-distribution-plot-settings/axes-settings)
