title: Design Tab
summary: The Multi-Plot Design tab contains the layout settings for the active Multi-Plot chart.
markdown:
## Design Ribbon Context Tab

***

![Ribbon multiplot context tab layout group](/img/help/ribbon-multiplotcontexttablayoutgroup.png)![Ribbon multiplot context tab cell span group](/img/help/ribbon-multiplotcontexttabcellspangroup.png)

### Overview

The Multi-Plot Design tab contains the layout settings for the active [Multi-Plot](/docs/reference/chart-displays/multi-plot) chart.

### Access and Visibility

The Multi-Plot tab appears in the ribbon when a suitable [Multi-Plot](/docs/reference/chart-displays/multi-plot) is active.

The tab updates its content based on what you select.

### Main Functional Groups

The Multi-Plot ribbon tab is organized into several key groups:

#### Layout Group

The multi-plot layout can be configured to set a number of columns and rows of cells with the appropriate controls.

##### Reset All Spans

This will reset all spans defined in the columns and rows.

#### Cell Span Group

The settings within this group refer to a single cell of the multi-plot.

The current active cell is defined by the last cell clicked on by the user. This is shown with Cell (i, j), where i is the row index and j the column index.

Clicking the ![Red cross](/img/help/red-cross-16-n-p.png) button will clear the contents from the active cell.

A chart cell can be made wider or taller by having it span across a number of columns or rows with Column Span and Row Span. The active cell can expand into the left column by increasing the Column Span and expand into the lower row by increasing the Row Span. The use of the cells under any span is lost.

title: R-Axis Settings
summary: The Radar Plot R-Axis Settings provides options to customize the appearance and presentation of a Radar Plot Dashboard widget.
markdown:
## R-Axis Settings

***

###

### ![Radar plot settings r axis](/img/help/radarplotsettings-raxis.png)

###

### Overview

The Radar Plot R-Axis Settings provides options to customize the appearance and presentation of a Radar Plot Dashboard widget. These settings allow you to control the R-axis title, line, label and range elements.

Any changes are applied directly to the Radar Plot widget as they are made.

#### Accessing the Radar Plot Widget Settings

You can access the Radar Plot Settings through the widget interface:

1. Open the Dashboard you wish to customize
2. Double left-click on the Radar Plot widget within the Dashboard
3. Select R-Axis from the parent Axes node of the treeview in the Dashboard Settings dialog

### Available Settings Categories

The R-Axis Settings are organized into four main sections:

#### Axis Title

Control how the axis title appears on your graph:

- Title: Add or modify the text of the main title of your Axis

* Font: Customize font (size, style, colour) with the options available by clicking Select. A preview of the current font is shown with the "Preview" label.

#### Axis Line

Configure the appearance of the axis:

- Thickness: Set the thickness of the axes lines.

* Colour: Set the colour of the axes lines.

+ Location: Toggle the top/bottom or left/right location of the axis.

#### Axis Labels

Customize how value labels appear along the axis:

- Visible: Toggle the visibility of the axis labels.

* Angle: Set the angle of the axis labels either with the slider or by typing into or stepping through the text box.

+ Format: Set the format for the axis labels:
  - Normal: Decimal representation of the label values, e.g. 2,000 or 3,000,000
  - Abbreviate: Engineering notation representation of the label values, e.g. 2K or 3M
  - Scientific Notation: Scientific notation representation of the label values, e.g. 2x103 or 3x106
  - Date: Represent the axis values as dates (when applicable)

- Font: Customize font (size, style, colour) with the options available by clicking Select. A preview of the current font is shown with the "Preview" label.

* Location: Toggle between presenting the labels Inside or Outside of the Chart.

#### Range Values

This section provides options for the user to set the limits and the interval steps of the axis:

- Minimum: Sets the maximum value for the axis limit
- Maximum: Sets the minimum value for the axis limit
- Interval: Sets the major interval value between labels for the axis
- Minor Interval: Sets the minor interval value between labels for the axis
- Invert: Toggles the inversion of the axis limits
- Log: Toggles a log scale for the axis

Any changes to the Range Values can be reset by clicking ![Undo icon](/img/help/undo-icon.png)

title: Treeview Elements
summary: One of the main features of S3analyse is the user friendly way in which data is presented to the user.
markdown: ## Treeview Elements *** ### Overview One of the main features of S3analyse is the user friendly way in which data is presented to the user. The [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) gives a summary of the loaded data. The following sections detail how what is available from the data stored in this treeview. The selection options are context specific. The options for each context are: - [Project Folder](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements#Project) - [Case Filter](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements#CaseFilter) - [Cases](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements#Cases) - [Grid](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements#Grid) - [Init](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements#Init) - [Table](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements#Table) - [Summary](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements#Summary) - [RFT](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements#RFT) - [Solution](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements#Solution) - [Observed Data Files](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements#ObservedData) - [Calculated Data](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements#CalculatedData) - Calculations - Fluid In Place - Layer Analysis - Opportunity Index - Regions *** ### Element: Project Folder Each loaded case or multi-case will be collected into a [Project](/docs/reference/loading-data/projects) and any associated data will be contained within this Project Folder. The Project Folder node has controls for affecting the data set as a whole. From the Project Folder node: ![Create restart](/img/help/create-restart-16-n-p.png) Resample: Clicking this will launch the [Resample Settings](/docs/reference/managing-data/resampling). ![Select well list control](/img/help/selectwelllistcontrol.png) Select Well List: Any saved [Well Lists](/docs/reference/managing-data/well-lists) will be available for selection from this drop-down list. By default all the wells are included in the data set. ![Well list](/img/help/welllist-16-n-p.png) Open Well List Manager: Clicking this button will launch the [Well List Manager](/docs/reference/managing-data/well-lists). ![Well list filter](/img/help/welllistfilter-16-n-p.png) Apply Well List: Toggling this button will apply the currently selected [Well List](/docs/reference/managing-data/well-lists) to the data set. ##### Context Menu The context menu for the Project Folder is: ![Project view directory context menu](/img/help/projectviewdirectorycontextmenu.png) Open Containing Folder This will open Windows Explorer at the location of the loaded case for the chosen project. Add Observed Data… This will open a file browser to select one or more text files containing observed data to associate with this project. See [Text Files](/docs/reference/loading-data/supported-data-types/text-files) for the supported formats. Delete Project This will remove the project from S3analyse and any associated charts. *** ### Element: Case Filter When a project contains multiple cases the Case Filter is available in the Treeview. Filters can be applied to view only a selected subset of the loaded Cases. The default filter is "\*" which matches everything. If the filter definition fails to match at least one Case then no Cases are selected. ##### Filter Wildcards - “\*” matches all - “?” matches a single character - "\#" matches a single digit character Filter elements are separated by commas or semicolons. The filter is applied/removed by clicking the Toggle Filter ![Filter](/img/help/filter-16-n-p.png). Clicking the Advanced Filter Settings ![Settings](/img/help/settings-16-n-p.png) expands the [Project-Wide Filter](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/project-wide-filter) on the right of the window, allowing more detailed filter options to be applied. *** ### Element: Cases When a project contains multiple cases the Cases is available. It lists all the loaded Cases for this project, subject to [Case Filtering](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements#CaseFilter). The currently “Active” case is shown in parentheses on the parent Cases node. It is also indicated by bold highlighting in the expanded Cases list. By default, the first Case is the “Active” case. To select a different Active Case, expand the Cases branch and click the dot to the right of the required Case. Each Case has a context menu with Open Containing Folder. This will open Windows Explorer at the location of the loaded case for the chosen project. *** ### Element: Grid The Grid node lists the main grid, usually ROOT, and any Local Grid Refinements (LGRs) present in this model. Each treeview entry shows the grid dimensions. Double-clicking on a grid will produce a new [Grid Display](/docs/reference/grid-displays) of the default or first Solution property in the [Display Area](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/display-area). ##### Context Menu The context menu for the Grid node is: ![Project view grid context menu](/img/help/projectviewgridcontextmenu.png) View Grid This will create a [Gird Display](/docs/reference/grid-displays) of the first grid, usually the ROOT, with the default map property. View Grid Details This will present the [Grid Details](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-details) dialog. Export Eclipse EGRID This will output the loaded grid(s) as an Eclipse EGRID formatted file. Export Eclipse GRID This will output the loaded grid(s) as an Eclipse GRID formatted file. *** ### Element: Init The Init node contains initial map properties of the grid (e.g. porosity and permeabilities). Double-clicking on a Init property will produce a new [Grid Display](/docs/reference/grid-displays) of the property in the [Display Area](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/display-area) for the main grid. ##### Context Menu The context menu for an Init property is: ![Project view init property context menu](/img/help/projectviewinitpropertycontextmenu.png) Grid <gridname> with <property> This will create a [Gird Display](/docs/reference/grid-displays) of the grid gridname with the chosen INIT property. Histogram for <property> in <gridname> Grid This will create a [Histogram](/docs/reference/chart-displays/histograms) of the grid gridname with the chosen INIT property. The submenu presents the other available grids. Line Analysis for <property> in <gridname> Grid This will create a [Line Analysis](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-analysis) of the grid gridname with the chosen INIT property. The submenu presents the other available grids. Scatter Plot for <property> vs ... This will create a [Scatter Plot](/docs/reference/chart-displays/grid-scatter-plot) of the chosen INIT property. The submenu lists the other INIT properties to plot the chosen INIT property against. *** ### Element: Table The Table node contains Table data for the model (e.g PVT tables, Saturation tables, etc.). The table types are listed in the Table node. Each table type contains a list of the table indices. Double-clicking on a table index produces a [Table Data Chart](/docs/reference/chart-displays/table-data-charts) in the [Display Area](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/display-area) of the corresponding Table data corresponding chart. *** ### Element: Summary The Summary node contains Summary or Plot data for the model (e.g. Field data , Well data, etc.). The Summary data classes are list in the Summary node. Each class may contain sub-folders of members (e.g. wells) as appropriate. Further sub-folders are necessary for some classes (e.g. Completion data). Double-clicking on a Summary property will produce a new [Line Plot](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots) of the property against Time in the [Display Area](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/display-area). ##### Context Menu The context menu for a Summary property is: ![Project view summary property context menu](/img/help/projectviewsummarypropertycontextmenu.png) Plot <property> vs Time This will create a [Line Plot](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots) of the chosen property against the Time property. Plot <property> for all <members> This will create a single [Line Plot](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots) of the chosen property against Time for all members of the Summary Class, where appropriate, i.e. all wells, groups, etc. Plot <property> for Well List: <welllist> This will create a single [Line Plot](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots) of the chosen property against Time for all wells included in the [Well List](/docs/reference/managing-data/well-lists). This is only available for well properties. Plot <property> for all cases This will create a single [Line Plot](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots) of the chosen property against Time for all loaded cases. This is only available for multi-case models. Plot <property> for filtered cases This will create a single [Line Plot](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots) of the chosen property against Time for the [Filtered](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/project-wide-filter) cases. This is only available for multi-case models. Plot <property> vs ... This will create a [Line Plot](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots) of the chosen property against an appropriate property chosen from the submenu. *** ### Element: RFT The RFT node contains Repeat Formation Test (RFT) data and Production Logging Tool (PLT) data: well pressure and depth measurements recorded at specific timesteps. If a case has no RFT file of its own, an equivalent data set is derived automatically from the loaded Grid, Init and Solution data, so the RFT node is available even when no dedicated RFT file has been loaded. Data under the RFT node is arranged as Timestep > Well > Branch > property (e.g. PRESSURE, DEPTH). Wells with multiple laterals or perforated intervals present a separate Branch entry for each. Double-clicking a RFT property will open a new [RFT Plot](/docs/reference/chart-displays/rft-plots) in the [Display Area](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/display-area) showing a property-versus-depth chart alongside a data grid of the values. Context Menu The context menu for a RFT property is: ![Project view RFT property context menu](/img/help/projectviewrftpropertycontextmenu.png) Display RFT Chart for <property> This will create a [RFT Plot](/docs/reference/chart-displays/rft-plots) of the chosen RFT property. *** ### Element: Solution The Solution node contains dynamic map properties of the grid (e.g. Pressure, Oil Saturation, etc.). The Solution timesteps are listed in the Solution node. Each timestep contains its properties. Double-clicking on a Solution property will produce a new [Grid Display](/docs/reference/grid-displays) of the property in the [Display Area](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/display-area) for the main grid. ##### Context Menu The context menu for a Solution property is: ![Project view solution property context menu](/img/help/projectviewsolutionpropertycontextmenu.png) Grid <gridname> with <property> This will create a [Gird Display](/docs/reference/grid-displays) of the grid gridname with the chosen Solution property. Histogram for <property> in <gridname> Grid This will create a [Histogram](/docs/reference/chart-displays/histograms) of the grid gridname with the chosen Solution property. The submenu presents the other available grids. Line Analysis for <property> in <gridname> Grid This will create a [Line Analysis](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-analysis) of the grid gridname with the chosen Solution property. The submenu presents the other available grids. Scatter Plot for <property> vs ... This will create a [Scatter Plot](/docs/reference/chart-displays/grid-scatter-plot) of the chosen Solution property. The submenu lists the other Solution properties to plot the chosen Solution property against. *** ### Element: Observed Data Files The Observed Data Files node will list any loaded data files containing [Observed or History Data](/docs/reference/loading-data/observed-data). This node lists the loaded files. Within each file entry is a list of the properties, arranged as Summary or Solution as appropriate. *** ### Element: Calculated Data The Calculated Data node lists the available analysis tools for the selected project. This node contains the: - [Calculations](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/calculations): User defined calculations. - [Fluid In Place](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/fluid-in-place-calculations): Fluid in Place calculations for the model. - [Layer Analysis](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/layer-analysis): Layer Analysis of the grid. - [Opportunity Index](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/opportunity-index): Calculated Opportunity Index properties. - [Regions](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/regions): Defined regions of the map and grid. This includes [Threshold Regions](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-settings/threshold-regions) and Numeric Regions (PVT regions, etc.). #### Calculations Calculations allows new data properties to be derived from existing data. The newly created property is added to the treeview and can be used in the same way as any other property. A Calculation function could be used, for example, to find the ratio of gas to oil production or to find the difference between the production rates of two separate simulator runs. Double-clicking the Designs node brings up the [Calculations](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/calculations) dialog, where new calculations can be added. #### Fluid In Place The [Fluid In Place Calculations](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/fluid-in-place-calculations) are defined in the Fluid In Place node. This lists the Gas, Oil and Water In Place values at Surface Conditions for each simulation timestep, weighted by Pore Volume. The SUM value is the total In Place volume added across all cells in the region. The AVERAGE value is the SUM divided by the number of active cells in the region to give the average cell contribution. Double-clicking on a Fluid In Place property will produce a new [Line Plot](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots) of the property against Time in the [Display Area](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/display-area). #### Layer Analysis [Layer Analysis](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/layer-analysis) allows grid map data to be analysed either by summing or averaging data over layers. ![Layer analysis treeview element group](/img/help/layeranalysistreeviewelementgroup.png) From the Layer Analysis node: ![Add item](/img/help/add-item-16-n-p.png) Add Layer Analysis: This creates a new Layer Analysis that is added as a new Layer Analysis item to the bottom of the list. From the individual Layer Analyses nodes: ![Red cross](/img/help/red-cross-16-n-p.png) Delete Layer Analysis: This delete the Layer Analysis. ![Settings](/img/help/settings-16-n-p.png) Show Layer Analysis Settings: This presents the [Layer Analysis](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/layer-analysis) dialog, where you can select the required settings. The node is named with an index, 1 in the example above. The node also has a label that lists the layers that the analysis sums/averages, (1 - 14) or layers 1 to 14 in the above example. Each Layer Analysis contains a single-layer Grid node and corresponding Init and Solution nodes containing the summed or averaged properties. These are treated as Grid, Init and Solution Treeview Elements. #### Opportunity Index [Opportunity Index](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/opportunity-index) offers data properties output from a calculation of the Opportunity Index. ![Settings](/img/help/settings-16-n-p.png) Show Opportunity Index Settings: This launches the [Opportunity Index Settings](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/opportunity-index). The Opportunity Index contains data properties of the calculation for each Grid, [Layer Analysis](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/layer-analysis) and Solution Timestep, available to create a [Grid Display](/docs/reference/grid-displays/creating-grids) as normal. #### Regions - Threshold Regions [Threshold Regions](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-settings/threshold-regions) are defined subsets of the grid cells defined by a range of map cell values. ![Regions treeview element group](/img/help/regionstreeviewelementgroup.png) From the Threshold Regions node: ![Add item](/img/help/add-item-16-n-p.png) Add Threshold Regions: This creates a new [Threshold](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-settings/threshold-settings) that is added as a new Threshold Region item under the Threshold Regions node From the individual Threshold nodes: ![Red cross](/img/help/red-cross-16-n-p.png) Delete Threshold Region: This delete the Threshold. ![Settings](/img/help/settings-16-n-p.png) Show Threshold Region Settings: This presents the [Threshold Settings](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-settings/threshold-region-editor) dialog, where you can select the required settings. Double-clicking on a Threshold Region will produce a [Grid](/docs/reference/grid-displays) with the Threshold applied. #### Regions - Numeric Regions The numeric regions defined by the loaded data (e.g. PVT, Saturation or Fluid in Place regions) are available from the Numeric Regions node. Each Numeric Region node is labelled with its associated property definition and the number of different regions defined. Double-clicking on a Numeric Region node or property node will produce a [Grid](/docs/reference/grid-displays) of the numeric property. ##### Context Menu The context menu for a Numeric Region node or property node is: ![Project view regions context menu](/img/help/projectviewregionscontextmenu.png) Grid <gridname> with <property> This will create a [Gird Display](/docs/reference/grid-displays) of the grid gridname with the chosen numeric property. Create Threshold Region For Numeric Region property nodes, e.g. FIPNUM \#1, this will create a new [Threshold](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-features/thresholds) region of (FIPNUM = 1) and add it to the Threshold Region node, named "Threshold <property> \#<index>", e.g. "Threshold FIPNUM \#1". For Numeric Region nodes, e.g. FIPNUM, this will produce a dialog where property indices can be selected to create a new [Threshold](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-features/thresholds) Region. ![Project view region threshold selection dialog](/img/help/projectviewregionthresholdselectiondialog.png) Indices can be selected from the list of available values. Clicking OK will produce a new Threshold Region. Cancel will abort the operation. A new region will be added to the Threshold Region node, named "Threshold <property> \#<index list>", e.g. "Threshold FIPNUM \#1,3".

title: Data Table Section
summary: The Data Table Section of a text file contains one or more formatted tables of data.
markdown:
## Data Table Section

***

The Data Table Section of a text file contains one or more formatted tables of data. The data comprises column headers to identify property name and, optionally, units, associated well name, etc. followed by numerical data.

### Formatting Columns

Data should be formatted in a way to determine the individual columns of data and their associated column headers. The reader assumes a single column delimiter type on each line. It will automatically detect the delimiter in the following order of priority:

1. Tabs ("\t")
2. Commas (",")
3. Spaces (multiple spaces are treated as a single delimiter)

Note: Tables should be consistently formatted throughout and not mix delimiters. Any variation in formatting may lead to the data failing to load or being misinterpreted.

### Table Column Headers

The reader expects data to be organized in a specific sequence of table header lines followed by numeric data.

- Property Names (Mandatory): The first non-keyword line defines the names of the data columns (e.g., DATE, WOPRH, WWIRH). Simulator-style mnemonic names are suggested to aid interpretation and integration with simulation data.

* Units (Optional): If the next line contains valid unit symbols (e.g., SM3, SM3/DAY), it is treated as the units row.

+ Member Names (Optional): Subsequent non-numeric lines are treated as "Member" or "Sub-Member" identifiers (e.g., well names or completion/perforation names). Any properties without a member, such as a time or date property, should leave a blank space, separated by the delimiters. In this case delimiters cannot be used.

### Table Numerical Data

The numerical data follows the table column headers and should be tabulated with a consistent delimiter. Values should be entered for each property in every row of the table.

Comment lines can be added within the numerical data and these are ignored by the reader.

#### Example

This example has a [Header Section](/docs/reference/loading-data/supported-data-types/text-files/header-section) setting the Start Date. This is necessary as the TIME data is in Days and so needs a reference for the first date of the count.

Following the header are the Table Column headers starting with the Property Names line containing TIME and WBHP mnemonics. The next line details the units for each property and the final header line has the well name associated with the property. Note that TIME does not include a well name so a delimiter is necessary at the start if the line to indicate that no well name is defined for TIME.

STARTDATE 01/01/2000

TIME, WBHP, WBHP, WBHP, WBHP

DAYS, PSIA, PSIA, PSIA, PSIA

title: Observed Data
summary: Observed Data (also referred to as historical data) is real-world measured well or field data — production and injection rates, pressures, well tests, etc.
markdown:
## Observed Data Files

***

Observed Data (also referred to as historical data) is real-world measured well or field data — production and injection rates, pressures, well tests, etc. — that can be associated with a loaded project so it can be compared against simulated results.

Observed data may be included in a simulation data set, such as Eclipse properties with an H-suffix (WOPRH, etc.). Otherwise data can be loaded directly from separate files.

### Adding Observed Data

Observed Data is added to an existing project using the Add Observed Data… command on the Project Folder's context menu in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements#Project). This opens a file browser to select one or more files to associate with the project.

The only currently supported input format is [Text Files](/docs/reference/loading-data/supported-data-types/text-files).

### Where Observed Data Appears

Once loaded, Observed Data is listed under the Observed Data Files node in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements#ObservedData), alongside the simulated data for the project.

On charts, the Show Observed Data and Hide Repeated Observed Data options on the [Chart Data](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs/chart-tools/chart-data-tab) Ribbon tab control whether observed data is displayed and whether it is de-duplicated when shared across multiple plotted properties.

The Show Observed Data (New Plots) setting on the [Home](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/home-tab) Ribbon tab automatically overlays observed data as a scatter line whenever a matching simulated property is plotted (and vice versa), so new [Line Plots](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots) need no extra setup to include it.

### Comparing Observed and Simulated Data

Observed Data is most commonly used when the corresponding historic data is automatically added to a [Line Plot](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots) of the simulated data, as described above.

The other main purpose of Observed Data is history-matching quality control using [Mismatch Analysis](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/mismatches-analysis), which ranks cases by how closely their simulated results reproduce the historical data and highlights which wells or measurements are driving a poor match.

Mismatch Analysis does not distinguish between historical data loaded separately as Observed Data and historical data already bundled with the simulation results (for example Eclipse's H-suffixed summary mnemonics, such as WOPRH) — both are treated as historical vectors for comparison against the simulated results.

title: Chart View Tab
summary: The Chart Data tab contains the settings for the appearance of the active Line Plot.
markdown:
## Chart View Ribbon Context Tab

***

![Ribbon chart view context tab axes group](/img/help/ribbon-chartviewcontexttabaxesgroup.png)![Ribbon chart view context tab font group](/img/help/ribbon-chartviewcontexttabfontgroup.png)![Ribbon chart view context tab graph group](/img/help/ribbon-chartviewcontexttabgraphgroup.png)![Ribbon chart view context tab legend group](/img/help/ribbon-chartviewcontexttablegendgroup.png)![Ribbon chart view context tab legend limit group](/img/help/ribbon-chartviewcontexttablegendlimitgroup.png)![Ribbon chart view context tab line type group](/img/help/ribbon-chartviewcontexttablinetypegroup.png)![Ribbon chart view context tab graph zoom group](/img/help/ribbon-chartviewcontexttabgraphzoomgroup.png)

### Overview

The Chart Data tab contains the settings for the appearance of the active [Line Plot](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots). The majority of these settings are also available in [Line Plot Settings](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots/line-plot-settings).

### Access and Visibility

The Chart View tab appears in the ribbon when a suitable [Line Plot chart](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots) is active.

The tab updates its content based on what you select.

### Main Functional Groups

The Chart View ribbon tab is organized into several key groups:

#### Axes Group

##### Axis

Select the X or Y axis from the list with which to apply the axes setting to.

##### Width

Set the width for the selected axis.

##### Invert

Toggles the inversion of the axis.

#### Font Group

##### Area

Select the component of the chart from which to alter the font. Choose from chart Title, Legend or Axis from the list.

The Font and Size of the selection will be changed by the Font and Size controls

##### Font and Size

Select font and font size for the selected area.

#### Graph Group

##### Colours

From this dropdown select the colour of each component of the chart. This includes:

- Line
- Marker
- Axis Lines
- Axis Test
- Graph Background
- Plot Background

##### Major and Minor Grid Lines

Toggles the display of the Major and Minor grid lines

#### Legend Group

##### Show Legend

Toggles the display of the legend.

##### Orientation

Toggles between horizontal and vertical orientation of the legend.

##### Position Relative to Axes

Toggle the position of the legend to within or outside the axes boundary.

##### Horizontal Position

Select whether the legend is positioned on the Left or Right, and when in Horizontal Orientation, Stretch or Centre.

If Stretch, then the width of the Legend will be the width of the X-axis. Otherwise the width will be the width of the legend contents.

##### Vertical Position

Select whether the legend is positioned at the Top or Bottom of the axes.

#### Legend Limit Group

##### Limit Legend Items

Charts with multiple lines will produce an item in the legend for each line. This can create large and unwieldy legends as it fills to fit the space and position.

This setting toggles the application of the limit. When the limit is reached the legend is hidden.

##### Limit

This options sets the limit of the number of items in the legend before it is automatically hidden.

#### Line Type Group

##### Series

Select which data series line to view and alter its settings.

#####

##### Line Style

Select the line style for the chosen series.

The line styles can be Solid, Dash, Dot, Dash Dot and Dash Dot Dot.

##### Width

Select the width for the chosen series.

##### Plot Type

Select the plot type for the chosen series.

The types can be Line, Scatter and Line & Scatter.

##### Marker

Select the marker style for the chosen series.

##### Size

Select the marker size for the chosen series.

##### Remove Selected Line

Remove the selected series from the chart.

#### Graph Zoom Settings Group

This group manages the Zoom history for the chart.

If the chart has been zoomed, the previous Zoom settings are remembered, and the Zoom settings can be restored using the Zoom Settings.

Navigating the Zoom history is achieved with:

| ![Rewind to start](/img/help/rewindtostart-16.png) First | Restores first Zoom (original view) |
| --- | --- |
| ![Play previous](/img/help/playprevious-16.png) Previous | Restores the previous Zoom |
| ![Play next](/img/help/playnext-16.png) Next | Restores the Next Zoom in the zoom list |
| ![Play to end](/img/help/playtoend-16.png) Last | Restores the most Recent zoom |
| ![Blue refresh](/img/help/blue-refresh-16.png) Reset | Restores the default zoom and removes all the other Zoom settings |

title: Ensemble Summary Plot

markdown:
## Ensemble Plot

***

### Overview

The Ensemble Plot widget in S3analyse dashboards visualizes a single property across multiple cases within a [Project](/docs/reference/loading-data/projects). It in intended for use in such projects as Sensitivity Analyses.

The Average; Average +/- 1 standard deviation; P10 and P90; Minimum and Maximum are all drawn and reported on with mouse hover on the respective line.

### Creating a Ensemble Plot

To create a Ensemble Plot:

1. Select an active [Dashboard](/docs/reference/dashboards)
2. In the [Dashboard Design Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs/dashboard-tools/design-tab) select Ensemble Plot from the Panels group.

This will add a widget Tile to the end of the Dashboard sequence containing the default Ensemble Plot of the Final Field Oil Production Total against the Time for all cases in a multi-case model.

### Modifying a Ensemble Plot

The data used to define the plot and its appearance can be modified.

The settings are described in [Ensemble Summary Plot Settings](/docs/reference/dashboards/widgets/ensemble-summary-plot/ensemble-summary-plot-settings).

markdown:
## Multi-Case Projects

***

### Overview

Multi-Case Projects are used to collect data from multiple runs, such as a sensitivity analysis, into a single collection.

Multi-case Projects have additional analysis options over single case Projects.

### Multi-Case Projects and Data Loading

Projects are used to organise all loaded data into a single working session. Multiple cases can be loaded into a single project.

The [Create New Project](/docs/reference/loading-data/projects#Dialog) dialog can be used to select multiple cases when creating a new Project.

### Multi-Case Projects

Multi-Case Projects have additional options and features in:

- [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view): A Cases node is added to select the base case for a Project
- [Project-Wide Filter](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/project-wide-filter): Cases can be filtered from consideration in visualisation
- [Indexing](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots/indexing): Indexing for efficient navigation across cases
- [Broadcasting](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/window-view/broadcasting): Synchronise updates across charts when working with multiple cases
- [Dashboards](/docs/reference/dashboards): Dashboards can be used for ensemble visualisation
- [NPV Calculations](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/npv-calculations): NPV Tools for economic analysis across multiple cases

title: Grid Scatter Plot
summary: A Grid Scatter Plot displays individual data points on a two-dimensional plane, plotting one map data property along the horizontal axis and another on the vertical axis.
markdown:
## Grid Scatter Plot

***

### Overview

A Grid Scatter Plot displays individual data points on a two-dimensional plane, plotting one map data property along the horizontal axis and another on the vertical axis. It excels at revealing relationships, correlations, and clusters between properties. By examining the density and distribution of points, you can identify outliers, subgroups, and the strength of associations at a glance.

### Creating a Grid Scatter Plot

Grid Scatter Plot charts are limited to map properties (Solution or Init data). They can be created:

- Navigating to the appropriate map property in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view).
- Right-click the chosen property in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) and selecting Scatter Plot for <property> in <grid name> Grid.

The Grid Scatter Plot appearance can then be customised, such as titles, axes and colours.

#### Region Filtering

[Regions](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/regions) can be used to show per-region data. Selecting the type of Numeric Region from the Region Filtering group of the [Scatter Plot Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs/chart-tools/scatter-plot-tab) will create a data series for each set of cells of the same region index and present them all on the same chart.

### Example

![Scatter plot example](/img/help/scatterplotexample.png)

This example show a Scatter Plot of the Pressure against Pore Volume at the first Timestep, using a log-axis for the Pore Volume.

### Modifying Grid Scatter Plot

The appearance of Grid Scatter Plots can be changed as desired and the data used in the chart can also be changed.

#### Modifying the Grid Scatter Plot

Grid Scatter Plot have an extensive list of settings to customise the appearance. These are outlined in [Grid Scatter Plot Settings](/docs/reference/chart-displays/grid-scatter-plot/grid-scatter-plot-settings) and can be accessed by double left-clicking on the any part of the Grid Scatter Plot chart.

These are in complement to the [Scatter Plot Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs/chart-tools/scatter-plot-tab) that offers a selection of settings controlling the formulation and the data used in the chart.

#### Modifying the Data in the Grid Scatter Plot

Changing the data used to generate a Grid Scatter Plot is achieved with the X Property and Y Property Groups in the [Histogram Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs/chart-tools/histogram-tab). This allows the selection of any appropriate data from the Project to update the X or Y values respectively.

### Exporting Line Plots

Grid Scatter Plots can be exported with the [Report](/docs/reference/exporting-reports) Feature.

### Scripts and Line Plots

Grid Scatter Plots are supported by [Python Scripting](/docs/reference/python-scripting).

title: Creating Charts

markdown:
## Creating Charts

***

###

### Overview

In S3analyse, creating a chart is as simple as double clicking on a chosen data property in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) and the chart is presented in the [Display Area](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/display-area).

Different chart types are available for the various data types to help you visualise data quickly and effectively.

### Example

###

![Line plot example](/img/help/lineplotexample.png)

###

An example of a [Line Plot](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots) of Well Oil Production Rate (WOPR) from Well B1 plotted against Time.

###

### Creating Charts

There are two main methods of creating charts:

1. Double-clicking the chosen property from the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view). S3analyse with create the default chart for the chosen data type and present it in the [Display Area](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/display-area). Alternatively the property can be drag and dropped from the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) onto the [Display Area](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/display-area) to create a new chart. This process is also how data can be added to an existing chart.

1) Right-click on a chosen property in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) to view the menu which contains the possible chart types available. Clicking on one of these will produce the corresponding chart in the [Display Area](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/display-area).

### Chart Types

There are a number of chart types available in S3analyse. These include:

[Line Plots](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots) are a chart type that connects individual data points with straight lines to reveal trends and patterns over a continuous interval. Commonly used for time-series data, line plots highlight rates of change, seasonal fluctuations, and overall trajectories.

[Multi-Plots](/docs/reference/chart-displays/multi-plot) allow users to combine multiple charts into a single, unified display. This is useful for comparing trends across different cases, wells or properties in a compact and organized layout.

[Histograms](/docs/reference/chart-displays/histograms) display the distribution of a property by grouping values into contiguous bins and representing each bin’s frequency with a bar. Histograms are essential for understanding central tendency, variability, and outliers in large datasets.

[Line Analysis](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-analysis) charts are a method of viewing maps data of a single cell and how it changes when viewed from each of the cell's four dimensions; I, J, K and Time.

[Grid Scatter Plots](/docs/reference/chart-displays/grid-scatter-plot) display individual data points on a two-dimensional plane, plotting one map data property along the horizontal axis and another on the vertical axis. By examining the density and distribution of points, you can identify outliers, subgroups, and the strength of associations at a glance.

[Table Data Charts](/docs/reference/chart-displays/table-data-charts) display table data, such as PVT or saturation tables, as a chart and data table.

### Exporting Line Plots

Charts can be exported with the [Report](/docs/reference/exporting-reports) Feature.

### Scripts and Line Plots

Charts are supported by [Python Scripting](/docs/reference/python-scripting).

title: Broadcasting
summary: Broadcasting in S3analyse enables users to link multiple Line Plots so that they respond collectively to changes in data selection.
markdown:
## Broadcasting *** ### Overview Broadcasting in S3analyse enables users to link multiple [Line Plots](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots) so that they respond collectively to changes in data selection. This feature is particularly useful when comparing related properties across different views, such as production rates for the same well across multiple charts. Broadcasting allows [Line Plots](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots) to be collected into Groups. Grouped items will be linked so that when one of the charts has its source property changed the other charts in the group will similarly be updated. ### Key Features - Linked Updates: When a source property (e.g., a well or property) is changed in one chart, all other items in the broadcast Group automatically update to reflect the same change. - Multi-Plot Integration: Broadcasting can be applied to [Multi-Plot](/docs/reference/chart-displays/multi-plot) charts, allowing all embedded charts to update simultaneously when the source changes. - Efficient Comparison: Ideal for ensemble analysis, sensitivity studies, and well performance comparisons. ### How to Use Broadcasting Broadcasting is managed via the [Window View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/window-view) Toolbar. Selected [Line Plots](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots) in the Window View can be formed into a Group that will link them as Broadcast Group. The toolbar contains: |
  • New Group
| Add all selected windows to a new broadcast group | | --- | --- | |
  • Add to Group
| Add selected windows to an existing or broadcast group or create a new group | |
  • Clear Group
| Remove selected windows from broadcast groups | Once a number of charts have been selected in the Window View, click on ![Group16](/img/help/group16.png) New Group to create a Group. Charts that are included in the new Group will be indicated in the [Window View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/window-view) with a Group Number in the Group column. To add a chart to an existing group first select the item in the Window View and then clicking ![New group16](/img/help/newgroup16.png) Add to Group. A dialog will then be presented allowing the user to select which Group to add the chart to, or, alternatively create a new Group. A chart can be removed from a Group by selecting the chart in the Window View and clicking ![Clear group](/img/help/cleargroup.png) Clear Group. ### Effects of Broadcasting When any [Line Plots](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots) within a Group is updated via [Indexing](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots/indexing), principally the Replace option in the [Chart Data Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs/chart-tools/chart-data-tab), the corresponding effect is applied to data in the other charts in the Group. During Indexing, a particular meta-data is chosen to change, whether this is the Case, Well or Property Name. Indexing will then attempt to apply the meta-data change to all other data series found in the Grouped [Line Plots](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots). Case or Well (or other member option) indexing is designed to allow multiple properties for a single case or well to be updated quickly for all charts in the Group. Property Name changes are for examining a single property across multiple cases or wells. #### Example Use Case Suppose you have three Line Plots showing oil, water, and gas production rates for a specific well. If you change the well in one plot using the [Chart Data Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs/chart-tools/chart-data-tab), the other two plots will automatically update to show the same well data, ensuring synchronized analysis.

title: Window View
summary: S3analyse allows the user to manage the different display item windows that are generated in the Display Area from a single point.
markdown:
## Window View *** ### Overview S3analyse allows the user to manage the different display item windows that are generated in the [Display Area](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/display-area) from a single point. The Window View provides a list of every display item window created during a session and allows the user to easily manage, close, reopen and delete items from the list. ![Window view panel](/img/help/windowviewpanel.png) ### Features The Window View lists every display item window created in the current session, captioned with the name of the window and its type. By default, when a display item window is closed in S3analyse it is actually only closed to the Window View rather than deleted and lost. All the information to recreate the display item Window can be quickly retrieved if required. Each row has a check box in the first column of the row. Selecting the row using this checkbox makes it active to the functions in the toolbar at the top of list. Closing a display item window in the [Display Area](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/display-area) does not remove it from the Window View. Instead it is closed to the Window View list where it can be recalled or deleted. Double-clicking on an item in the list will bring it to the front of the display area or recreate it if it has been closed. #### Broadcasting [Broadcasting](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/window-view/broadcasting) is the ability to link multiple [Line Plots](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots) in the [Display Area](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/display-area) and update all of them with a single action. Grouped charts will be linked so that when one of the items has its source property changed the other items in the group will similarly be updated. For example, when the source well of a well oil rate [Line Plot](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots) is changed, via its [Chart Data Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs/chart-tools/chart-data-tab), to another well the other linked Line Plots in the group, say showing water and gas production rates, will also be updated to source their properties from this well. #### Window View Toolbar - Window Controls The Window View toolbar offers controls to manage the display items: #### |
  • Check All 
| Check all items in the list | | --- | --- | |
  • Uncheck All
| Uncheck all items in the list | |
  • Close
| Selected Windows are closed from the [Display Area](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/display-area) but are preserved in the Window View | |
  • Open
| Selected Windows are reopened into the [Display Area](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/display-area) | |
  • Delete
| Selected Windows are permanently closed and deleted | #### Window View Toolbar - Broadcast Controls The Window View toolbar offers controls to define [Broadcasting](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/window-view/broadcasting) groups: |
  • New Group
| Add all selected windows to a new broadcast group | | --- | --- | |
  • Add to Group
| Add selected windows to an existing or broadcast group or create a new group | |
  • Clear Group
| Remove selected windows from broadcast groups |

title: Load Dialog
summary: By default when an CMG file is loaded into S3analyse the data set is loaded and presented in the Project View with the default load options.
markdown:
## CMG Load Dialog

***

![Load dialog CMG default](/img/help/loaddialog-cmgdefault.png)

### Overview

By default when an CMG file is loaded into S3analyse the data set is loaded and presented in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) with the default load options. These default options can be changed for the system in the [CMG Load Settings](/docs/reference/general-settings/simulators/cmg).

Additionally, a load dialog can be shown to allow the user to tailor the load options for each CMG data set. From this the user can select what data types and what summary classes to load and then click OK to complete the load.

#### Accessing the CMG Load Dialog

The CMG Load DIalog is presented when attempting to load an CMG file and Use Load Dialog is checked in the [CMG Load Settings](/docs/reference/general-settings/simulators/cmg).

### Available Settings Categories

The CMG Load options are organized into three main sections:

#### Use Load Dialog

Selecting Use Load Dialog will cause this dialog to be presented during the load process for CMG data sets to allow the user to configure the load of each data set.

Checking/checking this options will only affect future loads and only if Save Settings & Load is also clicked.

#### Data Types To Load

Select which types of simulation data to load:

- Grid: Loads structured grid data for the model.
- Init: Loads the initialised map data.
- Tables: Loads tabular data such as PVT, Saturation Tables, etc.
- Summary: Loads the summary data.
- Solution: Loads the dynamic map data.

Selecting Select All will check all the data types.

#### Summary Data

Use this section to specify which data classes from the summary file should be loaded:

- FIELD: Field-wide data.
- GROUP: Well Group data.
- WELL: Well production/injection data.
- SECTOR: Sector-wide data.
- LAYER: Perforation data.
- SPHIST: History data.

Selecting Select All will check all the Summary data types.

#### Save Settings & Load

Saves current selection as a new default and starts data loading.

#### Load

Loads using current selections without applying the settings as a new default.

#### Cancel

Exits the dialog and cancel the load process.

title: Y-Axis Settings

markdown:
## Y-Axis Settings

***

###

### ![Pearson coefficient settings y axis](/img/help/pearsoncoefficientsettings-yaxis.png)

###

### Overview

The Pearson Coefficient Y-Axis Settings provides options to customize the appearance and presentation of a Pearson Coefficient Dashboard widget. These settings allow you to control the Y-axis title, line, label and range elements.

Any changes are applied directly to the Pearson Coefficient widget as they are made.

#### Accessing the Pearson Coefficient Widget Settings

You can access the Pearson Coefficient Settings through the widget interface:

1. Open the Dashboard you wish to customize
2. Double left-click on the Pearson Coefficient widget within the Dashboard
3. Select Y-Axis from the parent Axes node of the treeview in the Dashboard Settings dialog

### Available Settings Categories

The Y-Axis Settings are organized into four main sections:

#### Axis Title

Control how the axis title appears on your graph:

- Title: Add or modify the text of the main title of your Axis

* Font: Customize font (size, style, colour) with the options available by clicking Select. A preview of the current font is shown with the "Preview" label.

#### Axis Line

Configure the appearance of the axis:

- Thickness: Set the thickness of the axes lines.

* Colour: Set the colour of the axes lines.

+ Location: Toggle the top/bottom or left/right location of the axis.

#### Axis Labels

Customize how value labels appear along the axis:

- Visible: Toggle the visibility of the axis labels.

* Angle: Set the angle of the axis labels either with the slider or by typing into or stepping through the text box.

+ Format: Set the format for the axis labels:
  - Normal: Decimal representation of the label values, e.g. 2,000 or 3,000,000
  - Abbreviate: Engineering notation representation of the label values, e.g. 2K or 3M
  - Scientific Notation: Scientific notation representation of the label values, e.g. 2x103 or 3x106
  - Date: Represent the axis values as dates (when applicable)

- Font: Customize font (size, style, colour) with the options available by clicking Select. A preview of the current font is shown with the "Preview" label.

* Location: Toggle between presenting the labels Inside or Outside of the Chart.

#### Range Values

This section provides options for the user to set the limits and the interval steps of the axis:

- Minimum: Sets the maximum value for the axis limit
- Maximum: Sets the minimum value for the axis limit
- Interval: Sets the major interval value between labels for the axis
- Minor Interval: Sets the minor interval value between labels for the axis
- Invert: Toggles the inversion of the axis limits
- Log: Toggles a log scale for the axis

Any changes to the Range Values can be reset by clicking ![Undo icon](/img/help/undo-icon.png)

## General Settings

***

![Main settings general](/img/help/mainsettings-general.png)

### Overview

The General Settings provides options to handle how S3analyse starts and ends and how data file paths in Projects are stored.

#### Accessing the General Settings

The General Settings dialog can be accesses in two ways; either click the Settings cog ![Options icon](/img/help/options-icon.png) icon in the Quick Access Toolbar or selecting Settings in the File menu. From this select General in the treeview.

### General Settings

The available settings are:

#### On startup load the most recent file

This setting, when checked, will automatically load the file at the top of the MRU (Most Recently Used) List in the File menu.

#### File Path type in Projects

The file paths referencing files can either be stored as Absolute or Relative.

Data file paths associated with a Project are internally referenced by the Project. For static data a Absolute path is recommended. If data files and Projects are to be portable then it will be necessary to reference them with Relative paths. In this case the paths will be stored as relative to the Project file.

#### Ask to exit software

Display a confirmation dialog when attempting to exit the software if data has been loaded.

This button resets the window / dialog locations to their defaults. This is intended to assist when switching between different monitor configurations and windows / dialogs may be appearing on screens that are no longer connected.

This button resets all saved pane and window layouts back to their default arrangement.

#### ![New item25](/img/help/newitem25.png) Reset All to Default

Applies any changes to the load selections without applying the settings as a new default.

Exits the settings and cancel any changes.

title: Grid visualisation
summary: Interactive 3D and 2D reservoir grids with wells, regions and timestep playback.
markdown: Reservoir grids render on the GPU resulting in fast 3D, 2D and single-layer renderings. Visualise multi-million cell models with no time lag. The demo above shows the Cell Lines page of the Grid Editors window: cell faces, wireframe, and active/inactive cell colours. The product additionally offers axis settings, clipping planes, lighting and transparency, ternary display, threshold filtering, scale factor, viewing angles and well markers — deferred for now, see [3D grid displays](/docs/reference) for the full set. ## Display controls - **Cell display** — active cells, inactive cells, local grid refinements - **Appearance** — cell faces, wireframe, lighting and transparency - **Views** — 2D, full 3D, or a single layer - **Axes** — flip X, Y or Z independently - **Scaling** — true scale, square, fit to window, or an arbitrary vertical exaggeration - **Dual porosity** — matrix, fracture, or both ## Wells Well trajectories can be drawn on the grid with labels, perforations, and markers above the reservoir so wells stay visible from any viewing angle. ## Colouring and legends Any grid property can be coloured by a selected scheme, with the legend shown on the view and limits taken from the data, the selected timesteps, or values you set yourself. Schemes can be inverted. ## Ternary saturation display Three-phase saturations can be displayed as a ternary blend, so oil, water and gas distribution is visible in a single view rather than three separate property plots. ## Timestep playback Solution properties animate through time with configurable start and end dates, playback delay, reverse and repeat, plus step controls for first, previous, next and last timestep.

S3analyse supports the VDB database format used by the Nexus and VIP simulators, enabling users to load and analyse simulation results with minimal setup.

title: Show Data In A Table
summary: The Vector Table displays data from the project as a spreadsheet-style grid, one column per vector, with filtering to narrow down which vectors are shown, and optional statistical values per column.
markdown:
## Show Data in a Table

***

###

### Overview

The Vector Table displays data from the project as a spreadsheet-style grid, one column per vector, with filtering to narrow down which vectors are shown, and optional statistical values per column.

#### Accessing the Table

Right-click a data type folder, such as [Summary](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements#Summary) or [Solution](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements#Solution), in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) and select Display <data type> Vector Table for <case name>. This opens a Vector Table tab in the [Display Area](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/display-area) for the chosen Project.

![Vector table display](/img/help/vectortabledisplay.png)

### Vector Tables

Once selected the data is presented in a Vector Table of data and a set of filter options.

#### Available Columns

The available data is presented in columns, headed by their metadata, such as Case, Member (well/group name) and Vector Name, with Units shown where available. Column widths adjust automatically to the available space.

#### Filtering Data

The panel on the right narrows the table by metadata appropriate to the data type, such as Class, Member, Timestep, Name, etc. Checking/unchecking an item updates the table to match. e.g. checking a single well name under Member restricts the table to that well's data.

Filters combine so checking values in more than one section (e.g. a Class and a Name) narrows the results further, since all active filters apply simultaneously.

#### Statistical Values

Click the Σ (sigma) symbol for any column header, check the required values (Average, Count, Maximum, Minimum and Sum), and confirm with the green check-mark. The chosen statistical summary values appear at the foot of that column in a separate row.

#### Data Navigation

Only one page-width of data is presented at a time. The controls at the bottom of the table page through the columns and show the current column / total row count.

title: Grid Property Plot
summary: The Grid Property Plot widget in S3analyse dashboards visualizes the distribution of values of a single map property for multiple cases within a Project.
markdown:
## Grid Property Plot

***

### Overview

The Grid Property Plot widget in S3analyse dashboards visualizes the distribution of values of a single map property for multiple cases within a [Project](/docs/reference/loading-data/projects). It in intended for use in such projects as Sensitivity Analyses.

Each case shows a vertical arrangement of:

- Marker at the Average value
- Bounded box around the marker indicates Average +/- 1 standard deviation
- Thin line shows the extent of the Maximum and Minimum values

Hovering the mouse over the marker shows the Case index, Maximum, Average and Minimum.

### Creating a Grid Property Plot

To create a Grid Property Plot:

1. Select an active [Dashboard](/docs/reference/dashboards)
2. In the [Dashboard Design Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs/dashboard-tools/design-tab) select Grid Property Plot from the Panels group.

This will add a widget Tile to the end of the Dashboard sequence containing the default Grid Property Plot of the POROSITY for all cases in a multi-case model.

### Modifying a Grid Property Plot

The data used to define the plot and its appearance can be modified.

The settings are described in [Grid Property Plot Settings](/docs/reference/dashboards/widgets/grid-property-plot/grid-property-plot-settings).

title: Analysis Tools
summary: S3analyse provides a suite of powerful analysis tools designed to enhance reservoir simulation post-processing.
markdown:
## Analysis Tools

***

### Overview

S3analyse provides a suite of powerful analysis tools designed to enhance reservoir simulation post-processing. These tools allow users to derive new insights, perform custom calculations, and extract meaningful metrics from complex simulation data.

The main Analysis Tools include:

#### Calculations

[Calculations](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/calculations) allow the creation of new vector properties using custom formulas based on existing data. Calculations can be applied across multiple cases, wells, or timesteps, and support a wide range of mathematical functions including sums, averages, and conditional logic. Calculated vectors are integrated into the Project View and can be used in plots and dashboards.

#### Layer Analysis

[Layer Analysis](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/layer-analysis) will Summarize or average grid data across layers to produce single-layer representations. This is particularly useful for visualizing vertical trends or aggregating properties like porosity or saturation. Layer Analysis supports pore volume weighting and flexible layer selection.

#### Regions

[Regions](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/regions) will define and manage spatial subsets of the grid using:

- Threshold Regions: Based on value ranges of grid properties.
- Numeric Regions: Derived from simulation inputs such as PVT or saturation regions.

These regions can be used for filtering, plotting, and targeted analysis.

#### Fluid In Place Calculations

[Fluid In Place Calculations](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/fluid-in-place-calculations) will automatically compute in-place volumes (oil, gas, water) at surface conditions for each timestep. Results are weighted by pore volume and presented as SUM and AVERAGE values, which can be plotted over time.

#### NPV Calculations

[NPV Calculations](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/npv-calculations) will perform Net Present Value analysis on a case/cases. An interactive chart is presented where income and costs can be input and the results presented in a chart.

#### Mismatch Analysis

[Mismatch Analysis](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/mismatches-analysis) compares simulated results against the observed (historical) data loaded with a case. The analysis is presented as an interactive dashboard listing the cases ranked by their fit to the historical data and charts showing the comparison between simulated and observed properties.

#### Case Comparison

[Case Comparison](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/case-comparison) gives an interactive dashboard comprising a side-by-side numerical and graphical comparison of the results from any two loaded cases.

title: Line Analysis Tab
summary: Line Analysis charts are a method of viewing maps data of a single cell and how it changes when viewed from each of the cell's four dimensions.
markdown:
## Line Analysis Ribbon Context Tab

***

![Ribbon line analysis context tab selected cell group](/img/help/ribbon-lineanalysiscontexttabselectedcellgroup.png)![Ribbon line analysis context tab selected vector group](/img/help/ribbon-lineanalysiscontexttabselectedvectorgroup.png)![Ribbon line analysis context tab region axis settings group](/img/help/ribbon-lineanalysiscontexttabregionaxissettingsgroup.png)

### Overview

[Line Analysis](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-analysis) charts are a method of viewing maps data of a single cell and how it changes when viewed from each of the cell's four dimensions.

Ribbon controls are provided to change the selected cell the plot is based around, the vector and time step.

### Access and Visibility

The Line Analysis context tab appears in the ribbon when a suitable [Line Analysis](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-analysis) chart is active.

The tab updates its content based on what you select.

### Main Functional Groups

The Line Analysis ribbon tab is organized into three groups to select the chosen cell, property and the axis styles.

#### Selected Cell Group

The selected cell to base the Line Analysis around can be set from the three controls. Selecting the I-, J- or K-index will update the Line Analysis plot as appropriate.

#### Selected Property Group

The selected property to base the Line Analysis on can be set from the [Selected Property](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/common-ribbon-controls/selected-property-ribbon-group) controls.

#### Axis Settings Group

The X-axis style can be defined for each Line Analysis plot.

For I, J and K plots the X-axis Axis Style is set to Index by default. This plots the chosen vector against the cell index. Alternatively it can be set to Value to plot the vector against the cell coordinate. This produces a set of plots for X, Y and Z.

For the Time plot the X-axis Time Axis Style is set to Date by default. This plots the chosen vector against the timestep date. If set to Index then timestep index is used and if set to Value then the Number of Days is used.

##### Interpolate Inactives

When checked, this options will connect across any gaps in the line where data points might be missing due to the presence of inactive cells.

title: Fluid In Place Calculations
summary: The Fluid In Place Calculations define the Gas, Oil and Water In Place values at Surface Conditions for each simulation timestep, weighted by Pore Volume.
markdown:
## Fluid In Place Calculations

***

###

### Overview

The Fluid In Place Calculations define the Gas, Oil and Water In Place values at Surface Conditions for each simulation timestep, weighted by Pore Volume. The calculations are available in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements#CalculatedData).

The SUM value is the total In Place volume added across all cells in the region. The AVERAGE value is the SUM divided by the number of active cells in the region to give the average cell contribution.

Double-clicking on a Fluid In Place property will produce a new [Line Plot](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots) of the property against Time in the [Display Area](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/display-area).

title: NPV Calculations
summary: S3analyse can take a simulation case, or an ensemble of cases, and calculate the Net Present Value (NPV) of the field, or of alternative field development plans, by using the (simulated) production...
markdown:
## NPV Calculations

***

### Overview

S3analyse can take a simulation case, or an ensemble of cases, and calculate the Net Present Value (NPV) of the field, or of alternative field development plans, by using the (simulated) production data to determine future revenues and costs.

There are two forms of NPV analysis available; the Single Case analysis and the Ensemble analysis. The Single Case analysis shows the NPV for the simulation run and the breakdown of the income and costs. The Ensemble analysis shows the NPV for the cases within the [Project](/docs/reference/loading-data/projects).

#### Accessing the Calculations

The NPV Calculations can be accessed from the [Home Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/home-tab).

### NPV Calculation Analysis

The NPV calculation takes a range of user inputs for costs and income to determine the profitability of a simulation prediction over time.

The analysis is presented in a dialog where the user inputs are listed and the resulting analysis presented in a chart:

![NPV single case](/img/help/npvsinglecase.png)

The NPV calculation incorporates the following inputs:

#### Revenue Streams

- Oil Production Income
- Gas Production Income

#### Production Costs

- Oil Production Cost
- Gas Production Cost
- Water Production Cost
- Polymer Production Cost

#### Injection Costs

- Water Injection Cost
- Polymer Injection Cost

#### Financial Elements:

- Discount, time value of money adjustment
- Royalties
- CAPEX (Capital Expenditure)
- OPEX (Operating Expenditure)
- ABEX (Abandonment Expenditure)
- Tax

The user should assign each component with an estimated value to apply to the calculation.

#### Display Options

There are a number of options for the displayed data in the chart:

- Abandon at Peak NPV: Automatically calculate optimal abandonment timing
- Show Abandonment Costs at Start: Display ABEX costs at the beginning of the timeline rather than the end
- Show Component Lines: Display individual cost and revenue components
- Accumulate Component Costs: Show cumulative values for cost components
- Show Annual Values: Display data on an annual basis

#### Chart Types

Choose from three chart formats:

- Lines: Continuous line chart showing NPV trends.
- Split Columns: Unstacked column chart displaying components separately.
- Stacked Columns: Stacked column chart showing cumulative components. This is the default option.

### Single Case NPV Analysis

The Single Case analysis shows the Total NPV trajectory line on the chart and the annual breakdown of the Component Contributions shown as stacked bars or separate lines.

For [Multi-Case Projects](/docs/reference/loading-data/projects/multi-case-projects) the case under analysis can be selected or changed from the [NPV Settings Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs/npv-tools/npv-settings-tab).

### Ensemble NPV Analysis

The Ensemble Case analysis is limited to showing the Total NPV line for each case in the [Project](/docs/reference/loading-data/projects).

The chart displays NPV curves for all cases simultaneously, revealing:

- Range of outcomes: The spread in NPV values across different realizations
- Peak NPV variation: Differences in maximum profitability (e.g., $5-9 billion range)
- Timing variation: Differences in when peak NPV occurs (e.g., 3-year spread)
- Uncertainty quantification: Visual representation of subsurface and operational uncertainty

Single case analysis can performed on any individual case from the ensemble to examine the breakdown of incomes and costs.

title: Loading Data
summary: S3analyse is designed to support a wide range of industry-standard data formats, making it suitable for workflows across multiple reservoir simulators.
markdown:
## Loading Data

***

###

### Overview

S3analyse is designed to support a wide range of industry-standard data formats, making it suitable for workflows across multiple reservoir simulators.

It is particularly well-suited for loading and comparing multiple runs of a base case, allowing users to analyse sensitivities, history matches, and scenario variations with ease.

This capability is ideal for iterative modelling, uncertainty analysis, and performance benchmarking.

Once loaded, data files are organised into [Projects](/docs/reference/loading-data/projects) in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view), providing a clear and structured interface for navigating simulation results.

Each project can contain one or more runs, and users can switch between cases, compare outputs, and visualise trends across time steps.

A full list of supported file formats is available in [Supported Data Types](/docs/reference/loading-data/supported-data-types), covering Eclipse, Nexus, CMG, tNavigator, UTCHEM, Meteor, and more.

### Scripts and Loading Data

To streamline data loading and automate repetitive tasks, S3analyse supports [Python Scripting](/docs/reference/python-scripting).

Users can write scripts to batch-load simulation runs, apply filters, generate plots, or export results.

Scripting is especially useful for large-scale sensitivity studies or when integrating with external modelling workflows.

Whether working interactively or in batch mode, Python support ensures flexibility and control over the data loading process.

title: Adding and Removing Lines
summary: In S3analyse, Line Plots are dynamic and flexible visualizations that can be expanded or refined by adding or removing data series.
markdown:
## Adding and Removing Lines

***

### Overview

In S3analyse, [Line Plots](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots) are dynamic and flexible visualizations that can be expanded or refined by adding or removing data series. This allows users to compare multiple properties, wells, or cases within a single chart, or to streamline the chart for clarity.

### Adding Lines to a Line Plot

Additional data lines can added to an existing Line Plot chart using either of two methods:

- Drag and Drop

Left-Click and drag a property from the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) and drop it onto an existing Line Plot in the [Display Area](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/display-area). This will offer control of what axes are used to represent the new data.

- Indexing Append

Use the Append option in the [Chart Data Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs/chart-tools/chart-data-tab) to add a new line based on the next [Indexed](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots/indexing) item, e.g., next well or case. This will always attempt to reuse the same axis.

#### Sharing Axis

When adding a line to a Line Plot with the Drag and Drop method S3analyse offers options on how to create a corresponding axis for the data. It is possible to reuse the existing axis of created a new axis. This is outlined in [Shared Axis](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots/adding-and-removing-lines/shared-axis).

### Removing Lines from a Line Plot

Lines can be removed from a Line Plot via the [Line Plot Settings](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots/line-plot-settings). The treeview in the dialog lists the presented data series/properties under the Data Series node. Any of these series may be removed from the Line Plot by clicking on the ![Red cross](/img/help/red-cross-16-n-p.png).

### Customizing Added Lines

Each added line can be individually customized with such settings as:

- Line Style: Solid, dashed, dotted, etc.
- Colour and width
- Marker type and size
- Line Type: Line, Scatter or Line & Scatter

These settings are accessible via the [Chart View Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs/chart-tools/chart-view-tab) and [Line Chart Settings](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots/line-plot-settings).

#### Best Practices

- Use consistent colours or markers for related data series.
- Limit the number of lines to avoid clutter; use the Legend Limit setting if needed.
- Consider using Multi-Plot or Dashboard layouts for large comparisons.
