title: Layer Analysis
summary: Layer Analysis lets you collapse a range of grid layers into a single value per column.
markdown:
## Layer Analysis

***

### Overview

[Layer Analysis](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/layer-analysis) lets you collapse a range of grid layers into a single value per column. For each I, J column of cells, it sums or averages the Init and Solution property values over a chosen range of Z-layers, producing a new single-layer grid you can view and compare like any other grid or map in the project.

An example of Layer Analysis of Oil Thickness showing the densities of oil across the reservoir.

![Layer analysis example](/img/help/layeranalysisexample.png)

#### Accessing Layer Analysis

The Layer Analysis is present in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) under the [Calculated Data](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements#CalculatedData) node. The analysis data set can be used to [create Grid Displays](/docs/reference/grid-displays/creating-grids) in the standard fashion.

You can add or modify the Layer Analysis from the settings found through the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) treeview:

1. Open the Project View and locate the [Calculated Data node](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements#CalculatedData)
2. Click ![Add item](/img/help/add-item-16-n-p.png) Add Layer Analysis for the top Layer Analysis node to create a new analysis
3. Click ![Settings](/img/help/settings-16-n-p.png) Show Layer Analysis Settings on the new Layer Analysis node to access the [settings](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/layer-analysis)

### What Layer Analysis Does

Layer Analysis reduces the chosen Layers range for each column into a single value, using either the Sum or Average across those layers. The calculation is weighted by Pore Volume by default, giving a volume-weighted result rather than treating every cell equally regardless of size.

The result is stored as its own single-layer grid, with corresponding Init and Solution properties, that can be dragged onto the [Display Area](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/display-area) just like the original data.

### Why Use Layer Analysis

- Collapse a multi-layer reservoir model into a single 2D map to see field-wide totals or averages of a property, such as total pore volume-weighted saturation or oil in place.
- Compare reservoir quality, such as porosity or permeability, between zones without paging through Z-layers one at a time.
- Sum or average over a specific interval, such as a single producing zone or formation, by narrowing the Layers range rather than using the whole column.
- Use Pore Volume Weighting to get a physically meaningful volume-weighted average rather than a simple cell-count average.
- Keep several Layer Analyses side by side, each with its own layer range or analysis type, to compare zones or intervals across the field.

### How to Use Layer Analysis

The operation of this feature is details in [Layer Analysis](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/layer-analysis).

markdown:
## Eclipse Load Dialog

***

![Load dialog eclipse default](/img/help/loaddialog-eclipsedefault.png)

### Overview

By default when an Eclipse file is loaded into S3analyse the data set is loaded and presented in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) with the default load options. These default options can be changed for the system in the [Eclipse Load Settings](/docs/reference/general-settings/simulators/eclipse).

Additionally, a load dialog can be shown to allow the user to tailor the load options for each Eclipse data set. From this the user can select what data types and what summary classes to load and then click OK to complete the load.

#### Accessing the Eclipse Load Dialog

The Eclipse Load DIalog is presented when attempting to load an Eclipse file and Use Load Dialog is checked in the [Eclipse Load Settings](/docs/reference/general-settings/simulators/eclipse).

### Available Settings Categories

The Eclipse Load options are organized into three main sections:

#### Use Load Dialog

Selecting Use Load Dialog will cause this dialog to be presented during the load process for Eclipse data sets to allow the user to configure the load of each data set.

Checking/checking this options will only affect future loads and only if Save Settings & Load is also clicked.

#### Data Types To Load

Select which types of simulation data to load:

- Grid: Loads structured grid data for the model.
- Init: Loads the initialised map data.
- Tables: Loads tabular data such as PVT, Saturation Tables, etc.

* - Load VFP Table Data: Load Vertical Flow Performance (VFP) lift curve table data.

+ Summary: Loads the summary data.

- - Prefer H5 File: Select to prioritize .H5 formats (default: unchecked).

* Solution: Loads the dynamic map data.
* RFT: Includes Repeat Formation Test (RFT) data.

+ - Create RFT: Select to extract the grid property values from the well completion locations to create RFT data.

- Group Hierarchy: Loads the well-group tree structure defined in the model.

Selecting Select All will check all the data types.

#### Summary Data

Use this section to specify which data classes from the summary file should be loaded:

- AQUIFERS: Aquifer performance and influence.
- BLOCKS: Fundamental grid blocks used in simulation.
- COMPLETIONS: Completion-level breakdown per well.
- EDGES: Structural connections or grid boundaries.
- FIELD: Field-wide aggregate results.
- GROUPS: Grouped performance across wells or fields.
- NODES: Key control points or reference markers.
- PIPES: Pipe flow and network structures.
- REGIONS: Spatial region data for segmented analysis.
- SEGMENTS: Pipeline or flow segments within the simulation.
- WELLS: Individual well production/injection data.

Selecting Select All will check all the Summary data types.

#### HPG Settings

The option to create and use the [HPG](/docs/reference/loading-data/hpg-files) data for the chosen data file(s) is available.

#### Name

The origin/case name of the data set can be defined with this text box. All data loaded in this action will be contains in a case of the specified name. If left default the case is named based on the file name.

#### Save Settings & Load

Saves current selection as a new default and starts data loading.

#### Load

Loads using current selections without applying the settings as a new default.

#### Cancel

Exits the dialog and cancel the load process.

### Access and Visibility

### Main Functional Groups

The Grid Data ribbon tab is organized into several key groups:

#### Selected Property Group

#### Data Limits and Legend Group

##### Scheme

Select from the list of available legend colour schemes.

##### Ternary Mode

### Overview

The data and its point of interest that define the chart are available to set for each widget chart type. These settings shown when the mouse cursor is hovering over the Cross Plot. They allow the selection of a property or setting to update the chart.

### Cross Plot Data Settings

title: Case Comparison
summary: Case Comparison gives an interactive dashboard comprising a side-by-side numerical and graphical comparison of the results from any two loaded cases.
markdown:
## Case Comparison

***

###

### Overview

Case Comparison gives an interactive dashboard comprising a side-by-side numerical and graphical comparison of the results from any two loaded cases. It is the general-purpose counterpart to [Mismatch Analysis](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/mismatches-analysis). Rather than checking a simulation against historical measurements, it checks one simulation against another. Typical uses include quantifying the impact of a single model change, sanity-checking a re-run against a previous version, or comparing two alternative development scenarios.

For every vector shared by both cases, S3analyse calculates the difference between them, summarises it in a set of tables, and lets you inspect the full time-series comparison on a chart.

#### Accessing Case Comparison

Case Comparison is accessed from the View Actions group of the [Home Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/home-tab). The current project must contain at least two cases; the tool initially compares the first two loaded.

![Output comparison example](/img/help/outputcomparisonexample.png)

### Settings

#### Choosing the Cases

The Settings panel has two case selectors where the cases for comparison can be selected.

Note: Every difference in the tool is reported as Model 1 minus Model 2 (or Model 1 relative to Model 2, as a percentage), so it's worth being consistent about which case is treated as the baseline.

#### Display Settings

The difference between the cases can be presented as an absolute value (Model 1 minus Model 2) or a percentage (or Model 1 relative to Model 2) in the Comparison Tables and the Comparison Chart. This is selected from the Table Difference Type and the Chart Difference Type respectively.

Any selected data properties that have no differenced between the cases can be suppressed from the Comparison Table by checking Hide Columns With No Differences.

#### Choosing Properties for Comparison

Below the case selectors, three checkbox groups narrow down what's included in the comparison table:

- Classes: The Summary data classes common to both cases (e.g. FIELD, WELLS, GROUPS).
- Members: The individual wells/groups common to both cases.
- Names: The property names common to both cases (e.g. FOPR, WWCT, GGPT) — each with its own Point of Interest dropdown.

Each panel has a "select all" checkbox in its header. Only items present in both cases are ever listed, so the comparison never breaks on a mismatched property.

#### Point of Interest

Because each property is a full time series, a single representative value has to be picked before it can appear in a comparison table. This is the Point of Interest, and it can be First, Last, Minimum, Maximum, Average, Sum, or RMS. S3analyse chooses a sensible default automatically depending on the vector type; cumulative vectors compare their Last value, in-place vectors their First value, delta/interval vectors are Summed. This can be overridden per vector in the Names panel if a different summary is more meaningful.

####

### Comparison Tables

The central Comparison Tables panel shows one table per Class, with a row per Member and a column per selected property Name. Each cell shows the difference between the two cases at that vector's Point of Interest, coloured green for an increase and red for a decrease (Model 1 relative to Model 2) so the biggest changes stand out immediately. The Table Difference Type setting switches every cell between a percentage change and an absolute change, and Hide Columns With No Differences removes any vector that came out identical in both cases. This is useful for finding exactly what a model change actually affected.

### Comparison Charts

Clicking any cell in a Comparison Tables plots that property on the Comparison Charts panel: the Comparison Chart overlays the full time series from both cases, and the Comparison Residual Chart below it plots the difference between them over time (as a percentage or absolute value, set independently via Chart Difference Type). Together these show not just how much a result changed, but when and how. This can be examined for a one-off step change, a growing trend, or just noise.

### Typical Workflow

A typical workflow might be:

1. Load the two cases to be compared into the Project, for example, a base case and a case with a single model change applied.
2. Click Show Case Comparison ribbon button and confirm the Model 1/Model 2 case selectors are set the way round you want the differences reported.
3. Scan the Comparison Tables for the most strongly coloured cells to see which wells/vectors were most affected by the change.
4. Override the Point of Interest for a property if its default summary value (e.g. Average) isn't the most meaningful way to judge the change for that measurement.
5. Click through to the Comparison Chart and Residual Chart for the property of interest to see the full shape of the change over time, not just its magnitude at one point.

title: Analysis and economics
summary: History matching, case comparison, calculations, NPV and opportunity index.
markdown:
Beyond plotting, S3analyse quantifies how runs differ from each other and from observed
data, and puts an economic value on the result.

## History matching and mismatch

Simulated results can be compared against observed or historic data, with mismatch analysis
highlighting where a case departs from measurement. Quality factors score and rank cases so
the best match across a study is identifiable rather than a matter of judgement.

## Case comparison

Side-by-side output comparison of two or more cases, with residuals and configurable
difference types, presented as tables and charts.

## Calculations

Derived quantity calculations defined from vectors applied across all cases and properties at once. Results become
derived vectors that plot exactly alongside existing vectors.

## Net present value

NPV analysis per case, and NPV across a whole ensemble, so economic outcome can be compared
alongside technical performance.

## Opportunity index

An infill and opportunity index computed from pressure thresholds together with oil and gas
fluid parameters, to highlight areas of remaining potential.

## Regions and thresholds

Numeric and threshold regions can be built and combined with boolean composites — AND, OR,
NOT and XOR — then used to filter both grids and plots, so analysis is restricted to the
part of the model that matters.

## Resampling

Case time series can be resampled onto a fixed interval, or onto another case's timeline, so
runs with different reporting frequencies compare correctly.

title: Header Section
summary: Data is often collected in Text Files and these can come in various formats.
markdown:
## Header Section

***

Data is often collected in Text Files and these can come in various formats. In general the format comprises of a Header section of keywords specifying the data origin name, start date, date format, etc. followed by tables of data with column headers containing property names, units, well names, etc. These can be split over multiple Pages.

### Supported Header Keywords

Any text data file can begin with a header section that can contain information about the data as a whole. Keywords are optional but aid interpretation and integration with other data sets.

Keywords must appear at the beginning of a line to be recognised.

Information can be defined with the following supported keywords:

- ORIGIN: Sets the Origin for the data as it appears in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view).
- DATEFORMAT: Specifies the date format for any date values in the file.
- STARTDATE: Sets the reference start date for the data.
- PAGE: Sets the Page number for files that contain multiple tables.

The keywords details are outlined as follows:

#### ORIGIN

Takes a single string, with no spaces, to set the origin of the dataset as it appears in the Project View

##### Example

ORIGIN Well\_B2\_History

#### DATEFORMAT

Takes a prescribed string to define the how a date value is represented in the data.

"DD" is a two digit day of the month value.

"MM" is a two digit month of the year value.

"YY" is a two digit year value.

"YYYY" is a four digit year value.

The prescribed date formats are:

- DD/MM/YYYY (This is the default option)
- DD-MM-YYYY
- DD.MM.YYYY

* DD/MM/YY
* DD-MM-YY
* DD.MM.YY

+ MM/DD/YYYY
+ MM-DD-YYYY
+ MM.DD.YYYY

- MM/DD/YY
- MM-DD-YY
- MM.DD.YY

##### Example

DATEFORMAT DD/MM/YYYY

#### STARTDATE

Takes a string, in the date format, to set the start date for the data.

This is advised when any TIME data is defined as a day count rather than a date.

##### Example

STARTDATE 01/01/2000

#### PAGE

Takes a string index of the page.

The PAGE keyword is principally needed when a text file contains more than one table of data, especially when the tables contain differing columns. Each table of data can be headed with a PAGE keyword and an incremented index.

##### Example

PAGE 1

title: HPG Files
summary: High Performance Grid (HPG) files are produced during the loading of the Grid geometry data.
markdown:
## HPG Files

***

High Performance Grid (HPG) files are produced during the loading of the Grid geometry data.

#### Corner Point Grid Optimisation

S3analyse uses several techniques to minimise the memory requirement of a corner point grid and these result in a substantially reduced memory allocation of that of similar products. As a corner point grid is loaded the optimisation techniques reduce the amount of memory required to describe the grid without any loss of resolution in the model. Using the HPG option it is possible to record the results of this process and save them for later use. Loading the HPG results can be significantly faster than starting with the original grid and going through the grid load and optimisation steps.

#### HPG Files

By default the HPG data for a grid is created in a directory (named HPG\_64) that is immediately below that where the grid file is located.

## Chart Data Ribbon Context Tab

***

![Ribbon chart data context tab options group](/img/help/ribbon-chartdatacontexttaboptionsgroup.png)![Ribbon chart data context tab search group](/img/help/ribbon-chartdatacontexttabsearchgroup.png)

### Overview

The Chart Data tab contains the settings for the data used on the active [Line Plot](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots).

### Access and Visibility

The Chart Data tab appears in the ribbon when a suitable [Line Plot chart](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots) is active.

The tab updates its content based on what you select.

### Main Functional Groups

The Chart Data ribbon tab is organized into several key groups:

#### Options Group

##### Show Observed Data

Toggles the display of observed data, if there is observed data loaded for the project.

##### Hide Repeated Observed Data

Toggles the suppression of the duplication of observed data on a chart when the same observed data is associated in with multiple displayed properties. Requires observed data loaded for the project.

#### Search Group

The [indexing](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots/indexing) options are presented to offer quick navigation of the data set.

##### Index By

Select the data property by which to index by, or indexing mode. This includes:

- Index by Case

This sets the search to be indexed by the case. Available only when multiple simulation cases are loading into a project.

- Index by Member

This sets the search to be indexed by the member, such as well name.

- Index by Submember

This sets the search to be indexed by the submember, such as completion location for a well.

- Index by Name

This sets the search to be indexed by the property name.

The current value for the active chart for the chosen index is shown on the ribbon as Current.

##### Use Project Filter

When enabled this option will limit the [indexing](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots/indexing) to the data defined with the [Project-Wide Filter](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/project-wide-filter).

#### Indexing controls

The search has three options for applying the indexing:

#####

##### Replace

Clicking the ![Find yellow](/img/help/find-yellow-16.png) Replace option will update each property on the active [Line Plot](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots) chart with the next item in the list based on the indexing selection.

Instead of the next item, selecting an item from the Select Item... drop down list of indexed values allows the choice of the index to update the active chart.

##### New

Clicking the ![Find blue](/img/help/find-blue-16.png) New option will create a new chart with the same line(s) as the active [Line Plot](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots) chart, updated with the next item in the list based on the indexing selection.

Instead of the next item, selecting an item from the Select Item... drop down list of indexed values allows the choice of the index with which to create a new chart.

##### Append

Clicking the ![Find green](/img/help/find-green-16.png) Append option will append a new line for each property on the active [Line Plot](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots) chart with the next item in the list based on the indexing selection.

Instead of the next item, selecting an item from the Select Item... drop down list of indexed values allows the choice of the index with which to create the new line(s) to append to the active chart.

##### Search Direction Buttons

Wrap ![Arrow loop](/img/help/arrow-loop-16.png)

This option allows the indexing to wrap around to the beginning/end of the list when indexing to the next item from the bottom/top of the list.

Search Direction ![Arrow pointing up](/img/help/arrow-pointing-up.jpg) ![Arrow pointing down](/img/help/arrow-pointing-down.png)

These buttons changes the order that the search operations moves in.

If the Up Arrow ![Arrow pointing up](/img/help/arrow-pointing-up.jpg) is selected the search will move up the alphanumeric list, and if the Down Arrow ![Arrow pointing down](/img/help/arrow-pointing-down.png) is selected searches downwards.

title: System Requirements
summary: S3analyse is a process and memory intensive 64-bit application.
markdown:
## System Requirements

***

S3analyse is a process and memory intensive 64-bit application. The system requirements for optimal performance are therefore:

- Operating System: 64-bit Windows 7 or later.
- Processor: Intel X64 based processor with at least 2 cores.
- Memory: 16GB minimum.
- Graphics: Any modern dedicated graphics card with at least 2GB of dedicated VRAM. Integrated graphics are supported as well, but performance will not be optimal.

title: Echelon
summary: S3analyse supports Echelon from Stone Ridge Technology.
markdown:
## Echelon Data Files

***

S3analyse supports Echelon from Stone Ridge Technology.

Echelon simulator files use many of the same industry-standard formats as Eclipse, but are optimised for GPU-based workflows and high-performance computing.

Echelon, developed by Stone Ridge Technology, supports both black oil and compositional models and is compatible with many of the same input and output file types used by [Eclipse](/docs/reference/loading-data/supported-data-types/eclipse).

Echelon data sets are loaded though the [Eclipse](/docs/reference/loading-data/supported-data-types/eclipse) file reader. All settings for Eclipse loading are applied to Echelon data sets.

The numeric regions defined by the loaded data (e.g. PVT, Saturation or Fluid in Place regions) are available from the [Numeric Regions node](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements) of the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) Treeview. Each Numeric Region node is labelled with its associated property definition and the number of different regions defined.

## Pearson Coefficient Plot

### Overview

The Pearson Coefficient Plot widget in S3analyse dashboards visualizes a Pearson Coefficient analysis of the multiple cases within a [Project](/docs/reference/loading-data/projects).

The Pearson Coefficient Plot looks up the parameters in the [.params file](/docs/reference/loading-data/supported-data-types/input-parameter-files) and builds the coefficient plot using those parameters and parameter values among the project cases.

### Creating a Pearson Coefficient Plot

To create a Pearson Coefficient Plot:

1. Select an active [Dashboard](/docs/reference/dashboards)
2. In the [Dashboard Design Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs/dashboard-tools/design-tab) select Pearson Coefficient Plot from the Panels group.

This will add a widget Tile to the end of the Dashboard sequence containing the Pearson Coefficient Plot across all cases in a multi-case model.

### Modifying a Pearson Coefficient Plot

The data used to define the plot and its appearance can be modified.

The settings are described in [Pearson Coefficient Plot Settings](/docs/reference/dashboards/widgets/pearson-coefficient-plot/pearson-coefficient-plot-settings).

title: Python scripting
summary: Drive S3analyse from Python to automate workflows and batch processing.
markdown:
S3analyse exposes a Python API that can query and control a running instance — loading data,
creating plots, applying calculations and reading case state. Scripts are the primary way to
automate repetitive analysis and to capture a workflow so it can be run again.

Script files use the `.s3py` extension and run against a bundled Python runtime, so there is
no separate Python installation to manage.

## A minimal script

```python
from load_pythonapi import load_pythonapi
load_pythonapi()
from PythonAPI.APIs import Analyse

project = Analyse.DataCentre.ActiveProject
plot = Analyse.Display.CreateLinePlot()
```

## What the API covers

- **Sessions and loading** — start a session, load cases and observed data
- **Query** — projects, cases, vectors, wells, producers and injectors, timesteps
- **Plot creation** — line, histogram, line analysis, grid display, scatter, dashboard,
  multi-plot, RFT, mismatch, table and VFP plots
- **Styling** — axes, legends, titles, colours and series appearance
- **3D grid control** — view angles, cut planes, clipping, legends, thresholds, ternary
- **Calculations** — create, associate variables, apply across cases
- **Regions** — leaf, threshold and boolean composite regions
- **Resampling** — fixed-interval and case-based
- **Export** — send results to Office

## Saving a session as a script

An entire project or session can be saved as a Python script rather than a binary project
file. Re-running it rebuilds the analysis, which makes a study reproducible and easy to
re-apply to a new set of runs.

> Objects are addressed by case name, object name or simulator-assigned number — never by
> internal identifiers — so a script written today still works against a reloaded project.

#### View Mode

Select the viewing option for the grid:

- 3D All: Display the entire grid in a full 3D mode.

* Single Layer: Display a single layer/slice of the grid in full 3D. This enables the Layers/Slices control.

+ 2D View: Switch to a flat, 2D representation of a single grid layer/slice. This enables the Layers/Slices control.

#### Layers/Slices

For Single Layer and 2D View, these options allow the selection of the orientation of the slice and which layer/Slice to show:

- Slice Mode: Select which orientation of slice of the grid to display. Choose from XY, XZ or YZ.

* Slice/Layer: Select which layer (for XY Slices) or slice (for XZ and YZ slices) to show.

+ Level: For 2D View only, choose which level of the cells to form the display from: Top/Front, Middle, or Bottom/Back.

The display can be created as a view of the Top/Front surface of the layer/slice or the Bottom. An alternative Middle provides an average of the top/front and bottom/back surface.

title: Grid Features
summary: The Grid Display offers a number of different features to facilitate the examination of the map data, from slicing and clipping the grid to reduce it to the part you need, to filtering, collapsing...
markdown:
## Grid Features

***

### Overview

The [Grid Display](/docs/reference/grid-displays) offers a number of different features to facilitate the examination of the map data, from slicing and clipping the grid to reduce it to the part you need, to filtering, collapsing and grouping the underlying cell data for analysis.

These features include:

| [Layer Analysis](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-features/layer-analysis) | Sum or average property values over a chosen range of layers for each column of cells, producing a single-layer grid |
| --- | --- |
| [Cut Planes](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-features/cut-planes) | Slice through the grid with one or more planes to inspect internal cell values while keeping the full 3D spatial context |
| [Grid Clipping](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-features/grid-clipping) | Trim the grid down to a rectangular sub-region defined by cell indices, hiding everything outside it |
| [Thresholds](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-features/thresholds) | Filter and highlight cells based on the value of a chosen property, using one or more criteria combined with AND, OR or XOR |
| [Regions](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-features/regions) | Save a named subset of grid cells, either from a threshold you define or predefined by the simulation dataset, for reuse across grids and analysis tools |

## Ribbon Menu

### Overview

The Ribbon Menu provides easy access to the common controls and settings of S3analyse, charts, grids, etc.

### Quick Access Toolbar

At the top of the Ribbon is the [Quick Access Toolbar](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/quick-access-toolbar) that provides access to new sessions, loading, saving and S3analyse general settings.

### Ribbon Tabs

The Ribbon contains a number of tabs that are always available:

- [File Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/file-tab) contains controls starting a new session, [selecting and loading data files](/docs/reference/loading-data), [Projects](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view), [Python scripts](/docs/reference/python-scripting), viewing logs and accessing the [General Settings](/docs/reference/general-settings).
- [Home Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/home-tab) for creating new [Grid displays](/docs/reference/grid-displays), [Charts](/docs/reference/chart-displays), etc. and [Reports](/docs/reference/exporting-reports).
- [View Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/view-tab) contains controls for storing and reapplying the arrangement of the panes within S3analyse and define the base font size for various components of the interface.

### Ribbon Context Tabs

Further there are a number of context tabs that are available only when the corresponding feature is active:

- For [Grid Displays](/docs/reference/grid-displays):
  - [Grid View Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs/grid-tools/grid-view-tab) for common settings for the appearance of the active [Grid](/docs/reference/grid-displays) display.
  - [Grid Data Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs/grid-tools/grid-data-tab) for settings for data used on the active [Grid](/docs/reference/grid-displays).

markdown:
## Modifying Charts

***

### Overview

All chart types can be extensively customized to suit your analysis and presentation needs. Modifications can be made directly through the chart interface or via [Contextual Ribbon Tabs](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs) that are available when a chart is active.

### Accessing Chart Settings

There are two primary ways to modify a chart:

1. Double Left-Click on any part of the chart to open the chart settings dialog, which provides access to the appearance options.

1) Use the [Contextual Ribbon Tabs](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs) that appear when a chart is active. These are specific to each chart type.

### Modifying Charts

Charts can be modified to change their appearance or how the chart is formulated.

#### Chart Settings

Each chart type has its own set of options presented in the settings dialog:

- [Line Plot Settings](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots/line-plot-settings)

title: Cut Planes
summary: The Cut Plane functionality allows users to slice through the simulation grid to inspect internal cell values while maintaining the full 3D spatial context.
markdown:
## Cut Planes

***

### Overview

The Cut Plane functionality allows users to slice through the simulation grid to inspect internal cell values while maintaining the full 3D spatial context. Using Cut Planes, you can expose internal layers or view cross‑sections of the grid to better understand spatial variations in properties such as pressure, saturation, permeability, etc.

An example of Cut Plane showing the cell values that intersect with an arbitrary plane.

![Grid cut plane example](/img/help/gridcutplaneexample.png)

#### Accessing the Grid Cut Planes

You can access the [Cut Plane Settings](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-settings/cut-planes) through the grid display interface:

1. Open the [Grid Display](/docs/reference/grid-displays) you wish to customize
2. Double left-click on the Grid
3. The [Grid Editors](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-settings) dialog will be displayed
4. Select [Cut Planes](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-settings/cut-planes) from the Treeview.

From these settings a Cut Planes can be created and controlled.

### What a Cut Plane Does

A Cut Plane is a plane passed through the body of the grid. It can be a single plane, a pair of parallel planes, or a regular stacked or mesh family of planes running through the grid at set intervals.

Wherever a plane intersects the grid, the cell values at that cross-section are displayed. You can choose to show only the cells the plane touches, for a thin slice through the data, or also keep the cells on one side, in-between, or outside the plane(s), so you can peel back part of the grid to reveal what's inside.

### Why Use Cut Planes

- See how a property such as pressure, saturation, or permeability varies inside the reservoir body, not just on its outer surface.
- Inspect a specific layer or cross-section, for example through a well or across a fault.
- Isolate a zone of interest by keeping only the slab between a pair of planes, or open up the middle of the grid to reveal the internal structure.
- Sweep systematically through the whole grid with stacked or mesh planes to QC geometry, layering, or property continuity.
- Angle a plane freely to align it with a fault or well trajectory, rather than being limited to a fixed axis.

### How to Use Cut Plane

Choose a [Cut Plane Mode](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-settings/cut-planes) based on what you want to see: a single angled slice, an isolated slab, or a systematic sweep through the grid.

#### Free-Orientated Planes

- Single Plane: Set Orientation (XY / XZ / YZ / Arbitrary), then Offset (and Rotation/Tilt if Arbitrary) to place the plane; choose Plane Only / Minus Side / Plus Side to decide how much of the grid stays visible.
- Plane Pair: Same orientation controls, plus Spacing between the two planes; choose Planes Only / Between / Outside to isolate or remove the slab between them.

#### Axis-Orientated Planes

- Stacked X / Y / Z: A series of parallel planes on one axis; set either a plane count (always odd — one at each extremity, one at centre) or a fixed spacing distance.
- Mesh in X and Y / Mesh in X, Y and Z: Combines two or three stacked axes into a waffle/lattice pattern, each axis configured independently the same way.

Appearance (Show Plane/Normal, colour, Transparency) applies regardless of mode and can be adjusted at any time.

title: Grid Clipping
summary: Grid Clipping allows users to display only a subset of the simulation Grid Display, hiding everything outside a chosen range of cells.
markdown:
## Grid Clipping

***

### Overview

Grid Clipping allows users to display only a subset of the simulation [Grid Display](/docs/reference/grid-displays), hiding everything outside a chosen range of cells. Unlike [Cut Planes](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-features/cut-planes), which slice the grid at a geometric plane, Grid Clipping trims the grid down to a rectangular sub-region defined by cell indices, letting you focus on the part of the model that matters without the rest of the grid getting in the way.

An example of Grid Clipping focusing the grid display around wells B4, B5 and B6.

![Grid clipping example](/img/help/gridclippingexample.png)

#### Accessing the Grid Clipping

You can access the [Grid Clipping Settings](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-settings/grid-clipping) through the grid display interface:

1. Open the Grid you wish to customize
2. Double left-click on the Grid
3. The Grid Editors dialog will be displayed
4. Select Grid Clipping from the Treeview.

From these settings the Grid Clipping can be defined.

### What Grid Clipping Does

Grid Clipping sets upper and lower limits on the I, J and K cell indices, so only the cells within that box are drawn; everything outside it is hidden.

You can thin out the display further with increments, which draw only every nth slice in a chosen dimension, and Intersect, which shows only the cells where the increment slices in different dimensions overlap. The clipped grid can also be rescaled to fill the display window.

### Why Use Grid Clipping

- Focus on a specific reservoir zone or fault block by hiding the rest of the grid.
- Reduce visual clutter and speed up interaction when working with very large grids.
- Isolate the region around a well or group of wells for closer inspection.
- Get a fast structural overview of a large grid by displaying only every few layers instead of every cell.
- Combine increments with Intersect to reveal a coarse structural "skeleton" of the grid geometry for a quick QC check.

### How to Use Grid Clipping

Start by bounding the region you want to see, then layer on thinning or rescaling as needed.

- Set the visible region (Range Controls): Set Min/Max index limits for I, J and K; only cells within all three ranges are drawn. Leave a dimension at its full range to leave that axis unclipped.
- Thin out the display (Increments): Set a step size in one or more dimensions to draw only every nth slice within the clipped range, useful for a fast structural overview of a large grid without drawing every cell.
- Isolate slice intersections (Intersect): With increments set in two or three dimensions, enable Intersect to show only the cells where those increment slices overlap, revealing a coarse structural "skeleton" for a quick QC check.
- Fit the display (Rescale to Window): Enable Rescale to Window so the clipped/thinned grid expands to fill the Grid Display, useful once clipping or increments have shrunk the visible region.

## Tooltip Settings

### Overview

The Tooltip Settings provide options to configure a tooltip for displaying detailed cell information at the cursor.

When this option is enabled with Show Cell Information hovering the cursor over a cell will display a tooltip window showing the value of the displayed property for that cell as well as any coordinates or additional property values specified in these settings.

Any changes are applied directly to the Grid as they are made.

#### Accessing the Grid Settings

You can access the Tooltip Settings through the grid interface:

1. Open the Grid you wish to customize

3. Select Tooltip Settings from the treeview in the Grid Editors dialog

### Available Settings Categories

The Tooltip Settings are organized into three sections:

#### Cell Information

Toggle the visibility of the tooltip with cell-related information. This option is also available in the [Grid View Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs/grid-tools/grid-view-tab). This option also enables the other controls on this dialog.

#### Coordinates

Define the type of cell coordinate-related information shown in tooltips:

- Corner Points: Displays the coordinates for the corner points of cell.
- Face Depths: Displays depths for cell top and bottom faces.

#### Additional Properties

Configure any other property data to include in the tooltip.

List Init will list any init properties found in the data set for the Grid and make them available for selection.

List Only Selected will list only properties that have been selected.

The Filter applies to the property names in the list to easily find the desired property.

title: Text Files
summary: Data is often collected in Text Files and these can come in various formats.
markdown:
## Text Files

***

Data is often collected in Text Files and these can come in various formats. S3analyse supports many text formats through a flexible approach to parsing the text data.

In general the recommended text format comprises of a Header section of keywords specifying the data origin name, start date, date format, etc. followed by tables of data with column headers containing property names, units, well names, etc. These can be split over multiple Pages.

Examples of various supported text file formats can be found in [Text File Examples](/docs/reference/loading-data/supported-data-types/text-files/text-file-examples).

### Adding Data from Text Files

Data can be added in two ways:

1. Text files can be loaded directly.
2. Text files can be added to a loaded data set as Observed Data.

Loading a text file directly creates a new dataset in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view); adding it as Observed Data attaches its vectors to an existing loaded project for comparison against simulated results.

### Text File Format

Text files are comprised of a [Header Section](/docs/reference/loading-data/supported-data-types/text-files/header-section) and a [Data Section](/docs/reference/loading-data/supported-data-types/text-files/data-table-section):

The [Header Section](/docs/reference/loading-data/supported-data-types/text-files/header-section) contains information about the data as a whole, such as case name, start date, etc.

The [Data Section](/docs/reference/loading-data/supported-data-types/text-files/data-table-section) contains a table of property columns; a column header, units, well name, etc. and a the property values.

#### Comment Lines

Comment lines can be added to the file. These are defined with a double dash "--" at the start of the line. Any text following these is disregarded. These are useful to add context notes and simulation references to the start of a text file.

#### Formatting Columns

Data should be formatted in a way to determine the individual columns of data and their associated column headers. The reader assumes a single column delimiter type on each line. It will automatically detect the delimiter in the following order of priority:

1. Tabs ("\t")
2. Commas (",")
3. Spaces (multiple spaces are treated as a single delimiter)

Note: Tables should be consistently formatted throughout and not mix delimiters. Any variation in formatting may lead to the data failing to load or being misinterpreted.

![Ribbon home tab clipboard group](/img/help/ribbon-hometabclipboardgroup.png)![Ribbon home tab view actions group](/img/help/ribbon-hometabviewactionsgroup.png)![Ribbon home tab graph settings group](/img/help/ribbon-hometabgraphsettingsgroup.png)![Ribbon home tab units group](/img/help/ribbon-hometabunitsgroup.png)![Ribbon home tab export group](/img/help/ribbon-hometabexportgroup.png)![Ribbon home tab workflows group](/img/help/ribbon-hometabworkflowsgroup.png)

### Overview

The Home tab contains controls to create new [Grid displays](/docs/reference/grid-displays), [Charts](/docs/reference/chart-displays), etc. and [Reports](/docs/reference/exporting-reports). It also accesses the [Workflow Manager](/docs/reference/workflows) and contains some system settings and the clipboard controls.

### Access and Visibility

The Home tab is always present in the ribbon.

### Main Functional Groups

The Home ribbon tab is organized into several key groups:

#### Clipboard Group

##### Copy

This will place the currently active display item in the [Display Area](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/display-area) onto the clipboard.

#### View Actions Group

##### Show Grid

Create a [Grid Display](/docs/reference/grid-displays).

##### Multi-Plot

Create a [Multi-Plot](/docs/reference/chart-displays/multi-plot).

##### User Dashboard

Create a [Dashboard](/docs/reference/dashboards).

##### Calculations

Create a new [Calculation](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/calculations).

##### Show NPV

Create a [NPV Chart](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/npv-calculations).

##### Show NPV Ensemble

Create a [NPV Ensemble Chart](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/npv-calculations).

#####

##### Show Mismatches

Create a [Mismatches Analysis](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/mismatches-analysis).

##### Show Case Comparison

Create a [Case Comparison](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/case-comparison) Analysis.

#### Graph Settings Group

##### Show Observed Data (New Plots)

When Show Observed Data is enabled any observed data associated with a simulated property will automatically be added as a scatter line to any new [Line Plots](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots) when plotting the simulated data. Additionally, when plotting observed data the associated simulated property will similarly be added.

#### Units Group

##### Units System

A loaded data set will contain its specified unit system. Alternatively, S3analyse can convert any data to an alternative unit system when creating charts or tables by choosing a system from this drop down.

The default unit system is that specified by the model. This is labelled as Data Units.

For Eclipse models the unit can be set to:

- Eclipse Field
- Eclipse Lab
- Eclipse Metric

For Nexus models the units can be set to:

- Nexus Field
- Nexus Lab
- Nexus Metric (Bar)
- Nexus Metric (Kg/cm2)
- Nexus Metric (KPa)

#### Export Group

Produce a [Report](/docs/reference/exporting-reports).

#### Workflows Group

##### Workflow Manager...

Launches the [Workflow Manager](/docs/reference/workflows).

title: Histograms
summary: A Histogram displays the distribution of a property by grouping values into contiguous bins and representing each bin’s frequency with a bar.
markdown:
## Histograms

***

### Overview

A Histogram displays the distribution of a property by grouping values into contiguous bins and representing each bin’s frequency with a bar. The height of each bar corresponds to how many values fall within its interval, illustrating the shape of the data - whether it’s symmetric, skewed, or multimodal. Histograms are essential for understanding central tendency, variability, and outliers in large datasets.

### Creating a Histogram

Histogram charts are limited to map properties (Solution or Init data). They can be created by:

- Navigating to the appropriate map property in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view).
- Right-click the chosen property in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) and selecting Histogram for <property> in <grid name> Grid.

The Histogram appearance can then be customised, such as titles, axes and colours.

#### Region Filtering

[Regions](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/regions) can be used to show per-region data. Selecting the type of Numeric Region from the Region Filtering group of the [Histogram Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs/chart-tools/histogram-tab) will create set of Histograms, one for each set of cells of the same region index.

### Example

![Histogram example](/img/help/histogramexample.png)

This chart shows a Histogram of the grid Pressure values at the first timestep.

### Modifying Histograms

The appearance of a Histogram can be changed as desired and the data used in the chart can also be changed.

#### Modifying the Histogram

Histograms have a list of settings to customise the appearance. These are outlined in [Histogram Settings](/docs/reference/chart-displays/histograms/histogram-settings) and can be accessed by double left-clicking on the any part of the Histogram chart.

These are in complement to the [Histogram Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs/chart-tools/histogram-tab) that offers a selection of settings controlling the formulation and the data used in the chart.

#### Modifying the Data in the Histogram

Changing the data used to generate a Histogram is achieved with the Selected Property Group in the [Histogram Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs/chart-tools/histogram-tab). This allows the selection of any appropriate data from the Project to update the chart.

### Exporting Line Plots

Histograms can be exported with the [Report](/docs/reference/exporting-reports) Feature.

### Scripts and Line Plots

Histograms are supported by [Python Scripting](/docs/reference/python-scripting).

title: Indexing
summary: Indexing is a powerful feature that allows users to quickly navigate data sets efficiently across multiple cases, wells, completions, or properties and updating Line Plots.
markdown:
## Indexing *** ### Overview Indexing is a powerful feature that allows users to quickly navigate data sets efficiently across multiple cases, wells, completions, or properties and updating [Line Plots](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots). It is especially useful when working with ensembles or large datasets, enabling quick comparisons and batch updates to charts. ### Accessing Indexing Tools Indexing controls are available in the [Chart Data Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs/chart-tools/chart-data-tab) when a [Line Plot](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots) chart is active. The chart updates dynamically based on the selected property in the Ribbon. ### Indexing Modes You can index by several data properties, depending on the data loaded: |
  • Case
| Index by the loaded simulation cases | | --- | --- | |
  • Member
| Index by the member name. Typically this refers to well names, region names, or other grouped items | |
  • Submember
| Index by the submember. This refers to more granular elements like completion locations | |
  • Name
| Index by property name, e.g., WOPR, GOR, etc. | The current value of the index for the active chart is shown in the [Chart Data Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs/chart-tools/chart-data-tab) as Current. ### Indexing Actions Once an indexing Mode is selected, you can apply it using the following actions from the Ribbon: |
  • Replace
| Updates each property on the active chart with the next item in the index list | | --- | --- | |
  • New
| Creates a new chart with the same structure but updated to the next indexed item | |
  • Append
| Adds a new line to the existing chart using the next indexed item | You can also manually select an item from the Select Item... drop down menu to apply a specific index value in any of the three actions. ### Search Direction and Wrapping The indexing can be performed up or down the list of indexing items and the result of reaching the end of the list controlled: |
  • Wrap
| Enables circular indexing, looping back to the start/end when reaching the limits | | --- | --- | |
  • Search Direction
| Use the Up or Down arrows to control the indexing order | ### Use with Project Filters Indexing can be combined with the [Project-Wide Filter](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/project-wide-filter) to restrict the indexed items to a subset of the ensemble or data properties. ### Use Cases Example use cases are: - Quickly compare WOPR across all wells. - Generate charts for each case in an ensemble. - Append multiple completions to a single plot for visual comparison. - Automate chart creation for batch reporting. ### Tips - Indexing is most useful when multiple cases or large number of wells are loaded. - Combine with [Broadcasting](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/window-view/broadcasting) to update linked charts simultaneously. - Use [Zoom History](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs/chart-tools/chart-view-tab) and [Axis Limits](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots/line-plot-settings/axis-settings) to manage complex multi-line plots.

title: Eclipse
summary: S3analyse is designed to seamlessly load, interpret and present a wide range of output files generated by the Eclipse and Intersect reservoir simulators.
markdown:
## Eclipse Data Files

***

S3analyse is designed to seamlessly load, interpret and present a wide range of output files generated by the Eclipse and Intersect reservoir simulators. These include:

• Summary files containing vector data, whether formatted or unformatted, unified or non-unified

• Restart files capturing solution states at various time steps

• Grid and initial files defining the simulation geometry and starting conditions

• RFT/PLT files providing well test and production logging data

Each simulation run can produce a substantial volume of output, encapsulating complex reservoir behaviour and performance metrics. Navigating this data manually can be time-consuming and error-prone. S3analyse streamlines this process by offering a fast, intuitive way to load and visualize simulation results.

Users can open multiple datasets from different runs simultaneously, enabling comparative analysis, trend identification, and efficient plotting workflows.

By default the entire data set will be loaded. To perform a selected load the [Eclipse Load](/docs/reference/loading-data/supported-data-types/eclipse/load-dialog) dIalog can be used.

The Histogram tab appears in the ribbon when a suitable [Histogram chart](/docs/reference/chart-displays/histograms) is active.

The tab updates its content based on what you select.

### Main Functional Groups

The Histogram ribbon tab is organized into several key groups:

#### Settings Group

The main settings of the construction of the Histogram are collected in this group:

##### Number of Bins

This sets the number of bins the data will be collected into. The higher the number the more bars on the chart.

##### Data Range Minimum/Maximum

This sets the lower and upper limits of the sampled range of the data property. It is this range that is divided into the bins.

This can be altered with the sliders or by typing the values into the textboxes.

##### Delta

This displays the size of each bin for the given number of bins over the specified range.

##### Reset

The reset button ![Refresh reload](/img/help/refresh-reload-16-n-p.png) will return the Histogram to the default settings for Number Of Bins and Data Range.

#### Selected Property Group

The selected property to base the Histogram on can be set from the [Selected Property](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/common-ribbon-controls/selected-property-ribbon-group) controls.

#### Region Filtering Group

The histograms can be broken down by [Numeric Regions](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/regions), like FIPNUM, by selecting a chosen region from the drop-down box.

Clicking on ![Filter](/img/help/filter-16-n-p.png) will open the list of available [Numeric Regions](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/regions). From this individual plots for a given regions can be added or removed from the display.

title: Well Statistics Plot
summary: The Well Statistics Plot widget in S3analyse dashboards visualizes a single Well property across all wells and across multiple cases within a Project.
markdown:
## Well Statistics Plot

***

### Overview

The Well Statistics Plot widget in S3analyse dashboards visualizes a single Well property across all wells and across multiple cases within a [Project](/docs/reference/loading-data/projects). It in intended for use in such projects as Sensitivity Analyses.

The Well Statistics Plot ranks the wells based on the selected Vector from high to low, left to right, across all cases. For each well the Average; Average +/- 1 standard deviation; Minimum and Maximum are all drawn for the Point of Interest value across the cases.

Each well shows a vertical arrangement of:

- Marker at the Average value across all cases
- Bounded box around the marker indicates Average +/- 1 standard deviation
- Thin line shows the extent of the Maximum and Minimum values across all cases

Hovering the mouse over the marker shows the Well Name, Maximum, Average and Minimum.

### Creating a Well Statistics Plot

To create a Well Statistics Plot:

1. Select an active [Dashboard](/docs/reference/dashboards)
2. In the [Dashboard Design Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs/dashboard-tools/design-tab) select Well Statistics Plot from the Panels group.

This will add a widget Tile to the end of the Dashboard sequence containing the default Well Statistics Plot of the Final Field Oil Production Total against the Time for all cases in a multi-case model.

### Modifying a Well Statistics Plot

The data used to define the plot and its appearance can be modified.

The settings are described in [Well Statistics Plot Settings](/docs/reference/dashboards/widgets/well-statistics-plot/well-statistics-plot-settings).

title: Export and reporting
summary: One-click export to Excel, Word and PowerPoint, plus simulator decks and schedules.
markdown:
Analysis usually has to leave the application. S3analyse exports both the presentation of a
result and the underlying data.

## Microsoft Office

The active window or dataset exports directly to **Excel**, **Word** or **PowerPoint** from
the Home ribbon, so a plot can go into a report or presentation without a screenshot.

## Data and images

Vector data tables export to CSV with configurable settings, and any view can be exported as
an image for use elsewhere.

## Simulator decks and schedules

S3analyse writes Eclipse and Nexus decks and schedules, along with deviation and trajectory
files — so a change explored in the application can be taken back to the simulator.

title: Opening Files
summary: You can open a file in two simple ways:
markdown:
## Opening Files

***

You can open a file in two simple ways:

### Using the File Menu

Click [File Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/file-tab) and select ![File open](/img/help/file-open-16-n-p.png) Open. This will launch the File Browser dialog. This can be used to browse to the file you want to open. Select it and click Open to load it into the application. This works just like in most Office or productivity applications.

### Drag and Drop

Drag a file from your Desktop or File Explorer and drop it directly onto the application window. The file will load automatically once dropped.

### Load Process

The default load process is for S3analyse to automatically load as much as it is able to find on a data set and present it in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view).

If a selective load is required then a load dialog can be presented to allow the user to control what is loaded from a data set. The dialog is requested individually for each simulator type. It can be set from the specific [Simulator Options](/docs/reference/general-settings/simulators).

Loaded data sets are presented in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) as a [Project](/docs/reference/loading-data/projects).

If a data set comprises multiple cases, for example a sensitivity analysis, it is presented as a [Multi-Case Project](/docs/reference/loading-data/projects/multi-case-projects).

title: Loading simulation data
summary: Read cases from every major reservoir simulator into a single project.
markdown:
S3analyse reads simulation output natively, so cases from different simulators sit side by
side in the same project and can be plotted and compared together.

## Supported simulators

| Simulator | Typical files |
|---|---|
| Eclipse Grid Data | `.EGRID`,`.GRID`, `.GRD`, `.GSG`, `.FGRID`, `.FGR`|
| Eclipse INIT Data | `.INIT`, `.INI` ,`.FINIT`, `.FIN`|
| Eclipse RFT Data | `.RFT`, `.FRFT` ,`.FRT`|
| Eclipse Solution Data | `.UNRST`, `.UNR`, `.FUNRST`,`.FUR`|
| Eclipse Summary Data | `.SMSPEC`, `.SMS`, `.UNSMRY`,`.USY`,`.FSMSPEC`,`.FSM`,`.FUNSMRY`,`.FUS`,`.H5`|
| Nexus | `.FCS`,`.vdb` case folders, `main.xml` |
| CMG | `.sr3` |
| METEOR/UTCHEM | `.S3ECHO`, `.S3PERM`, `.S3DATA`, `.S3OVERAL`, `.S3HIST` , `.S3TRAC`  |
| S3analyse Project File | `.anax` |
| Observed Data CSV | `.csv` |

See the [Simulators](/docs/reference/general-settings/simulators) section for more information.

Observed and historic data can be loaded alongside simulated results, from S3GRAF export
format and .csv files.

## Projects and sessions

A loaded session can be saved as an S3analyse project (`.anax`) and reopened later, or
saved as a Python script that regenerates the whole session — useful for repeating an analysis
against a new set of runs.

## Loading only what you need

Large studies do not need everything in memory. Load options control how much of each case
is read. Hundreds of runs can be loaded quickly and large multimillion cell models can be loaded in seconds.
S3analyse can automatically load the necessary HPG files for faster performance.

title: Chart Displays
summary: S3analyse can be used to quickly create Line Plot charts by double-left clicking on time series data in the Project View.
markdown:
## Charts Displays

***

###

### Overview

S3analyse can be used to quickly create [Line Plot](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots) charts by double-left clicking on time series data in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view). The data is presented as line plot against an associated time vector. Other chart types are also available.

There are a number of chart types available in S3analyse:

- [Line Plots](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots) for displaying time series properties.
- [Multi-Plot](/docs/reference/chart-displays/multi-plot) for creating a selection of charts as part of a single display.
- [RFT Plots](/docs/reference/chart-displays/rft-plots) for creating a property versus depth chart of Repeat Formation Test (RFT) data.
- [Histograms](/docs/reference/chart-displays/histograms) for creating a chart of the distribution of map data properties.
- [Line Analysis](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-analysis) for viewing the change in a map data property in space and time.
- [Grid Scatter Plot](/docs/reference/chart-displays/grid-scatter-plot) for viewing the relationship between corresponding values for two map data properties.
- [Table Data Chart](/docs/reference/chart-displays/table-data-charts) for viewing table data, such as PVT or saturation tables, as a chart and data table.

### Creating Charts

The full range of possible chart displays can be created by right clicking on a property on the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) and selecting a chart type from the menu.

Detailed information on creating chart can be found in [Creating Charts](/docs/reference/chart-displays/creating-charts).

### Modifying Charts

All charts have an extensive list of settings to customise the appearance. These are detailed in their sections.

The displayed property can be changed from the appropriate tab of the [Ribbon Menu](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu) or by left-click drag and dropping a new map property from the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) to the existing chart.

Settings can be accessed by double left-clicking on the any part of a chart. A dialog outlining all the available options is presented to the user.

Detailed information on modifying grids can be found in [Modifying Charts](/docs/reference/chart-displays/modifying-charts).

### Exporting Charts

All chart types can be exported with the [Report](/docs/reference/exporting-reports) Feature.

### Scripts and Charts

All chart types are supported by [Python Scripting](/docs/reference/python-scripting).

The list of Ensemble Plot properties contains the Summary Field and Field Errors vectors.

#### Point of Interest

title: Project-Wide Filter
summary: The Project-Wide Filter allows users to filter and select loaded cases.
markdown:
## Project-Wide Filter

***

### Overview

The Project-Wide Filter allows users to filter and select loaded cases. It provides both pattern-based filtering and manual case selection capabilities. It is used to support simulations containing multiple runs.

The results of any case filtering will be shown in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) and will affect some components of the application.

#### Accessing the Project-Wide Filter

The filter can be accessed only when the [active project](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) has multiple cases. A button, labelled Project-Wide Filter, is available on the right-hand side of the [Display Area](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/display-area). Clicking this button will show the panel dialog.

The panel dialog will be automatically collapsed when no longer the active control. The panel dialog can be preserved by toggling the pin button on its title bar.

![Project wide filter panel](/img/help/projectwidefilterpanel.png)

### Case Filtering

The filter is made of three components:

1. Case Name Filter: Filtering the cases based on the case name.
2. Select Cases list: Select/unselect individual cases from the list of cases to be included/excluded from the filter.
3. Summary Property Filter: Filter the cases based on the value of a chosen Summary property.

Each component is independent. The total filtering is based on the application of all three options.

The results of any filtering performed in the Case Name Filter will be shown in the Select Case list.

#### Case Name Filter

This facilitates filtering of the case based on the name.

##### Filter Pattern

Enter a filter pattern to match the desired case names. This will filter the available cases in the Select Cases list. Wildcards "\*" and "?" are available for the name matching. To include all cases either leave the textbox empty or use a single "\*" wildcard.

##### ![Check list lines filled](/img/help/checklistlines-filled-16.png) Case List

Show/hide the Select Cases selection list.

##### ![Filter](/img/help/filter-16-n-p.png) Filter Toggle

Enable/disable all filtering of the cases, including Summary Property Filter.

#### Select Case List

Cases can be selected/unselected from the expandable list. Clicking on Select Cases or the arrow will expand/collapse this list.

This panel will list all the loaded cases for the selected project. Any filtering defined by the Case Name Filter will be applied to this list.

Individual cases can be included/excluded from the filter by selecting/unselecting them with their corresponding checkboxes.

#### Summary Property Filter

Clicking on Summary Property Filter or the arrow will expand/collapse these filter settings.

This panel allows the cases to be filtered on a chosen Summary property value and range.

Checking/unchecking Include in Filter will enable/disable the property filter.

Select the Summary property to filter the cases with the first drop down list.

Select value of property to be filtered on with the second drop down list. This can be:

- First: Filter on the first value of the chosen property
- Last: Filter on the last value of the chosen property
- Minimum: Filter on the minimum value of the chosen property
- Maximum: Filter on the maximum value of the chosen property
- Average: Filter on the average value of the chosen property
- Sum: Filter on the Sum of the values of the chosen property
- RMS: Filter on the Root Mean Squared (RMS) value of the chosen property

With the chosen property and value to be filtered selected the range of the values across the cases is set with the slider. The range of values to filter can be defined with the slider or with the minimum and maximum limits text boxes.

The filter range can be reset by clicking on ![Refresh reload](/img/help/refresh-reload-16-n-p.png).

Additional Summary Property FIlters can be added by clicking on ![Add item](/img/help/add-item-16-n-p.png) at the bottom of the panel. Filters can also be removed by clicking on ![Red cross](/img/help/red-cross-16-n-p.png).

### Effects of the Filtering

[Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) will list the filtered list of cases under the Cases node in the treeview.

[Indexing](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots/indexing) will operate over the filtered list of cases when Use Project Filter is enabled in the [Chart Data Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs/chart-tools/chart-data-tab).

[Dashboards](/docs/reference/dashboards) will filter the displayed cases according to the Project-Wide Filter when the Include Project Filter is checked in the [Dashboard Filter](/docs/reference/dashboards/filtering/dashboard-filter).

title: Table Data Charts
summary: A Table Data Chart displays the values of a Table data table, such as a PVT or saturation table, as a chart of one column against another, shown alongside a data grid of the table values.
markdown:
## Table Data Charts

***

### Overview

A Table Data Chart displays the values of a Table data table, such as a PVT or saturation table, as a chart of one column against another, shown alongside a data grid of the table values.

Table data is organised by table type (e.g. PVTO, SWOF, SGFN), each of which contains a list of table indices.

### Creating a Table Data Chart

Table Data Charts are not created from a right-click menu. Instead they can be created by:

- Double left-clicking a table index in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view).
- Drag and dropping a table index from the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) onto the [Display Area](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/display-area).

Both actions open a new Table Data Chart pane in the [Display Area](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/display-area), pre-selecting the table type and index that was double-clicked or dragged.

#### Selecting the Data

Each Table Data Chart pane includes a Selection Panel to the left of the chart, offering:

- Table: The table type to display, e.g. PVTO or SWOF.
- Region: The table index (region) to display, i.e. PVTNUM or SATNUM value.
- Y-Axis: The column of the table plotted against the table's default property, where more than one column is available, e.g. PVTO can plot RS, BO and VO against Pressure.
- Secondary Phase: The secondary phase, Gas or Water Saturation, to plot against Oil Saturation for SOF3 tables.

Selecting new values from these lists updates the chart and data grid without needing to open a new pane.

### Table Types

The chart produced depends on the type of table selected:

- Most tables plot a single curve of the selected column against the table's default property.
- PVT tables (e.g. PVTO) plot the selected property against Pressure. Where the table includes a solution GOR column, short spur lines are also drawn at each saturation pressure break point to represent the undersaturated branch.
- Relative permeability and capillary pressure tables (e.g. SWFN or SGFN, cross-referenced with the corresponding SOF3 region) plot the water or gas curve together with its corresponding oil curve on the same chart, using a secondary, inverted axis for the second saturation.

### Example

![Table data chart example](/img/help/tabledatachartexample.png)

This example shows a Table Data Chart of the SOF3 table for Region 1, plotting Oil and Water Saturation curves against Relative Permeability. The corresponding values are listed in the data grid to the left of the chart.

### Modifying Table Data Charts

The appearance of a Table Data Chart can not be changed.

### Exporting Table Data Charts

Table Data Charts can be exported with the [Report](/docs/reference/exporting-reports) Feature.

### Scripts and Table Data Charts

Table Data Charts are supported by [Python Scripting](/docs/reference/python-scripting).

#### Axis Title

- Title: Add or modify the text of the main title of your Axis

* Font: Customize font (size, style, colour) with the options available by clicking Select. A preview of the current font is shown with the "Preview" label.

#### Axis Line

Configure the appearance of the axis:

- Thickness: Set the thickness of the axes lines.

* Colour: Set the colour of the axes lines.

#### Axis Labels

Customize how value labels appear along the axis:

- Visible: Toggle the visibility of the axis labels.

* Angle: Set the angle of the axis labels either with the slider or by typing into or stepping through the text box.

  - Normal: Decimal representation of the label values, e.g. 2,000 or 3,000,000
  - Abbreviate: Engineering notation representation of the label values, e.g. 2K or 3M

## Ensemble Summary Plot Settings

title: Creating Grids
summary: In S3analyse, creating a Grid Display is as simple as double clicking on a chosen map data property in the Project View and the grid is presented in the Display Area.
markdown:
## Creating Grid Displays

***

###

### Overview

In S3analyse, creating a Grid Display is as simple as double clicking on a chosen map data property in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) and the grid is presented in the [Display Area](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/display-area).

Additionally they can be created with the Show Grid button on the [Home Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/home-tab).

### Example

![Grid example](/img/help/gridexample.png)

An example of a [Grid Display](/docs/reference/grid-displays) of Pressure for the first timestep.

###

### Creating Grids

There are three main methods of creating grids:

1. Clicking on Show Grid in the [Home Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/home-tab) will produce a new grid in the [Display Area](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/display-area). It will show the first Solution property in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) or, if unavailable, from the Init data.

1) Double-clicking the chosen map property from the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view). S3analyse with create a grid of the chosen data and present it in the [Display Area](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/display-area). When Local Grid Refinements (LGRs) are present the Root grid is chosen by default.

Alternatively the property can be drag and dropped from the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) onto the [Display Area](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/display-area) to create a new grid. This process is also how data can used to update an existing grid.

1. Right-click on a chosen map property in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) to view the menu which contains the possible chart types available. Clicking on Grid <grid name> with <property> will produce a grid in the [Display Area](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/display-area). This method allows for the choice of which grid when Local Grid Refinements (LGRs) are present.

### Exporting Grids

Grid Displays can be exported with the [Report](/docs/reference/exporting-reports) Feature.

### Scripts and Grids

Grid Displays are supported by [Python Scripting](/docs/reference/python-scripting).
