title: Workflows
summary: A Workflow is a Python script written to be run repeatedly through the Workflow Manager, rather than loaded once from a saved session.
markdown: ## Workflows *** ### Overview A Workflow is a [Python](/docs/reference/python-scripting) script written to be run repeatedly through the Workflow Manager, rather than loaded once from a saved session. Workflows can automate tasks such as ranking wells, building a set of plots, or exporting a report, and can be shared between users. #### Accessing the Workflow Manager Workflows are managed and run from the Workflow Manager, opened from the Workflows group of the[Home Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/home-tab). ### Types of Workflow There are two kinds of workflow script, distinguished only by their file extension: #### Simple Workflows (.s3py) A .s3py workflow takes no arguments. Clicking Run executes the script directly. #### Parameterised Workflows (.py) A .py workflow declares arguments using Python's argparse, so a single script can be re-run against different data. When such a workflow is selected, S3analyse reads its arguments and shows them as Required and Optional fields above the list (see Arguments below). ### Workflow Manager The Workflow Manager lists every available workflow, grouped under category headings, sorted alphabetically within each category. The list details the filename of the workflow and a description of its operation, lifted from the workflow file. A user can select a workflow from the list be clicking on the appropriate row of the list. Selecting a workflow shows its details in the panel below the list: ![Workflow manager dialog](/img/help/workflowmanagerdialog.png) The workflow panel details the: - Name and description of the selected workflow. - ![Text editor](/img/help/texteditor-16.png) View Script opens the underlying script file in the preferred available editor. - Any Arguments or Options are listed for the user to fill out. Appropriate options may be types in or selected from a dialog opened via the corresponding ![Search](/img/help/search-16-n-p.png) Set Arguments button. - Run will runs the workflow. For a Parameterised Workflow this stays disabled until every Required argument has a value (see [Arguments](/docs/reference/workflows#Arguments) below). While a workflow is running, a progress bar and Cancel button are shown in place of the list. Close dismisses the Workflow Manager. ### Adding and Organising Workflows Workflows do not need to be individually registered or imported. Any .py or .s3py script placed in a Workflows folder is picked up automatically, and the Workflow Manager updates immediately as scripts are added, edited or removed. Workflow scripts are read from a Workflows folder in either of these locations: - Workflows to be shared by every user of the machine: - %ProgramData%\Sciencesoft Ltd\S3analyse\Workflows * Workflows available only to the current (roaming) user. - %AppData%\Sciencesoft Ltd\S3analyse\Workflows The folder a script is placed in becomes its category in the Workflow Manager list. Scripts placed directly in the Workflows folder (not in a subfolder) are grouped under General. A subfolder name can be prefixed with a number and a space (e.g. 02 Well Surveillance) to control the order categories are listed in; the number itself is not shown. A "Modules" subfolder is not scanned for workflows, use it to hold shared code that your scripts import. ### Arguments For a Parameterised Workflow, each argument the script declares is shown as a text field, split into Required and Optional sections. Optional fields can be left blank to use the script's own default value. If an argument's name refers to a Case, Well, Grid Property or Summary Vector, S3analyse recognises it and adds a ![Search](/img/help/search-16-n-p.png) Set Arguments button next to the field to pick values from the current project instead of typing them. If a project has only one Case loaded, its Case field is filled in automatically. Entering more than one comma-separated value into an argument runs the workflow once for every combination of the values entered across all such arguments, e.g. two Cases and three Wells run the workflow six times. ### Running a Workflow and Viewing Output Click Run to execute the selected workflow (or once per combination of argument values, see above). A busy cursor is shown while it runs; Cancel stops it early. Anything the script prints is written to the S3analyse log file only. A workflow can instead show results directly to the user in a dedicated Output window, intended for output that should actually be read or copied. If the script itself fails, a Python Script Error message is shown with the details.

title: Workflows
summary: Package a script as a reusable workflow with its own parameters.
markdown:
A workflow wraps a Python script so it can be run repeatedly with different inputs, without
anyone needing to edit the script itself.

The Workflow Manager lists available workflows and prompts for their arguments — a well
selection, a case, a threshold value — then runs the script against the current session.

## Why workflows rather than bare scripts

- The person running the analysis does not have to read or edit Python
- Inputs are validated and presented as a form rather than typed into source
- The same workflow applies consistently across studies

## Example workflows

S3analyse ships with worked examples covering common tasks:

| Workflow | What it does |
|---|---|
| Active case well production | Plots production for wells in the active case |
| All cases well production | The same plot across every loaded case |
| Multi-case well vector | Compares one well vector across cases |
| Plot region volumetrics | Volumetrics summarised by region |
| Top N field vector | Ranks and plots the highest-performing runs |
| Top X% well oil producers | Filters to the best-producing wells by percentile |

## Eclipse Settings

***

![Main settings eclipse](/img/help/mainsettings-eclipse.png)

### Overview

The Eclipse Settings provide options for loading Eclipse data sets.

#### Accessing the Eclipse Settings

The General Settings dialog can be accesses in two ways; either click the Settings cog ![Options icon](/img/help/options-icon.png) icon in the Quick Access Toolbar or selecting Settings in the File menu. From this select Eclipse in the treeview.

### Eclipse Settings

#### Use Load Dialog

Selecting Use Load Dialog will add a step to the load process for Eclipse data sets to allow the user to configure the load of each data set. The Eclipse [Load Dialog](/docs/reference/loading-data/supported-data-types/eclipse/load-dialog) will be presented when selecting a Eclipse model for loading allowing the selection of data types to load. The load dialog will be initialised with the setting defined in Eclipse settings.

If unselected the load operation will use the settings as defined in Eclipse Settings.

#### Data Types to Load

Select the relevant checkboxes for each data type to be included when loading the model:

- Grid: Loads structured grid data for the model.
- Init: Loads the initialised map data.
- Tables: Loads tabular data such as PVT, Saturation Tables, etc.

* - Load VFP Table Data: Load Vertical Flow Performance (VFP) lift curve table data.

+ Summary: Loads the summary data

- - Prefer H5 File: Select to prioritize .H5 formats (default: unchecked).

* Solution: Loads the dynamic map data.
* RFT: Includes Repeat Formation Test (RFT) data.

+ - Create RFT: Select to extract the grid property values from the well completion locations to create RFT data.

- Group Hierarchy: Loads the well-group tree structure defined in the model.

####

#### Summary Data

Select the relevant checkboxes for each Summary data class to be included when loading the model summary data:

- AQUIFERS: Aquifer performance and influence.
- BLOCKS: Fundamental grid blocks used in simulation.
- COMPLETIONS: Completion-level breakdown per well.
- EDGES: Structural connections or grid boundaries.
- FIELD: Field-wide aggregate results.
- GROUPS: Grouped performance across wells or fields.
- NODES: Key control points or reference markers.
- PIPES: Pipe flow and network structures.
- REGIONS: Spatial region data for segmented analysis.
- SEGMENTS: Pipeline or flow segments within the simulation.
- WELLS: Individual well production/injection data.

### Dialog Controls

#### ![New item11](/img/help/newitem11.png) Reset Current to Default

Resets the current page of settings to the system default.

#### ![New item10](/img/help/newitem10.png) Reset All to Default

Resets all the settings to the system default.

#### OK

Applies any changes to the load selections without applying the settings as a new default.

#### Cancel

Exits the settings and cancel any changes.

#### ![New item9](/img/help/newitem9.png) Help

Open the Help at the relevant section.

## Text File Examples

***

The following examples illustrate common Text File layouts supported by S3analyse.

### Example 1

This simple example contains a full Header and lists a time property and three data properties. It uses comma delimiters to separate the values. Well names have been specified for each data column, with the exception of the DATE column which is left blank.

-- Observed data for run MYMODEL1

ORIGIN MYMODEL1

DATEFORMAT DD/MM/YY

DATE,FOPTH,FOPRH,FGPRH

,SM3,SM3/DAY,SM3/DAY

,G5P,G5P,G5P

31/03/06,0,0,0

01/04/06,3360000,3360000,0

### Example 2

This example uses the PAGE keyword to store two unrelated tables in the same file. PAGE 1 defines a WBHP table for wells N1 and N2. PAGE 2 then starts a completely independent table — here a WTEST vector for the same wells — with its own Property Names, Units and Member Names rows. Each PAGE keyword resets the column headers, so the tables either side of it do not need to share the same columns.

PAGE 1

, N1, N2

PAGE 2

DAYS, PSIA, PSIA

, N1, N2

0, 4140.738, 3679.575

1, 4000, 3157.185

2.9695, 4000, 3071.517

### Example 3

This example uses spaces rather than commas to delimit columns, and records TIME as an elapsed day count instead of a date, so a STARTDATE is set in the header to give the count a reference date.

Because runs of spaces collapse into a single delimiter, a blank cell cannot be left in place the way a leading comma can. Instead the Member Names row supplies only one value, "N1", which the reader aligns to the last column (WBHP), leaving TIME without a member. This is the same result as the blank cell in Example 1 and 2, achieved differently because of the delimiter in use.

-- Single well test, elapsed time in days

ORIGIN N1\_Well\_Test

STARTDATE 01/01/2000

TIME WBHP

DAYS PSIA

N1

0 4140.738

1 4000

2.9695 4000

## Input Parameter Files

***

When S3control creates a Sensitivity Analysis or History Match the input parameter values for each case are written to a parameters file next to the model. These files have the extension .params and list each parameter's name and value, for example:

PoroM;0.713426853707415

PermM;0.911823647294589

PermZM;0.29809619238477

AQPV;475150300.601202

AQJ;74.749498997996

OWCD;3578.95791583166

GOCD;2597.09418837675

These files will be loaded automatically when data is loaded into S3analyse. When this data is present, additional features will be available in the [Dashboards](/docs/reference/dashboards):

- [Radar Plots](/docs/reference/dashboards/widgets/radar-plot) are available.
- [Pearson Coefficient Plots](/docs/reference/dashboards/widgets/pearson-coefficient-plot) are available.
- [Cross Plots](/docs/reference/dashboards/widgets/cross-plot) can use these values for the x and y axes.
- [Filters](/docs/reference/dashboards/filtering) can be created based on these values file.

## Cumulative Distribution Plot

***

### Overview

The Cumulative Distribution Plot widget in S3analyse dashboards visualizes Cumulative Distribution Function for a chosen property. It supports both simulation outputs and parameter-based axes (e.g., from [.params files](/docs/reference/loading-data/supported-data-types/input-parameter-files)).

### Creating a Cumulative Distribution Plot

To create a Cumulative Distribution Plot:

1. Select an active [Dashboard](/docs/reference/dashboards)
2. In the [Dashboard Design Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs/dashboard-tools/design-tab) select Cumulative Distribution Plot from the Panels group.

This will add a widget Tile to the end of the Dashboard sequence containing the default Cumulative Distribution Plot of the Percentage against Final Field Oil Production Total.

### Modifying a Cumulative Distribution Plot

The data used to define the plot and its appearance can be modified.

The settings are described in [Cumulative Distribution Plot Settings](/docs/reference/dashboards/widgets/cumulative-distribution-plot/cumulative-distribution-plot-settings).

title: Calculations
summary: The Calculations functionality allows new vector properties to be generated from existing (loaded or previously calculated) data via a formula.
markdown:
## Calculations

***

### Overview

The Calculations functionality allows new vector properties to be generated from existing (loaded or previously calculated) data via a formula.

New vector properties are created by defining a formula containing variables, associating the variables with existing vectors, setting the name and location in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements#CalculatedData) node for the created property, and specifying whether to apply the calculation to all cases in an ensemble, or to all items (Wells or Solution timesteps, for example, depending on the type of data) in the data set.

Note that, although the vector properties are generated when the calculation is initially carried out, they are only evaluated when the vector is used (on a [Line Plot](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots) or [Grid Display](/docs/reference/grid-displays), for example).

#### Accessing the Calculations

The Calculations dialog can be accessed in two ways:

1. Clicking on Calculations in the View Actions group of the [Home Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/home-tab).
2. Double-clicking on the Designs node under the Calculations node within the [Calculated Data](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements#CalculatedData) node in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view).

### Calculations Dialog

The Calculations dialog has two areas: the left panel displays and manages the collection of calculations created during the current session; the right panel is the editor and is populated with the currently selected calculation.

![User function example](/img/help/userfunctionexample.png)

### List of Calculations

The left panel shows all calculations that have been created in the current session. Each item has three elements:

1. An icon: The icon can be one of:
   1. ![Show graph](/img/help/show-graph-16-n-p.png) Line Plot: Indicating that the calculation creates a new summary data vector from existing summary vectors.
   2. ![All layers3](/img/help/alllayers3d-16-n-p.png) Grid Display: Indicating that the calculation creates a new grid property vector (INIT or solution data) from existing grid property vectors.
   3. ![Calculator](/img/help/calculator-16.png) Calculator: Indicating that the type of vector to be created by the calculation has not yet been specified.

1) An identifying name for the calculation that includes the name of the resulting calculated vector and the formula used to create it. (Note that it is possible for two different calculations to have the same result vector name and calculation formula and therefore the same identifier.)

1. The ![Red cross](/img/help/red-cross-16-n-p.png) Delete, which allows any of the calculations to be removed from the list.

New calculations can be added by clicking Add New which creates a new, blank calculation item with the default name NEW.

When the Calculations dialog is first displayed it contains no calculations, so the Add New button must be clicked to add one.

### Calculation Editor

The right panel on the Calculations dialog comprises the controls for designing and executing new calculations.

#### Result Vector Properties and Formula

The properties of the created vector and the formula to be used to calculate it are set in the top panel:

1. Result Name: The short name of the vector property to be created (this is what will appear in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view)).

1) Formula: This is the expression that will be used to define the calculation to be performed. The formula will generally contain variables that can be associated with existing data values. Many functions can be used in the formula, including all the usual analytic functions (SIN, COS, EXP, LOG, etc.), and several other useful function (such as a lookup function, a random number generator, and special CUMMIN and CUMMAX functions for solution data. In addition, there are sum and average functions, which can be used to sum values over multiple items (over wells, for example). The complete set of supported functions is set out below.

1. Units: The units of the created vector can be selected from the dropdown, which contains all supported units. These units will be shown in the axis titles when the created vector is displayed on a line plot.

1) Description: The longer description of the created vector can be set. This will be shown in the axis titles when the created vector is displayed on a line plot.

#### Variables

When the formula is set, the formula expression is parsed and free of errors any variables it contains are identified (variables can be any sequence of alphabetic characters or digits, or underscores; the variable cannot begin with a digit). The list of variables is then displayed in the yellow Variables table section of the Calculations dialog. The yellow colour indicates that the rows of the table are drag and drop targets (that is, the properties to be associated with the variable must be dragged from the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) and dropped onto the corresponding variable row of the table).

In the example below there are two free variables, a and b, in the formula y = a + b. These have been associated with the vectors WOPR and WWPR from well B1.

![User function variables example](/img/help/userfunctionvariablesexample.png)

##### The Variables Table

The variables table has several columns containing information about the associated vector and ![Lock brass open](/img/help/lock-brass-open-16.png)/![Lock brass closed](/img/help/lock-brass-closed-16.png) Padlock buttons that can be used to specify whether the vector or its properties are fixed when applying the calculation to multiple cases or items (see below). The number of columns that appear depends on the associated vectors. The full list of possible columns is:

1. ![Lock brass open](/img/help/lock-brass-open-16.png)/![Lock brass closed](/img/help/lock-brass-closed-16.png) Fix lock button [always present]: If this is locked, the associated vector’s case or item, etc., will not change when the calculation is applied to different cases or items. The exact vector that is associated with the variable will always be used in every evaluation of the calculation.

1) Variable [always present]: the name of the variable in the formula.

1. Associated Vector [always present]: The path in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) to the vector that is associated with the variable. (This is blank if no vector has been associated with the variable.)

1) Case [always present]: The name of the case from which the associated vector comes. When the current project contains multiple cases, this is a dropdown that displays all the available cases and allows the case of the associated vector to be changed from the case of the vector that was dropped. Usually, this will not be necessary, but it can be used to set up a calculation that involves the difference of a vector between two different cases. Note, though, that care must be taken to ensure that the two cases have the same number of timesteps (for summary data) or grid cells (for solution data), otherwise the calculation cannot be performed.

1. ![Lock brass open](/img/help/lock-brass-open-16.png)/![Lock brass closed](/img/help/lock-brass-closed-16.png) Fix Case Lock button [present only if the current project contains multiple cases]: If this is locked, the associated vector’s case will not change when the calculation is applied to different cases. Other properties (item names, etc.) will change when the calculation is applied to different items (if they are not also fixed).

1) Item (Well, Timestep, etc.) [present only if the associated vector has a property that can be ‘looped over’]: The column displays the item name of the associated vector (well name, timestep, etc.). This is a property of the associated vector that can be changed in each evaluation of the calculation to apply the calculation to all of the corresponding items (wells, timesteps, etc.) in the case.

1. ![Lock brass open](/img/help/lock-brass-open-16.png)/![Lock brass closed](/img/help/lock-brass-closed-16.png) Fix Item Lock button [present only if the associated vector has a property that can be ‘looped over’]: If this is locked, the associated vector’s item will not change when the calculation is applied to other items.

1) Item2 (possibly completion index, for example) [present only if the associated vector has a second property that can be ‘looped over’]: The column displays the name of the second property of the associated vector. This is a property of the associated vector that can be changed in each evaluation of the calculation to apply the calculation to all of the corresponding secondary items (completions, for example) in the case.

1. ![Lock brass open](/img/help/lock-brass-open-16.png)/![Lock brass closed](/img/help/lock-brass-closed-16.png) Fix Item2 Lock button [present only if the associated vector has a second property that can be ‘looped over’]: If this is locked, the associated vector’s secondary property will not change when the calculation is applied to other items.

Note that the items selected as the things that can be looped over is calculated and updated dynamically as vectors are dropped onto the rows of the variables table. If the associated vectors have several different properties that can be looped over, the properties that occur most often are selected. Most commonly, though, for summary data the items will be well names. For grid data (Init or solution data) the items will be timesteps.

##### Apply to Multiple Cases or Items

When vectors have been associated with the variables, the ‘Apply to all…’ checkboxes above the variables table will be active. There are three ‘Apply to all’ options, but they may not all be visible or enabled. Which options are visible/enabled will depend on the properties of the associated vectors (whether the current project contains multiple cases and whether there are one or two item properties that can be ‘looped over’).

- Apply to all cases [always visible; enabled if the current project contains multiple cases]: If this is checked, the calculation is performed for all cases in the current project. For each case, the associated vectors are replaced with the corresponding vectors from that case (unless they have been set to be fixed, or have fixed case, in the variables table).

* Apply to all Items [only visible if (at least one of) the associated vectors has a variable property (such as wells or timesteps); that is, if the variables table has an ‘Item’ column]: If this is checked, the calculation is performed for all corresponding items (well, timesteps, etc.). For each item, the associated vectors are replaced with the corresponding vectors for that item (unless they have been set to be fixed, or have fixed item, in the variables table).

+ Apply to all Items2 [only visible if (at least one of) the associated vectors has a second variable property (completion index, for example); that is, if the variables table has an ‘Item2’ column]: If this is checked, the calculation is performed for all corresponding secondary item properties. For each secondary item, the associated vectors are replaced with the corresponding vectors for that secondary item (unless they have been set to be fixed, or have fixed secondary item, in the variables table).

##### Result Location

The Result Location box specifies the location in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) where the calculated vector should be placed. This can be set in two ways:

- Automatically: When the associated vectors have been set for one or more of the variables, the properties of those vectors are analysed to determine whether the free vectors (that is, the vectors that have not been set to be fixed or have fixed case or other properties) all belong to a single case and/or item (well or timestep, etc.). If they are consistent, the result location is set to be the corresponding location (with that case and item properties) in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view). When the result location has been set automatically, the text is grey and italic.

* By the user: To set the result location to a specific place in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) drag and drop a vector from the desired branch of the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) onto the yellow Result Location box (the name of the vector dropped will be ignored, only the path will be used). When the result location has been set by the user the text is black.

Once the result location has been set the corresponding case is displayed. If the current project contains multiple cases, this is a dropdown that allows the case of the result vector location to be changed. Usually, this will not be necessary, and note that the result location is included in the analysis of whether the case is a free property that can be looped over, so if the result vector’s case is set to be different from the variable’s associated vector cases it will not be possible to apply the calculation to all cases.

#### Validation Messages and the Calculate Button

The section of the Calculation panel below the Variables section contains the validation message and the Calculate button:

1. If there is any problem with the calculation setup (a syntax error in the formula, not all variables being associated with vectors, etc.) a validation indicator icon and message will be displayed and the Calculate button will be disabled. The validation icon indicates the severity of the error (![White tick on green flat10](/img/help/whitetickongreen-flat10-16.png) No Error, ![Info](/img/help/info-16-n-p.png) Information, ![Problem](/img/help/problem.png) Warning, ![Error](/img/help/error-16-n-p.png) Severe Error). If there are no errors or warnings, ![White tick on green flat10](/img/help/whitetickongreen-flat10-16.png) and ‘No errors’ will be displayed and Calculate will be enabled.

1) Clicking Calculate will perform the requested calculation(s). Note that the new vectors will appear in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view), but the actual evaluation will not be performed until the vector is used on a line plot or grid plot, etc.

### The Sum (SUM) and Average (AVG) Functions

S3analyse can perform calculations involving sums or averages over items such as Wells or timesteps. The list of items over which the sum or average should be performed can be specified by the user.

To set the list of items to sum or average over follow these steps:

1. Enter a formula containing the SUM() or AVG() function, operating on a variable or expression (e.g., SUM(a), or SUM(a+b\*c)).

1) Associate the variables in the SUM or AVG function with vectors. At least one of the associated vectors must have properties that can be summed or averaged over. For example, well vectors or solution vectors can be summed or averaged over, but FIELD vectors or INIT vectors cannot (the expression can include Summary Field or Init vectors, but there must be at least one other vector in the SUM or AVG expression that can be summed or averaged over). The associated vectors are validated, and the validation status of the SUM or AVG function is indicated by the coloured line under the function name. The actual error will be indicated in the error reporting box at the bottom of the calculation panel (unless a different, more severe, error is reported there).

1. When the function has been set up correctly, so that the function’s validation status indicator is green, hovering over the function will show the Select button (this only appears when the cursor is close to the function text). Clicking Select will show the Select Items dialog:

![Calculations sum select](/img/help/calculationssumselect.png)

1. In the Select Items dialog, items may be selected by specifying a pattern with wildcards (P\*, for example), and/or by individually selecting/deselecting the items. Once the desired items have been selected, click Close on the Select Items dialog, and the sum or average function setup is complete.

![Calculations select items dialog](/img/help/calculationsselectitemsdialog.png)

title: Load Dialog
summary: By default when an Meteor file is loaded into S3analyse the data set is loaded and presented in the Project View with the default load options.
markdown:
## Meteor Load Dialog

***

![Load dialog meteor default](/img/help/loaddialog-meteordefault.png)

### Overview

By default when an Meteor file is loaded into S3analyse the data set is loaded and presented in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) with the default load options. These default options can be changed for the system in the [Meteor Load Settings](/docs/reference/general-settings/simulators/meteor).

Additionally, a load dialog can be shown to allow the user to tailor the load options for each Meteor data set. From this the user can select what data types and what summary classes to load and then click OK to complete the load.

#### Accessing the Meteor Load Dialog

The Meteor Load DIalog is presented when attempting to load an Meteor file and Use Load Dialog is checked in the [Meteor Load Settings](/docs/reference/general-settings/simulators/meteor).

### Available Settings Categories

The Meteor Load options are organized into three main sections:

#### Use Load Dialog

Selecting Use Load Dialog will cause this dialog to be presented during the load process for Meteor data sets to allow the user to configure the load of each data set.

Checking/checking this options will only affect future loads and only if Save Settings & Load is also clicked.

#### Data Types To Load

Select which types of simulation data to load:

- Grid: Loads structured grid data for the model.
- Init: Loads the initialised map data.
- Summary: Loads the summary data.
- Solution: Loads the dynamic map data.

Selecting Select All will check all the data types.

#### Summary Data

Use this section to specify which data classes from the summary file should be loaded:

- WELL: Well production/injection data.
- TRACER: Tracer data.
- OVERAL: Field-wide data.

Selecting Select All will check all the Summary data types.

#### Save Settings & Load

Saves current selection as a new default and starts data loading.

#### Load

Loads using current selections without applying the settings as a new default.

#### Cancel

Exits the dialog and cancel the load process.

title: Projects
summary: Projects are used to collect all loaded data into a single collection.
markdown: ## Projects *** ### Overview Projects are used to collect all loaded data into a single collection. ### Projects and Data Loading Projects are used to organise all loaded data into a single working session. This structure allows users to manage multiple simulation runs, sensitivity cases, and history matches within a unified environment. Each project acts as a container for related files, making it easy to navigate between datasets, compare results, and maintain a clear overview of the modelling workflow. When a file is loaded into a project, S3analyse automatically searches for any associated data in the appropriate folder. This includes summary files, restart files, grid definitions, and parameter sets. By detecting and loading these linked files, the system ensures that all relevant information is available for plotting, analysis, and comparison without requiring manual intervention. This streamlined approach helps users focus on interpretation rather than file management. ### Creating a New Project Data can be loaded via [drag and drop](/docs/reference/loading-data/opening-files) onto S3analyse or with [File Open](/docs/reference/loading-data/opening-files). This will create a default project for the session. Alternatively, data can be added by formally creating a new project. This is achieved by clicking on New Project in the [File Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/file-tab) or the [Quick Access Toolbar](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/quick-access-toolbar). This will produce the Create a New Project dialog: ![Create new project dialog](/img/help/createnewprojectdialog.png) The creation process has two steps; select the data set(s) then select the data types to be loaded. The treeview on the left lists the steps to create the project. Both Select Cases and Select Data need to be valid to create the new project. Their status is shown in the left list, defined as follows: - ![Green checkmark](/img/help/green-checkmark-16-n-p.png) indicates a valid selection and the next step is available. - ![Red cross](/img/help/red-cross-16-n-p.png) indicates an issue with the selection. A status message of the creation process is shown in the bottom-left of the dialog to indicate any issues. - ![Smaller bullet point](/img/help/smaller-bullet-point-16-n-p.png) indicates an undefined status. An invalid step leads to later steps as undefined. #### Select Cases The location of the data is set with Base Folder. A path can be typed into the textbox or browsed for by clicking ![Folder](/img/help/folder-16-n-p.png). Clicking the ![Close all](/img/help/close-all-16-n-p.png) will clear the entry for the Base Folder. The Simulator can be selected to find data sets only from the chosen simulator. The Project Name is inferred from the chosen folder, otherwise the user can set the name from the textbox. When a valid path has been entered the Case list will be populated with any data sets found in the chosen Base Folder. The list can include subfolders of the Base Folder if Search Subfolders For Case Files is checked. Any case can be selected/deselected from the load by checking the corresponding checkbox for that case. The Case Filter offers the ability to filter cases based on their name to aid finding the cases of interest. Once the required case or cases have been selected clicking Next will move to the second step of Selecting Data. Alternatively, the default data selection can be used and Create Project can be clicked to create the new project and skip the Select Data step. #### Select Data Once a valid case or cases have been selected the next step is to select what data types to load for the cases. ![Create new project dialog data select](/img/help/createnewprojectdialogdataselect.png) #### The available data for the case or cases is shown in the left-hand treeview. Individual types can be included/excluded from the new project by checking/unchecking their corresponding checkboxes in the list. Clicking on a data type, such as Init or Summary, will list a breakdown of available sub-components, such as properties or wells, for that data type in the right-hand list. These can be individually included/excluded for finer granularity in the load. With a valid data selection the New Project can be created by clicking on Create Project.

title: Centre Of Rotation
summary: The Centre of Rotation Settings provide options to customize the centre point about which the grid rotated when being manipulated by the user.
markdown:
## Centre of Rotation Settings

***

###

### ![Grid settings centre of rotation](/img/help/gridsettings-centreofrotation.png)

###

### Overview

The Centre of Rotation Settings provide options to customize the centre point about which the grid rotated when being manipulated by the user. These settings allow you to set and reset the cell about which the grid is centred.

Any changes are applied directly to the Grid as they are made.

#### Accessing the Grid Settings

You can access the Centre of Rotation Settings through the grid interface:

1. Open the Grid you wish to customize
2. Double left-click on the Grid
3. Select Centre of Rotation from the treeview in the Grid Editors dialog

### Available Settings Categories

The Centre of Rotation Settings are organized into three sections:

#### Use Centre of Rotation

Enables/disables a user set centre of rotation. If unchecked, the default rotation centre is used.

####

#### Get from Last Selected Cell

Clicking this populates the X, Y, and Z coordinates with the position of the currently selected cell or element in the grid. This defines the user set centre of rotation.

#### Coordinates

These text boxes show the current defined user set centre of rotation for the grid as a set of X, Y and Z coordinates. The coordinates can be entered directly into the text box fields to set the centre of rotation.

#### Reset Centre

This button resets the centre of rotation to the default location. This will be the centre point of the grid.

title: Y-Axis Settings
summary: The Cumulative Distribution Y-Axis Settings provides options to customize the appearance and presentation of a Cumulative Distribution Dashboard widget.
markdown:
## Y-Axis Settings

***

###

### ![Cumulative distribution settings y axis](/img/help/cumulativedistributionsettings-yaxis.png)

###

### Overview

The Cumulative Distribution Y-Axis Settings provides options to customize the appearance and presentation of a Cumulative Distribution Dashboard widget. These settings allow you to control the title and axes elements.

Any changes are applied directly to the Cumulative Distribution widget as they are made.

#### Accessing the Cumulative Distribution Widget Settings

You can access the Cumulative Distribution Settings through the widget interface:

1. Open the Dashboard you wish to customize
2. Double left-click on the Cumulative Distribution widget within the Dashboard
3. Expand the Axes treeview node from the Cumulative Distribution node
4. Select Y-Axis from the parent Axes node of the treeview in the Dashboard Settings dialog

### Available Settings Categories

The Y-Axis Settings are organized into four main sections:

#### Axis Title

Control how the axis title appears on your graph:

- Title: Add or modify the text of the main title of your Axis

* Font: Customize font (size, style, colour) with the options available by clicking Select. A preview of the current font is shown with the "Preview" label.

#### Axis Line

Configure the appearance of the axis:

- Thickness: Set the thickness of the axes lines.

* Colour: Set the colour of the axes lines.

+ Location: Toggle the top/bottom or left/right location of the axis.

#### Axis Labels

Customize how value labels appear along the axis:

- Visible: Toggle the visibility of the axis labels.

* Angle: Set the angle of the axis labels either with the slider or by typing into or stepping through the text box.

+ Format: Set the format for the axis labels:
  - Normal: Decimal representation of the label values, e.g. 2,000 or 3,000,000
  - Abbreviate: Engineering notation representation of the label values, e.g. 2K or 3M
  - Scientific Notation: Scientific notation representation of the label values, e.g. 2x103 or 3x106
  - Date: Represent the axis values as dates (when applicable)

- Font: Customize font (size, style, colour) with the options available by clicking Select. A preview of the current font is shown with the "Preview" label.

* Location: Toggle between presenting the labels Inside or Outside of the Chart.

#### Range Values

This section provides options for the user to set the limits and the interval steps of the axis:

- Minimum: Sets the maximum value for the axis limit
- Maximum: Sets the minimum value for the axis limit
- Interval: Sets the major interval value between labels for the axis
- Minor Interval: Sets the minor interval value between labels for the axis
- Invert: Toggles the inversion of the axis limits
- Log: Toggles a log scale for the axis

Any changes to the Range Values can be reset by clicking ![Undo icon](/img/help/undo-icon.png)

title: Histogram Settings
summary: The Histogram Settings provides options to customize the appearance and presentation of your histograms.
markdown:
## Histogram Settings

***

###

### ![Histogram settings histogram](/img/help/histogramsettings-histogram.png)

###

### Overview

The Histogram Settings provides options to customize the appearance and presentation of your histograms. These settings allow you to control the title and background elements.

Any changes are applied directly to the Histogram as they are made.

title: Plotting and dashboards
summary: Line plots, histograms, scatter plots, multi-plot layouts and analysis dashboards.
markdown: S3analyse plots production history, grid properties and ensemble uncertainty analysis. S3analyse will load and plot data from ensembles with 100s of simulation runs in seconds. Multiple standard dashboards include single run and ensemble NPV, with the ability for the user to create their own dashboards. ## Line plots Plot summary and observed vectors over time, with multiple axes, logarithmic scales, configurable legends, series styling, markers and value overlays. Observed data can be shown alongside simulated results for direct comparison. Search and broadcast controls step a plot through wells or vectors without rebuilding it — move every line to the next item, append the next item to the same plot, or open it in a new window. The demo above shows part of the Chart View tab: series styling, the logarithmic and inverted axis options, grid lines and legend placement. The product additionally offers font control, multiple Y axes, zoom history, legend limits and per-axis ranges — see [line plots](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots) for the full set. ## Histograms Distribution histograms of any grid property, with control over bin count and range, and per-region colouring. ## Scatter plots High-density cross plots of one grid property against another, with region filtering, point size control, axis swapping and trend lines. ## Line analysis Property profiles along an I, J or K traverse through the grid, with optional interpolation across inactive cells. ## Multi-plot layouts Compose grid views, line plots, histograms, line analysis and scatter plots into a tiled layout — 1×2, 2×2, 3×3 and others — with individual cells able to span rows and columns. ## Dashboards Purpose-built analysis panels that can be combined and filtered together: - Cross plot - Cumulative distribution plot - Ensemble plot - Grid property plot - Pearson correlation plot - Radar plot - Well statistics plot

title: Project View
summary: One of the main features of S3analyse is the accessible way in which the user's data is presented.
markdown:
## Project View

***

### Overview

One of the main features of S3analyse is the accessible way in which the user's data is presented. The Project View gives a easily navigable summary of the loaded data. Further data can be derived and extracted from the loaded data set and is also presented for easy access.

The main function of the Treeview is to offer the selection of data properties to create and update charts or grids. Items can be drag and dropped to the [Display Area](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/display-area) as a new chart/grid or to update an existing chart/grid. Alternatively, properties have a [context-specific right-click menu](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements) that lists the available options.

![Project view panel](/img/help/projectviewpanel.png)

Example with a single data set loaded into S3analyse.

#### Treeview Structure

The data is structured as a treeview in the Project View.

The Project Name is listed at the top and all data items are contained within this folder. If the project comprises multiple runs, these are shown in a separate Cases node of the treeview.

Within the project there are branches for all the different data files loaded for the project, e.g. Grid, Init, Table, Summary, Solution, etc. Sub-branches show breakdowns for each data type, e.g. FIELD, WELLS, etc. for Summary data.

Multiple projects can be loaded simultaneously, with each separate project shown on the treeview as a separate project folder.

### Project View Controls

The view offers controls to aid navigating the loaded data.

#### Sorting

The treeview is presented in the order that the data files are loaded and the order it appears within the files. The treeview can alternatively be sorted alphabetically in an ascending or descending order. This sort occurs at every level of the treeview.

- ![Sort](/img/help/sort-16-n-p.png) Sort in ascending order
- ![Reverse sort](/img/help/reverse-sort-16-n-p.png) Sort in descending order

The sort can be toggled between these orders or the original load order.

#### Search and Filter

Text can be entered into the treeview Search textbox to perform searches and filters.

Clicking on the ![Search](/img/help/search-16-n-p.png) will match on any the next property that contains the search text specified in the textbox. The Treeview will be expanded to show the next match.

Clicking on the ![Filter](/img/help/filter-16-n-p.png) will filter the treeview to only present the properties that match the search text in the textbox. The treeview will be expanded to show all the matches.

### Interacting with the Project View

Each element in the Project View can be interacted with. A list of the elements and how the can be used is presented in [Treeview Elements](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements).

title: Shared Axis
summary: The Shared Axis feature in S3analyse allows users to plot multiple data series on a single line plot and easily manage how each series is represented on the chart's axes.
markdown:
## Shared Axis

***

### Overview

The Shared Axis feature in S3analyse allows users to plot multiple data series on a single line plot and easily manage how each series is represented on the chart's axes. This is particularly useful when comparing properties with similar or compatible units, such as production rates across wells or cases.

### How to Use Shared Axis

When a new property is added to a [Line Plot](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots) via Drag and Drop S3analyse provides options on the chart to:

- Reuse an existing Y-axis
- Create a new Y-axis on left
- Create a new Y-axis on right

This is presented in the form of an overlay to the existing Line Plot. The different zones of the overlay define different actions. The action can be chosen by releasing the mouse drag on the specified zone.

### Sharing Axis Overlay

When dragging a property over to an existing Line Plot the chart shows an overlay describing what actions can be taken with regard to providing an axis for the new data, as seen below:

![Shared axes overlay](/img/help/sharedaxesoverlay.png)

Dropping the new data property on:

- New Axis On Left:

Results in a new Y-axis being produced on the left of the chart.

- Reuse Axis <Axis Title>:

Will use the existing Y-axis with the title Axis Title.

This may result in the range of the Y-axis being changed to accommodate the new range of values introduced by the new property and result in a rescaling of the exiting property line or lines on the chart.

- New Axis on Right:

Results in a new Y-axis being produced on the right of the chart.

For the case when the existing chart contains multiple axes additional zones will be added to the overlay to allow any of the Y-axes to be selected to represent the new property. Each is identified with its title.

title: Line Plots
summary: A Line Plot is a chart type that connects individual data points with straight lines to reveal trends and patterns over a continuous interval.
markdown:
## Line Plots

***

### Overview

A Line Plot is a chart type that connects individual data points with straight lines to reveal trends and patterns over a continuous interval. By mapping one variable along the horizontal axis and another along the vertical axis, it makes it easy to trace how values rise or fall in relation to each other. Commonly used for time-series data, Line Plots highlight rates of change and overall trajectories.

### Creating a Line Plot

Line Plot charts can be created in a number of ways:

- Double-click an appropriate time series property in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) will create a new Line Plot.
- Drag and drop a time series property from the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) to an empty [Display Area](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/display-area).
- Drag and drop a time series property from the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) to the Tab region of the filled [Display Area](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/display-area).
- Right-click an appropriate time series property in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) will offer options to create more specific Line Plots.

The Line Plot appearance can then be customised, such as titles, axes and colours.

### Example

![Line plot example](/img/help/lineplotexample.png)

This example of a Line Plot shows Well Oil Production Rate (WOPR) for well B1 against Time.

### Modifying Line Plots

The appearance of a Line Plot can be changed as desired and the data used in the chart can also be changed, added to or removed.

#### Modifying the Line Plots

Line Plots have an extensive list of settings to customise the appearance. These are outlined in [Line Plot Settings](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots/line-plot-settings) and can be accessed by double left-clicking on the any part of the Line Plot chart.

These are in complement to the Line Plot [Chart View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs/grid-tools/grid-view-tab) and [Chart Data](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs/chart-tools/chart-data-tab) Ribbon Tabs that offer a selection of settings controlling the appearance and the data used in the chart.

#### Modifying the Data in the Line Plots

Line Plots are often created from one property. Additional properties can be [added to the Line Plot](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots/adding-and-removing-lines) with a left-click drag and drop of a new property from the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) onto the chart.

Changing the data used to generate a chart is achieved with the Search Group in the [Chart Data Ribbon Tab](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/ribbon-menu/contextual-tabs/chart-tools/chart-data-tab). This allows [Indexing](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots/indexing) of the chart data that can used to replace data, add to a chart or used to create a new chart.

Data can be removed from the plot via the [Data Series](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots/line-plot-settings/data-series) settings in [Line Plot Settings](/docs/reference/chart-displays/line-plots/line-plot-settings).

### Exporting Line Plots

Line Plots can be exported with the [Report](/docs/reference/exporting-reports) Feature.

### Scripts and Line Plots

Line Plots are supported by [Python Scripting](/docs/reference/python-scripting).

## Legend - Settings

### Overview

Any changes are applied directly to the Grid as they are made.

#### Accessing the Grid Settings

You can access the Legend Settings through the grid interface:

1. Open the Grid you wish to customize
2. Double left-click on the Grid
3. Select Settings from the parent Legend Settings node of treeview in the Grid Editors dialog

### Available Settings Categories

The Legend Settings are organized into three sections:

#### Legend Settings

Toggle the visibility of various components of the legend:

- Display Legend: Show/Hide the legend.

* Display Vertically: Toggle between vertical and horizontal legend orientation.

![Grid settings horizontal legend](/img/help/grid-settings-horizontallegend.png)

- Display Caption: Show/Hide the legend caption showing the displayed grid property.

![Grid settings legend no caption](/img/help/grid-settings-legendnocaption.png)

Set the legend limits:

- Apply Rounding: Enable/Disable rounding of the legend limits.

![Grid settings rounded legend](/img/help/grid-settings-roundedlegend.png) ![Grid settings legend values normal decimal](/img/help/grid-settings-legendvaluesnormaldecimal.png)

- Min / Max: The legend range, and so the cell colouring, can be set with the Min and Max text boxes.

* Tick Count: Define the number of ticks displayed in the legend.

#### Label Format

Set the format of the legend labels:

- Mixed Scientific: Values between 0.001 and 1000 displayed normally; those outside this range appear in scientific notation.
- Scientific: Values less than 1 or greater than 10 use scientific notation, e.g. 1x10-4 or 1x101.
- Decimal: Full decimal notation regardless of range.
  - Precision: Adjust the number of decimal points displayed for the Decimal format.

#### Colour Scheme

Configure gradient colours used for data visualisation:

The colour scheme can be chosen from the drop-down menu:

- - Black & White: Monochromatic, black and white option.
  - Default: Default scheme of a spectrum of pink through to blue
  - Rainbow: Red to violet scheme in a standard rainbow spectrum
  - Water Saturation: Light blue, for low values, to dark blue for high, designed for displaying water saturation
  - Gas Saturation: Light red, for low values, to dark red for high, designed for displaying oil saturation
  - Oil Saturation: Light green, for low values, to dark green for high, designed for displaying gas saturation
  - Brown: Dark brown, for low values, to light brown for high
  - White/Blue: White, for low values, to dark blue for high
  - White/Red: White, for low values, to dark red for high
  - White/Green: White, for low values, to dark green for high
  - Gas/Water: Red, for low values, to blue for high
  - Water/Gas: Blue, for low values, to red for high
  - Oil/Water: Green, for low values, to blue for high
  - Water/Oil: Blue, for low values, to green for high
  - Gas/Oil: Red, for low values, to green for high
  - Oil/Gas: Green, for low values, to red for high

* Logarithmic Mode: Toggle the logarithmic scaling of the steps between colour changes.
* Reverse: Toggle the reversal of the colour scheme order.

## Threshold Settings

1. Open the Grid you wish to customize

### Available Settings Categories

The Threshold Settings are presented as a system to define and set thresholds.

#### Threshold Settings

The general threshold settings are:

- On: Toggle thresholds on/off. If unchecked, thresholds will not appear in the grid.

* Region: Choose a saved region from the drop-down list of presets, if available.

+ ![Save icon](/img/help/save-icon.png) Save: Save the current threshold settings as a [new region](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-settings/threshold-regions). Enter a region name via the text box and click ![Save icon](/img/help/save-icon.png). The new region will be available in the Region drop-down for use elsewhere. This name will also appear in the Thresholds section in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view).

#### Threshold Items List

Any existing Thresholds (or the default initial, empty Threshold) are displayed in a scrollable list. Each Threshold item includes the following controls:

- ![Invert colours](/img/help/invert-colours-16-n-p.png) Invert Item (NOT): Inverts the range values for a single threshold (e.g., flipping a range when the slider’s value is 10–20 sets it to everything outside that range).
- Property Selection: Allows assigning a specific property to the threshold.
- Operator Selection: Assign logical operators (AND, OR, XOR) for combining threshold conditions. This selection is only available when combining more than one Threshold item.
- ![Refresh reload](/img/help/refresh-reload-16-n-p.png) Reset: Reset the threshold limits to the minimum and maximum range of the property.
- ![Red cross](/img/help/red-cross-16-n-p.png) Remove: Remove the selected threshold item from the list.

#### Range Tool Slider:

Configure a Thresholds using a slider that dynamically updates to a property's min/max. The slider will apply to the currently highlighted Threshold in the list.

Adjust values for the Threshold range by typing into numeric fields or directly moving the slider.

#### General Controls

There are a set of controls for creating new thresholds and for editing all existing thresholds. They are found at the bottom of the dialog.

- ![Add item](/img/help/add-item-16-n-p.png) Add New Threshold: Create a new Threshold item. This will be appended to the list as a blank Threshold to the list.

  - ![Invert colours](/img/help/invert-colours-16-n-p.png) Invert All: Reverses the selection state of all Threshold items.

markdown:
## Colour Schemes Settings

***

![Main settings vector colours](/img/help/mainsettings-vectorcolours.png)

### Overview

The Colour Schemes settings let you define a default colour scheme for a specified grid property name, so that any new [Grid Display](/docs/reference/grid-displays) of that vector automatically uses your preferred scheme instead of the system default.

#### Accessing the Colour Schemes Settings

The General Settings dialog can be accesses in two ways; either click the Settings cog ![Options icon](/img/help/options-icon.png) icon in the Quick Access Toolbar or selecting Settings in the File menu. From this select Grid, then Colour Schemes in the treeview.

### Colour Schemes Settings

Any existing rules are listed in this dialog. Adding a new rule produces a blank template to define various settings for the given colour scheme to be applied to a Grid Displays showing the defined property name. These settings correspond to the [Legend Settings](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-settings/legend-settings/settings) for a Grid Display.

Rules only apply to new Grid Displays, grids already on screen keep their existing settings.

The default rule for Any Other Vector is always present. It defines the default case when there is either no other rules or the chosen property displayed on the grid does not match any of the Vector Names. It cannot be deleted and only offers a choice of Colour Scheme and the ability to toggle the Reversed option.

Clicking Add creates a new rule.

![Main settings vector colour scheme](/img/help/mainsettings-vectorcolourscheme.png)

#### Colour Scheme Rules

Each item defines the default display settings for one named map property:

- Vector Name: The property this rule applies to (e.g. PRESSURE). The property name can be typed into this field.
- Colour Scheme: The colour scheme applied by default when this property is displayed.
- Logarithmic: Whether the colour scale uses a logarithmic distribution by default.
- Reversed: Whether the colour scheme's direction is reversed by default.
- Range: The default minimum/maximum range for the colour scale. Values for the minimum and maximum limits can be added to the scheme. An entry of Auto will use the default limits of the data.

Clicking on ![Red cross](/img/help/red-cross-16-n-p.png) will remove that rule.

### Dialog Controls

#### ![New item17](/img/help/newitem17.png) Reset Current to Default

Resets the current page of settings to the system default.

#### ![New item16](/img/help/newitem16.png) Reset All to Default

## Dashboard Filters

***

### Overview

[Dashboards](/docs/reference/dashboards) offer the ability to filter the cases included in the display. Cases can be included/excluded explicitly or based on values of the Summary Field property values. Filtered cases are no longer included in the widget charts. This allows easy exclusion of outlier data sets or poorly performing simulation runs in a sensitivity runs.

#### Accessing the Dashboard Filters

The Dashboard Filters are presented on a pane on the right-hand side of the [Dashboard](/docs/reference/dashboards):

![Dashboard filters pane](/img/help/dashboardfilterspane.png)

### Dashboard Options

There are a number of options to working with the filters.

#### Include Project Filter

Check Include Project Filter to apply the [Project-Wide Filter](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/project-wide-filter) to directly include/exclude cases as defined in the filter.

#### Freeze Plot Axes

This option allows the axis range to be fixed and prevents a new range being applied when updating the chart data based on changes to the filter.

![Add item](/img/help/add-item-16-n-p.png) Add Filter

Click Add Filter to add a Summary Property Filter to the filtering. Multiple filters can be added to further refine the case selection.

### Summary Property Filter

The Summary Property Filter allows cases to be included/excluded based on a the Summary Field data. To define this filter a Field property can be selected and a particular Point of Interest value chosen. A value range for the chosen point can then be set to define the included cases in the filter.

![Dashboard filters pane add](/img/help/dashboardfilterspaneadd.png)

#### Include in Filter

Check the Include in Filter checkbox to apply this filter definition in the case filtering.

#### Property

This drop down list contains all the available properties to define the case filter.

The list of properties contains the Absolute of Field Errors Summed; Summed Absolute Field Errors; and Summary Field vectors.

#### Point of Interest

The Point of Interest is the data point of the chosen property to filter the cases.

#### Value Range

Once a Property and corresponding Point of Interest have been chosen the available range of values across the cases are present. The valid range can be set from the slider or the Minimum and Maximum textboxes.

## Python Scripting

***

### Overview

S3analyse supports the creation and loading of scripts in Python, which has become the industry standard for scripting. At a simple level, S3analyse can save a session by creating a Python script that records the data loaded and the plots created, etc. The resulting script can be reloaded to reproduce the session quickly.

User-created Python scripts can also be loaded to reproduce specific workflows.

Using scripts at a basic level to save and reload sessions in S3analyse does not require any knowledge of Python whatsoever. The scripts can be treated as black boxes. It is easy to edit scripts created by S3analyse to make simple changes (such as changing well names or case names) without knowing any Python. However, a rudimentary knowledge of Python will open up a panoply of possibilities for creating sophisticated workflows via scripting.

title: Opportunity Index
summary: The Opportunity Index combines three normalised grid properties into a single "sweet spot" indicator that highlights zones of remaining reservoir potential — good flow capacity, good remaining move...
markdown:
## Opportunity Index

***

###

### Overview

The Opportunity Index combines three normalised grid properties into a single "sweet spot" indicator that highlights zones of remaining reservoir potential — good flow capacity, good remaining moveable volume, and retained pressure support, all at once. It is calculated separately for oil (OPPO) and gas (OPPG), for [Eclipse](/docs/reference/loading-data/supported-data-types/eclipse)-format grid data.

Use it as a first-pass screening tool during mature-field surveillance, to flag candidate zones for infill drilling, recompletion, or restimulation or to track how a sweet spot shrinks or migrates over time, before moving to detailed, well-specific volumetric or economic evaluation of any individual cell.

#### Accessing the Opportunity Index

The Opportunity Index is calculated automatically on load when the loaded Eclipse case contains the required properties, and appears as an [Opportunity Index](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements#CalculatedData) node in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view), grouped by grid and timestep. Settings are opened from the Show Opportunity Index Settings ![Settings](/img/help/settings-16-n-p.png) button on the [Opportunity Index](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements#CalculatedData) node of the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view).

#### Required Data

If the node does not appear for a case, check the following properties were exported from Eclipse and loaded:

- Static/INIT properties: PERMX, PERMY, PERMH (horizontal permeability), NTG, DZ
- Restart properties, per timestep: SOIL/SGAS, PRESSURE, plus the critical/residual saturations SOWCR (oil) and SGCR (gas)
- Relative permeability curves for OILKR/GASKR

### The Three Components

The Opportunity Index calculation produces three sets of map properties:

- Relative Flow Capacity: Identifies zones with the greatest capacity to flow fluid.

Calculation: Horizontal Permeability × Relative Permeability × Net-to-Gross × Net Thickness,

(PERMH/PERMX/PERMY × OILKR/GASKR × NTG × DZ)

- Mobile Fluid Volume: Identifies zones still holding moveable hydrocarbon.

Calculation: Pore Volume × Mobile Saturation, i.e. saturation above the critical/residual saturation,

(SOIL−SOWCR for oil, SGAS−SOGCR for gas)

- Pressure Support: Identifies zones that have retained reservoir energy rather than depleting.

Calculation: Ratio of Current to Initial Pressure.

#### Combining and Normalising

Each component is normalised to a 0–1 scale before combining, using automatically-calculated lower/upper thresholds (the lower pick sits 75% of the way from the average down to the minimum across all timesteps; the upper pick sits 33% of the way from the average up to the maximum). The three normalised components are then combined via a geometric mean, i.e.:

Opportunity Index = (FlowNormalised x VolumeNormalised x PressureNormalised)1/3

The index is only high where all three factors are favourable; a cell strong in two components but weak in the third will still score low overall. For example, a cell with excellent permeability-thickness but pressure depleted to 20% of its initial value will still pull down to a low combined score, since the weak Pressure Support term drags the geometric mean down regardless of how strong the other two components are.

Note: because the thresholds are calculated once across all timesteps rather than per-timestep, the colour scale stays fixed through time. This is what makes the index useful for surveillance, the same value at two different timesteps means the same thing, so a sweet spot can be watched shrinking, growing or migrating across the field's production history rather than being re-scaled and re-coloured at every step.

The Opportunity Index Settings window lists the lower/upper threshold pair per component, split by phase (Oil/Gas). Values are in the same units as the underlying Eclipse property (e.g. mD·ft-equivalent for Flow Capacity, reservoir volume units for Mobile Volume, psia for Pressure).

![Opportunity index settings](/img/help/opportunityindexsettings.png)

### Settings

The Opportunity Index Settings window lists the lower/upper threshold for each component, separately for Oil and Gas. Each threshold can be typed in directly or reset. The thresholds can be reset to their auto-calculated values with the Reset All button. Adjusting the thresholds changes the contrast of the index. Narrowing them exaggerates differences between cells, widening them smooths the result.

Close will close the window.

### Interpreting the Index

A value near 1 marks a "sweet spot," a strong flow capacity, meaningful remaining volume, and retained pressure. This makes it a useful starting point for identifying bypassed pay, infill drilling targets, or candidates for further stimulation. A value near 0 means at least one of the three components is poor in that cell.

Limitations: The Opportunity Index is a relative screening indicator, not a volumetric or economic ranking. It says nothing about well spacing, drainage from existing wells, completion feasibility, faulting or compartmentalisation, or the economics of accessing a given cell. Treat a high value as a prompt to investigate further with full reservoir engineering analysis, not as a stand-alone recommendation to drill or recomplete.

Like any other grid property, the Opportunity Indices can be displayed in a [Grid Display](/docs/reference/grid-displays) and used for further analysis or [Region](/docs/reference/analysis-tools/regions) definitions.

markdown:
## Layer Analysis

***

###

### Overview

[Layer Analysis](/docs/reference/grid-displays/grid-features/layer-analysis) is a grid feature that creates grid properties where the grid layers have been summed or averaged into a single layer for analysis.

The Layer Analysis functions allow simulation grid map data to be analysed either by summing or averaging data over layers for each column of cells in the Grid. The result is a single sum or average value for each column of cells presented as a single-layer grid geometry, organised with the corresponding Init and Solution properties. The calculation is weighted by Pore Volume by default.

#### Accessing the Layer Analysis

When a project is loaded, and appropriate data is found then the Layer Analysis is prepared and added to the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view) automatically under the [Calculated Data](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements#CalculatedData) node.

### Creating Layer Analyses

A default Layer Analysis, performing a sum of cell values for all layers, is automatically created and added to the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view). This Layer Analysis can be modified as needed.

Additional Layer Analyses can be created from the [Layer Analysis node](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements#CalculatedData) in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view).

![Layer analysis treeview element group](/img/help/layeranalysistreeviewelementgroup.png)

Clicking on ![Add item](/img/help/add-item-16-n-p.png) Add Layer Analysis will create a new Layer Analysis that is added to the bottom of the list.

Analyses can be removed by clicking ![Red cross](/img/help/red-cross-16-n-p.png) Delete Layer Analysis on the corresponding [Layer Analysis node](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements#CalculatedData) in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view).

A Layer Analysis will contain a single-layer grid, extrapolated from the data set, where each cell contains the sum or average of the column of cells for that I, J coordinate for the chosen Z-layers. Value are available for every Init and Solution property in the data set.

### Modifying Layer Analyses

Individual Layer Analyses nodes can be modified by clicking ![Settings](/img/help/settings-16-n-p.png) Show Layer Analysis Settings for the corresponding [Layer Analysis node](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view/treeview-elements#CalculatedData) in the [Project View](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/project-view). This will presents the Layer Analysis dialog, where you can select the required settings:

![Layer analysis settings dialog](/img/help/layeranalysissettingsdialog.png)

#### Analysis Type

The analysis type can either be the sum or average of the column of cells.

##### Layer Sum

The Sum option can be used to sum solution values over selected layers.

##### Layer Average

The Average option is an extension to the Layer Analysis Sum in that it creates an average instead of a summation over the selected layers.

#### Pore Volume Weighting

The calculation can be weighted by the cell Pore Volume by checking Pore Volume Weighting. Other wise the summation is unweighted.

#### Layers

The Layers control allows the selection of the start and end layers to sum each column over.

### Using Layer Analyses

Within the Layer Analyses nodes the Grid, Init and Solution elements are presented. These operate in the same fashion as those in the data set in that they can be dragged and dropped on the [Display Area](/docs/reference/the-user-interface/display-area) to create a [Grid Display](/docs/reference/grid-displays/creating-grids).
